# Store spec v2.175

`store@1` provides typed tables and indexes, cells, logs, transactions and snapshots.
A writer publishes new roots at commit. Its journal acknowledges a durable prefix,
and a checkpoint writes immutable packs and publishes the current roots.

- [API](#1-api) covers transactions, queries and handles.
- [On-disk format](#2-on-disk-format) covers frames and recovery. The current format
  word is defined by AP1 in [§11.1](#111-format-word-kinds-and-limits).
- [Authorities and followers](#12-authorities-the-claim-fence-levels-and-followers)
  covers Directory, Bucket and simulation stores.
- [Tiered collections](#13-tiered-collections) and [Cell and Log collections](#14-cell-and-log-collections)
  describe those collection types.
- [Backup, restore and operator commands](#15-backup-and-restore-store-15-v2106)
  covers inspecting, verifying and copying stores.

See [Store history](STORE-HISTORY.md) for the version entries, CHANGES sections and
review references cited below.

## 1. API

**Conventions.**
- Module `store`, in package `store`.
- **Dictionaries are values.** A table takes `codec.Key[K]` and `codec.Codec[V]` values (S0, §7). It takes no `codec` bound.
  - Use a type annotation to select a derived dictionary, for example `let c: codec.Codec[Account] = codec.of()`.
- **Every handle names its store.** `Table`, `Index`, `Branch`, `Snapshot`, `Ticket` and `CallId` carry the 16-byte `StoreId`. `Snapshot` and `Ticket` also carry the number of the Db's open (§1.12). A handle from another Db is `Foreign`. That is checked before any effect.

### 1.1 Opening and closing

```hirsel
pub type Options {
    create: bool,
    lock_wait_ms: u64,
    group_commits: u32,       // default 64: the most frames one journal write takes; 0 is Missing("group_commits") at open (W1)
    group_bytes: u32,         // default 4 MiB: the most bytes one journal write takes; 0 is Missing("group_bytes") at open (W1)
    checkpoint_bytes: u64,    // default 64 MiB of journal since the last cut starts a checkpoint
    pack_bytes: u64,          // default 64 MiB: a pack closes before a NODE that would take it past this many bytes, unless it holds no NODE yet (H1)
    resident_limit: u64,      // default 1 GiB (GUESS, R8): the accounted resident bytes a Db admits (§1.11)
    checkpoint_task_bytes: u64, // default 262,400,276: the checkpoint task's root limit, max(pack_bytes, 64 MiB + 88) + 2⌈resident_limit / 11⌉ + 64 KiB (Q1a)
    retain: u8,               // v2.47: CHECKPOINT entries in the retained set, 1–255, default 2, 0 is Missing("retain") (§12.6); objects@1 and sim@1 only
    checkpoint_entries: u64,  // v2.46: a cut runs when this many entries follow the latest CHECKPOINT, default 4096, at least 1 (§12.2)
    claim_ms: u64,            // v2.46: how long `open` retries a lost claim, local monotonic clock, default 30,000; 0 = one attempt (§12.3)
    head_poll_ms: u64,        // v2.46: the idle head poll's interval, default 1,000, at least 1 (§12.3)
    expect: Option[StoreId],  // v2.46: open only this store; another is `Foreign` before any write (§12.1)
    activation: Option[u64],  // v2.46: open only at this activation; another is `NotCurrent` before any write (§12.1)
    image: Option[Digest],  // v2.47: open only when the active image is this Describe digest; another is `NotCurrent` before any write (§12.1)
}
pub opaque type Authority   // v2.46 §12.1: the granted keeper of the history; config only, never a credential in program bytes
pub type StoreId { hi: u64, lo: u64 }
pub type Kind = Memory | Directory | Bucket(std.object.LaneConfig)
pub type Overrides { resident_limit: Option[u64], journal_limit: Option[u64], checkpoint_bytes: Option[u64], pack_bytes: Option[u64], group_bytes: Option[u64],
                      group_commits: Option[u32], lock_wait_ms: Option[u64],
                      cache_bytes: Option[u64], writer_pin_bytes: Option[u64], dirty_bytes: Option[u64], pager_task_bytes: Option[u64], readers: Option[u64] }   // v2.60: the Tiered plan (§1.1)
pub type Shortage { need: u64, have: u64, parts: List[(String, u64)] }
pub fn sized(kind: Kind, share: u64) -> Result[Options, Shortage]            // v2.57 DX Q6a: replaces defaults(); every byte figure derived from share
pub fn sized_with(kind: Kind, share: u64, o: Overrides) -> Result[Options, Shortage]   // each Some replaces its derived figure; the sum must still fit share
pub fn directory_writer_need(o: Overrides) -> u64                            // the least share sized_with accepts for Directory, or the largest u64 if none fits
pub opaque type PlacePlan: send                                                // v2.76: sized Options, the writer plan and (Bucket) the capture; holds no heap storage beyond its Options
pub fn planned(kind: Kind, share: u64, o: Overrides) -> Result[PlacePlan, Shortage] // v2.76: replaces sized_reservation; planned_bytes(p) ≤ share
pub fn planned_options(p: PlacePlan) -> Options
pub fn planned_bytes(p: PlacePlan) -> u64                                           // T + X: the caller's whole store term
pub fn planned_capture(p: PlacePlan) -> Option[FollowerPlan]                           // Bucket: the capture's plan, F = T − L; other kinds None
pub opaque type WriterPlan: send                                               // v2.76: T, its lifetime terms and its maximizing phase
pub fn writer_plan(kind: Kind, o: Options) -> Result[WriterPlan, Shortage]    // the same pricing `planned` uses, for a caller that holds Options
pub fn writer_bytes(p: WriterPlan) -> u64                                      // T

pub opaque type Db                         // not send: holds Task handles (CONC-1/2). RUN db_task.
pub type Refusal { error: Error, authority: Authority }   // v2.70 D1: a failed open's error and the Authority it took, handed back whole
pub fn open(tasks: Tasks, take a: Authority, c: Clock, r: Random, o: Options) -> Result[Db, Refusal] waits   // v2.46: opens; a writer open of objects@1 or sim@1 claims (§12.3); v2.70: takes `a`, hands it back with every failure
pub fn close(take db: Db) -> Result[(), Error] waits   // §1.10: always consumes, always releases and joins
pub fn identity(db: Db) -> StoreId
```

**A failed open hands its Authority back (v2.70, D1).** `open` takes `a`. On success the Db owns the transport: on objects@1 the Client's `Workers` stay in the Db and its `Requests` endpoint moves into the journal task. **Every** failure returns `a` in `Refusal.authority`, whatever the `error` and wherever in §3.4 or §12.3 it arose, whether in §12.1's opening checks, recovery and admission, the claim loop, genesis, or after a won replace whose CLAIM advance failed:
- memory@1 hands back the value and log@1 its `Dir`. objects@1 hands back the same `std.object.Client`, never split, its lanes running, with the level and `op_ms` it was granted. sim@1 hands back the same way, with its `SimLevels`, its `LevelSync` and `op_ms` (v2.73).
- Before `open` returns, the attempt's tasks are joined (CONC-6/8), and every reservation it made is refunded (MEM-23): §12.9's fixed buffers, the journal and timer task limits, a claimant's private state. So the caller holds exactly what it held before the call, plus the error's own storage.
- The Authority carries no attempt state. The epoch, holder, position, tag and recovered state belong to the attempt and are dropped with it. Another `open` with the returned Authority claims afresh (§12.3), and a `follower` with it only reads (§12.5).

**Derived sizes (v2.57, DX Q6a).** `share` is the bytes this store may hold: the runner passes the executable's root limit minus `operate_bytes` minus main's 1 MiB keep (RUNNER-SPEC v2.45 §13). `sized` derives, in this order (all GUESS until measured, R8):
- `Memory`: `resident_limit` = share − 1 MiB, and no journal, pack or checkpoint figure is used.
- `Directory` and `Bucket`: `group_bytes` = 4 MiB, `pack_bytes` = min(64 MiB, share / 16), `checkpoint_bytes` = `pack_bytes`, `journal_limit` = `checkpoint_bytes` + `FRAME_LIMIT`, and the cut's working bound = 2⌈r / 11⌉ + 64 KiB (Q1a's term). `journal_limit` is the append rule's cap on uncovered journal bytes on disk (§3.4).
- **`Directory` (v2.75).** The grant is the writer's simultaneous peak: its **lifetime** terms plus the **largest** of three phases that never overlap. Lifetime: r; the journal worker, a grant of `align_up(group_bytes, 4096)` + 4 KiB + 32 KiB plus its MEM-24 task charge 288 + 64 (it returns `Result[(), Error]`); the 4 KiB journal-creation buffer; and the five journal channels at their MEM-24 charges, 168g + 456 for g = `group_commits` (§3.4), 11,208 B at g = 64 (v2.174). Directory has no idle timer; the 4 KiB timer task and its timer channel are Bucket terms (v2.153 corrects this sentence). Phases: **recovery** holds one 64 KiB input chunk and one checked frame, 64 KiB + `FRAME_LIMIT`; **write** holds a sealed frame while earlier frames up to `FRAME_LIMIT` wait for their ack (§3.4's in-flight bound), 2 × `FRAME_LIMIT`; a **cut** first drains every handed-off frame, then holds its output, max(`pack_bytes`, the MANIFEST file at its 16 MiB metadata limit = 16,777,604, charged as round8 = 16,777,608), and its working bound. `resident_limit` = r, the largest value with lifetime + max(recovery, write, cut) ≤ share. A `Shortage` itemizes the lifetime terms, r and the maximizing phase's terms, so `need` is still their sum. `journal_limit` is not a term: its bytes are on disk. v2.75 left the writer's fixed state unpriced. The writer plan below prices it.
- **The writer plan (v2.76).** `writer_plan(kind, o)` prices the grant that `open` makes for `o`. `planned` sizes with the same function, so one function owns T. Every term is a recipe applied to a type (MEM-33), and none is a literal:
  - **Journal channels.** The five channels of §3.4 (input, ack, ready, written, synced) are priced as `charge.channel(bytes[Item], capacity)`, one call per channel, with capacities 2g, 3g + 3, 1, 2 and 1: (64 + 2g × 112) + (64 + (3g + 3) × 64) + (64 + 24) + (64 + 2 × 20) + (64 + 0) = 416g + 576, or 27,200 B at g = 64 (v2.153 corrects v2.75's six channels and 416g + 640).
  - **Directory queue split (v2.174).** The Directory input item is `DirJournalMsg` (8-byte tag plus 40-byte Rotate payload) and the ack item is `DirAck` (8-byte tag plus two u64s for the largest payload). The five charges are (64 + 2g × 48) + (64 + (3g + 3) × 24) + (64 + 24) + (64 + 2 × 20) + (64 + 0) = 168g + 456, or 11,208 B at g = 64. Bucket keeps the common queue types and the preceding channel charges.
  - **Worker and timer.** The Directory journal worker is `charge.task(bytes[Result[(), Error]], journal_group_room(group_bytes) + JOURNAL_WORKER_SLACK)`, that is 256 + 32 + 64 + `align_up(group_bytes, 4096)` + 4,096 + 32,768 (102,752 B at a 64 KiB group, 67,146,080 B at 64 MiB). Directory has no timer task. Bucket's object journal adds its own timer, `charge.task(bytes[()], 4 KiB)`, and its capacity-1 timer channel (v2.153). **L94:** group coalescing and the END cadence (§3.3) add **no charge**: no timer task, no timer channel and no queue slot. The deadlines are waits in the worker's own `channel.receive_until` (tasks.md CONC-5), whose one live deadline registration per task is 40 B prepaid within the existing `TASK_RECORD`, with no admission at the call; the payload-less `Flush` variant leaves `bytes[JournalMsg]` at 112 (48 for the split `DirJournalMsg`); the worker's `Clock` (8 B) and its private cadence settings (16 B) come out of its existing slack, which L94 J4's exact-share open checks with both deadline paths exercised. L94 kept the common queue charge. With the Directory split in v2.174, `journal_channel_bytes(g)` is `168g + 456` and the old minimum share still admits the writer. (v2.149's two 4 KiB timer tasks, two request channels and `2g + 3` queue, 9,248 B, are withdrawn.)
  - **The writer's fixed state** is a new lifetime term, `writer_state`. At genesis the five empty pages (680 B) and the four initial branch slots (272 B each; a slot's roots are three 64-byte page trees and the 24-byte keyed tree list) cost 1,768 B by MEM-24. The Db record is inline and the provider holds its mechanical file bookkeeping. Store's size law measures the retained writer charge after the 88 B startup channel is refunded.
  - **Growing metadata.** The location tables, the branch list and the pin list grow with what the store holds: one row per pack, per branch and per pin. They cannot go in r's resident account, because §1.11 recomputes that account from tree contents at each cut. Each growth is charged at its row's recipe size to the current limit of the Db call that grows it (MEM-26), which is the opening task's limit. A refusal is that call's `Full`, with nothing changed. The count is the live packs, branches and pins. **Open (v2.76):** no plan term covers these rows yet, so a caller budgets them beside T. The end state prices each list at a stated bound (a bound on packs from `retain` and compaction, and on branches and pins from new count limits) as a lifetime term. Choosing those bounds is a later STORE change.
  - **Phases.** Recovery, write and cut are as v2.75 states them. A cut's output is `cut_output_bytes`, max(`pack_bytes`, the MANIFEST file at its metadata limit). The cut phase also gains `CUT_STEP_BYTES` = 16,715,776, one step's copy into the paused writer's state (§13.8 "Each step's peak").
  - **`WriterPlan`** keeps T, its lifetime terms and the maximizing phase's terms. A `Shortage` lists the same parts.
- **The place plan (v2.76).** `planned(kind, share, o)` returns the `Options` that `sized_with(kind, share − X, o)` returns (for `Memory` and `Directory`, X = 0, so `sized_with(kind, share, o)`), together with:
  - X = 0 for `Memory` and `Directory`. For `Bucket`, X = `service_bytes([])` + `follower_starter_bytes()`, and `planned_capture` is the `FollowerPlan` of those `Options`.
  - `planned_bytes`, which is T + X. This equals max(T, L + `service_bytes([capture])` + `follower_starter_bytes()`), because F = T − L.
  - **How the share is solved.** Store solves for T + X ≤ `share`, so X comes out of the share inside Store, never in a caller.
  - **Shortage.** A `Shortage` itemizes X's two parts beside T's parts.
  - **What a caller does.** A caller multiplies `planned_bytes` by the number of stores it holds at once and adds its own terms, and does nothing else with a Store figure (MEM-33 "Who computes what").
- **`Bucket` (v2.78).** As for Directory, r is the largest value with lifetime + max(recovery, write, cut) ≤ the writer's share. The lifetime terms are r, fixed writer state, journal channels, and §12.9's lane reservation, journal workspace, timer and worker (with its reclaim page).
  - **Recovery.** A fetched entry and one decoded frame, or the checkpoint packet and one pack read, whichever is larger. Suffix and location tables are charged where they grow (§12.9).
  - **Journal write.** One staged frame and up to `FRAME_LIMIT` of frames awaiting journal acknowledgment. The worker uses its own grant and the §12.9 workspace for the history packet and comparisons.
  - **Cut.** After draining journal frames, the writer takes the journal session and keeps its workspace while the cut uses a second one. The cut holds one output of up to max(`pack_bytes`, the MANIFEST file bound), two head buffers, a key, a packet large enough for the locator root and retained checkpoint references, and a comparison buffer large enough for the output. Its upload room covers the greater of one multipart part with its list slot and the encoded MANIFEST, which occur in separate steps. Add the per-node working bound and `CUT_STEP_BYTES` (§13.8). A `Shortage` lists the lifetime and maximizing phase terms.
  - `journal_limit` sets the uncovered-history limit. `Bucket` carries the lane configuration passed to `std.object.start`, including its default-lane selection.
- `group_commits` keeps its listed default of 64 and `lock_wait_ms` defaults to 0 unless explicitly overridden. The other count fields (`retain`, `checkpoint_entries`, `claim_ms`, `head_poll_ms`) keep their listed defaults.
- `Options.streams_max: Option[u64]` declares the global call stream quota. `Some(0)` disables new streams. `None` uses the recorded control row on reopen and derives the initial quota at one stream per 4 KiB of `resident_limit` when no quota has been recorded. A writer open with a declared quota that differs from the recorded control row returns `Changed("streams_max")`. The per-caller quota and retention time are writer options. Actual stream rows and replies consume resident bytes under the usual Store accounting. `create`, `expect`, `activation` and `binding` are the caller's.
- **The Tiered plan (v2.60, astra 1995 #14).** The Tiered figures are carved out of r, never added beside it, because §13.8's resident account already holds `cache_bytes`. Let V = `VALUE_LIMIT`, Wmin = 2V + 1 MiB, and U the sum of the Reader reservations the caller will make (`Overrides.readers`, default one Reader of V + 1 MiB; each at least V + 1 MiB, §13.3). For an integer q from Wmin through 64 MiB: `writer_pin_bytes` W = q, `dirty_bytes` D = q and `pager_task_bytes` P = ⌈q / 4⌉, and `cache_bytes` C is sized from the remainder (v2.76, below). These weights are GUESS defaults (R8). At q = 64 MiB and r ≥ 439,374,696, they are §13.8's listed values. An override replaces its own field before solving, W in C's floor included. The plan requires W ≥ Wmin, C ≥ W + U and §13.8's resident floor r ≥ C + K + D + P + 64 MiB, with K, D and P counted once and the writer and reader pins inside C, never again. K = `CUT_PIN_BYTES` = 19,944,296 is the cut pin quota (v2.74, §13.8). It is a constant of the format, derived from the cut's access path. It is not an `Overrides` or `Options` field, and it does not depend on q. `sized` picks the largest feasible q; Memory rows get what remains of r. When no q is feasible, `sized` sets the four fields to 0 and the store can hold no Tiered collection: `open` of a catalog with one is `Missing("cache_bytes")`, and a promotion is refused as below, each before anything is reserved or claimed. C is reserved once with its partitions, K once as the backing of the pager's cut-pinned frames, D with the replaced list (§13.6), and P for the pager. A pager GET's frames land in C, or in K for a cut's demand. Its range buffer is the pager's own (§13.11). Neither has a term of its own.
- **The cache from the remainder (v2.76; replaces C = max(4q, W + U)).** C has a guaranteed part and an optional part:
  - **The floor is the guarantee.** For q, the floor is f(q) = (W + U) + K + D + P + 64 MiB. That is 2.25q, rounded up through P, plus U + K + 64 MiB, so f increases strictly in q. A q is feasible when W ≥ Wmin and f(q) ≤ r, and feasibility is monotone in q, so `sized` binary-searches it as before and picks the largest feasible q.
  - **The cache is what remains, up to its target.** C = max(W + U, min(4q, r − K − D − P − 64 MiB)). The upper bound 4q is the old tuning target, now a ceiling instead of a floor. The Memory rows keep the 64 MiB floor and everything above C, so the cache and the Memory rows never claim the same byte.
  - **Overrides.** An override of `cache_bytes` replaces C and must still be at least W + U and fit f. An override of W moves W + U with it.
  - **Every outstanding pin grant is protected.** C ≥ W + U holds at every r, so the writer's W and each Reader's reservation (§13.3) keep their partitions in full. The part of C above W + U is the shared unpinned side (§13.2), which no grant and no cut pins.
  - **The default floor.** At q = Wmin = 2 × 16,711,680 + 1,048,576 = 34,471,936, with one default Reader U = 17,760,256: C = 52,232,192, K = 19,944,296, D = 34,471,936, P = 8,617,984, and the Memory floor is 67,108,864. The sum is **182,375,272**, against 268,030,824 when C was 4q = 137,887,744. Above the floor q grows faster than before, because f(q) is about 2.25q where it was about 6.25q. q reaches 64 MiB at r = 255,808,360, where it used to need 439,374,696. Between those two figures W, D and P are larger than v2.75 gave and C is smaller. At r = 268,030,824, W and D move from 34,471,936 to 67,108,864 and C from 137,887,744 to 97,091,584. From 439,374,696 up every figure is unchanged.
  - **No per-slot term.** No plan figure depends on a slot or row count, so M3 S5 can drop its 24 B/slot exact-growth accounting without moving the floor.
- **Which plan.** `open` selects the plan from the recovered catalog (or, at genesis, the schema it is about to declare) before it reserves anything or claims a Bucket. A store with no Tiered collection reserves zero cache, dirty and pager bytes and starts no pager, so its Memory rows get all of r. The first Memory → Tiered `set_residency` is admitted against the Tiered plan before it changes anything: the Memory rows already resident plus C + K + D + P + 64 MiB must fit r, else `Full(Resident(Capacity { requested, available: r }))` with nothing changed. On a memory store Tiered is `Tiered(Memory)` (§13.8) and the plan is the non-Tiered one.
- **Checked arithmetic.** The root subtraction and every sum above are checked; an overflow or a negative remainder is the `Shortage` below (in `sized`) or the refusal above (at `open` and promotion), never a wrapped figure.
- `sized` refuses when r would be below 1 MiB or any floor (`journal_limit` ≥ `checkpoint_bytes` + `FRAME_LIMIT`,) fails: `Shortage{need, have: share, parts}`, where `parts` names each figure with its bytes and `need` is their sum at the floors. With `Overrides`, a `Some` figure replaces its derived value, and the remaining derived figures are computed after it; a sum past `share` is the same `Shortage`. There are no named profiles, and the "default" comments above are the figures for share = 2 GiB.

**A follower's plan (v2.69 B, MEM-30).**

```hirsel
pub opaque type FollowerPlan: send                                            // effective Options, the kind and F; computing or copying it reserves nothing
pub fn follower_plan(kind: Kind, o: Options) -> Result[FollowerPlan, Shortage]
pub fn plan_bytes(p: FollowerPlan) -> u64                                     // F
pub fn service_bytes(plans: List[FollowerPlan]) -> Option[u64]                // S + the sum of F; None on overflow
pub fn follower_starter_bytes() -> u64                                         // v2.70 D2: the starter's charge outside `budget` (§12.5 "The starter's charges"); 1,434 at the current build's types
```

- **Which fields.** The plan keeps `o`'s size and count fields, and **holds no heap storage** (v2.70, D2): no String or Bytes content of `o` is copied into it, so copying or cloning a plan allocates nothing. `create`, `activation` and `image` select a writer and are ignored, and `expect` is `follower`'s own argument, so the plan ignores `o.expect`.
- **The service's limit.** A `FollowerService` started with `budget` provisions slots inside that limit. S is the service's own fixed storage: its request channel and its loop state, each at its MEM-24 logical size. `service_bytes` returns S plus the sum of the plans' F with checked arithmetic, which is the `budget` that lets every listed plan hold a slot at once; a smaller `budget` is legal, and a slot it cannot fit is refused as below.

- **T and L.** T is the checked total of the parts above at `o`'s figures for `kind` (for `Directory`, v2.75's lifetime terms plus its largest phase, priced by v2.76's writer plan): the figure `sized` and `sized_with` compare with `share`, and the parts a `Shortage` itemizes. For `Directory` L = 0. For `Bucket`, L is exactly the `client_lanes` part at `o`'s lane configuration. The follower envelope is **F = T − L**. A follower's transport is the authority's: it was started with its own reservation under its own owner, and moving its `Requests` endpoint into a worker resets no inherited bound, so any transport workers it depends on are started under their owner at startup too. L is the sizing term removed from T, not a claim that the transport costs L. A deployment budgets each transport once at its owner and F once per provisioned follower, and a caller planning several followers fits their sum and its other live charges at the service's limit.
- **The holder-derived total (open item, v2.69 B).** F uses the holder's parts, so the journal, timer, cut and PUT terms enlarge the envelope although a follower creates none of those objects and reserves nothing a second time for them. The `Shortage` and `Overrides` rules above apply with their floors. F is fixed by the plan, however much room the service has. A tighter default needs a follower sizing law of its own.
- **Q and N.** Q is the fixed per-slot control storage at the service: one capacity-one command channel (64 + the command's logical size, MEM-24) and the MEM-24 charge of the service's entry that holds the worker's Task handle and retirement notification, each at its logical size and in fixed per-slot storage, so a growing registry cannot consume another slot's grant. Replies use a capacity-one channel per request, charged to the requester. All other worker control storage is made inside the worker. The worker returns `()`, so its MEM-24 task charge is 288 + N, and its root limit is **N = F − Q − 288**. Every product, sum and difference is checked. When Q + 288 > F, `follower_plan` returns `Shortage{need: Q + 288, have: F, parts}` with both parts itemized.
- **What N pays.** Every allocation the worker makes draws on N (§12.9), including a Tiered follower's pager task and its cache, which are the worker's children. A Reader's pin partition already inside that cache adds no reservation (§13.4). `resident_limit` stays AP15's separate logical ceiling, carried in the plan's Options (§12.5 "Resident memory").

`open` takes `Random` for the identity: 16 bytes from `host.random(r, mut b)` (host.hirsel:31, landed 1951a976), drawn once at genesis (D7).

```hirsel
pub type Error =
      Held                         // another writer holds LOCK (log@1; objects@1 has no Held, a later claim deposes, §12.3)
    | NotFound                     // no MANIFEST (log@1) or no head (objects@1) and create is false; or no head while `o.expect` or `o.activation ≠ 0` is set (§12.1)
    | Corrupt(Fault)               // bytes from disk failed a check (§2.8)
    | Unsupported(u64)             // a format number other than 1, or an unknown MUST kind (value = kind)
    | Io(IoError)                  // a host operation failed before anything was published
    | Poisoned(IoError)            // a write or a sync failed earlier; the Db accepts only close
    | Full(Capacity)               // resident_limit: an open, a schema commit or a committing admit would pass it (§1.11, AE3)
    | Limit(Limit)
    | Schema(u64)                  // codec.resolve: the stored writer schema does not resolve; offset into it (SEM-10)
    | Stale(u32)                   // a handle's id is not live in the catalog it reads (I3), or the write Tx's registry lacks the table id (§1.2)
    | Conflict(String)             // v2.57 DX Q3: a Unique index entry is owned by another key (index name); the Tx is abort-only after it (§1.2)
    | NotReady(String)             // v2.115: a read of an index whose record is not Public (index name) (§1.2 "Index states")
    | Drift(String)                // v2.115: a remove found its index entry absent on a row the index covers; the index is demoted (index name) (§1.2)
    | Changed(String)              // v2.57 DX Q1: Open or Follower: an index's kind, composite identity (v2.172) or projection revision differs from the catalog's (index name)
    | Undeclared(String)           // v2.57 DX Q1: a catalog table or index that the declaration does not name (§1.2)
    | Decode(codec.DecodeError)    // a stored row failed its codec: only a schema bug in user code
    | Exists(String) | Missing(String)
    | Diverged(u32)                // adopt: main moved after the branch forked (branch id)
    | Foreign                      // a handle of another store, or a Snapshot or Ticket of another open (§1.12); an authority that holds another store (§12.1)
    | Fenced(u64)                  // another holder's bytes are in the head; the value is this holder's epoch. Whether an outstanding group applied is unknown until the next claim (§12.3)
    | Lost                         // open's claim lost: another claimant won, a genesis race was lost, or `claim_ms` ran out (§12.3)
    | Retired                      // follower worker or service endpoint closed (§12.5, v2.71)
    | Undecided                    // a head write's outcome stayed unknown after the Q5 rule; the claim is dead and only a later claim decides (§12.3)
    | Remote(std.object.Error)     // an authority request failed before any byte of it could have applied; the holder stops until reopened (§12.3)
    | NoLevel(String)              // the authority declares no level of this name (§12.4)
    | Declared(String)             // the grant's level declaration differs from the store's at this level name; nothing written (§12.1, §12.4)
    | NotCurrent(u64)              // `Options.activation` differs from the head's; the value is the head's (§12.1)
    | Endpoint(EndpointRefusal)    // v2.77: the endpoint cannot hold the store: Insecure | Unproven | NotSimulator | IgnoresIfNoneMatch | IgnoresIfMatch (§12.2)
    | Behind(Position)             // a follower reached its deadline; the value is its applied Position on that branch (§12.5)
    | Gone(u32)                    // the branch of a Position was deleted or adopted (§12.5)
    | Unseen(u32)                  // v2.47: a follower's deadline passed before it applied the branch's creation (§12.5)
    | Missed                       // v2.59: a latched Cold miss inside a body attempt (§13.3); seen only by the body, never returned from run, serve or look
    | Reclaimed(u64)               // a follower needed an object that reclaim removed; the value is the new floor (§12.5, §12.6)
    // OutOfOrder: not built (failed ship gate in v2.162).
pub type Limit = Key | Value | Transaction | Name
pub type Fault { file: String, offset: u64, why: Why }
pub type Why = Checksum | Truncated | Flags | Kind(u64) | Header | Gap(u64) | Order | Dangling(u64) | Malformed | Absent   // Absent (v2.46): a named object that is still live is missing (§12.5)
```

There is **no `Cancelled` case.** A cancellation is a failure that `isolate` does not catch, so it never reaches a caller as a value (C5, §3.7).

**Limits.** These are fixed at creation and recorded in the manifest. The values are the old store's (STORE-RECORD.md, BY READING):

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| tree key (table prefix included) | 4096 bytes |
| value | 1 MiB |
| one transaction's COMMIT payload (the frame's `len`, head excluded) | 16 MiB + 64 = 16,777,280 bytes in a store with a journal; the one transaction limit, the same as §2.7's COMMIT row (U1). A `memory` store has no frame and no transaction size limit: its resident account (§1.11) and the caller's byte bound limit a transaction (v2.55, Spec Q4) |
| branch, pin and table names | 255 bytes |
| fan-out | 16–32 entries per node (998's occupancy) |

The old limit of 10,000 rows per range is dropped: a cursor needs no limit.

### 1.2 Tables and indexes

v2.57 (DX Q1, Q3): one handle per table, and index extractors live in a registry. `Shape`, `shape`, `spec`, `with_index`, `TableSpec`, `create_table`, `create_index`, `table`, `index` and the store-level `migrate`/`drop_table` are deleted. A program declares its schema through `Declare`, and changes its catalog only through `Migration` in `Migrate` mode.

```hirsel
pub opaque type Readers[V]: shareable + send   // Codec[V], current schema number, List[Option[codec.Reader[V]]] by number
pub opaque type Table[K, V]: shareable + send  // StoreId, table id, catalog key, Key[K], Arc[Readers[V]]: reads and writes; no extractors, no epoch
pub opaque type Index[J, K, V, P]: shareable + send // StoreId, index id, catalog key, kind, owning table id, Key[J], Key[K], Arc[Readers[V]], Arc[Readers[P]]
pub type IndexKind = Many | Unique

pub type Mode = Migrate | Open | Follower
pub opaque type Declare                          // not send: the mode, the captured base, the staged catalog, the index registry being built, the names declared
pub opaque type TableDecl[K, V]                  // not send: a table being declared; unusable for reads and writes until `finish`
pub fn declare_table[K, V](mut d: Declare, name: String, take key: codec.Key[K], take value: codec.Codec[V]) -> Result[TableDecl[K, V], Error]
pub fn index[J, K, V](mut d: Declare, mut t: TableDecl[K, V], name: String, kind: IndexKind,
        by: StaticFn[fn(K, V) -> Result[List[J], Capacity]], take key: codec.Key[J]) -> Result[Index[J, K, V, ()], Error]
pub fn covering[J, K, V, P](mut d: Declare, mut t: TableDecl[K, V], name: String, kind: IndexKind,
        by: StaticFn[fn(K, V) -> Result[List[J], Capacity]], take key: codec.Key[J],
        project: StaticFn[fn(K, V) -> Result[P, Capacity]], take payload: codec.Codec[P]) -> Result[Index[J, K, V, P], Error]
pub fn covering_row[J, K, V](mut d: Declare, mut t: TableDecl[K, V], name: String, kind: IndexKind,
        by: StaticFn[fn(K, V) -> Result[List[J], Capacity]], take key: codec.Key[J]) -> Result[Index[J, K, V, V], Error]   // the identity projection
pub fn finish[K, V](mut d: Declare, take t: TableDecl[K, V]) -> Result[Table[K, V], Error]
pub fn declare(db: Db, mode: Mode) -> Result[Declare, Error]             // Migrate or Open; Follower is `declare_follower`
pub fn declare_follower(f: Follower) -> Declare
pub fn declare_read_only(source: ReadOnly) -> Declare
pub fn seal_read_only(source: ReadOnly, take d: Declare) -> Result[(), Error]
pub fn bind_read_only[H](source: ReadOnly, schema: fn(mut Declare) -> Result[H, Error]) -> Result[H, Error]
pub fn seal(mut db: Db, take d: Declare) -> Result[Ticket, Error] waits  // Migrate: the one schema commit; Open: checks undeclared names, commits nothing
pub fn seal_follower(f: Follower, take d: Declare) -> Result[(), Error]  // checks undeclared names at the captured base

pub opaque type Migration                        // not send: made for `on_migrate` only, in Migrate mode (AL4)
pub type CollectionKind: send = Table() | Cell() | Log()
pub type CollectionInfo: send { name: String, kind: CollectionKind }
pub fn list_collections(m: Migration) -> Result[List[CollectionInfo], Error]
pub fn migrate_table[K, V, K2, V2](mut m: Migration, from: String, take key: codec.Key[K], take value: codec.Codec[V],
        to: String, take key2: codec.Key[K2], take value2: codec.Codec[V2],
        f: fn(K, V) -> Result[Option[(K2, V2)], Capacity]) -> Result[(), Error]
pub fn drop_named_table(mut m: Migration, name: String) -> Result[(), Error]
pub fn rename_table(mut m: Migration, from: String, to: String) -> Result[(), Error]
```

A `mut` lend lasts for one call (OWN-7, OWN-8), so `declare` captures a private base through a view. `seal` takes a fresh mutable lend and checks the exact base before publishing.

`list_collections` returns an owned list of top-level application collections in unsigned UTF-8 byte order by name. It reads the current staged catalog, so it sees collections created, renamed or dropped earlier in the same migration. It skips `hirsel.*` names and secondary indexes. An Edge appears once as `Table`, and Cells and Logs appear under their own kinds.

The call checks `Tiered(Migrate)` before opening the catalog cursor (§13.10). It scans only the top-level key range and reads no collection rows. The scan and result allocations spend steps and bytes under the migration grant. The step cost grows with the top-level catalog scanned. A capacity refusal aborts the listing through the migration's `Full(Allocation(...))` path. Listing never changes the staged catalog.

**The registry (DX Q1, Fable 5).** Each `Db` and each `Follower` owns one index registry: a map from table id to the erased extractors and projections of that table's indexes, in declaration order. Each entry is an owning `own[send] fn(K, V) -> Result[(List[Bytes], Bytes), Capacity]` that returns the sorted, deduplicated encoded keys and the encoded payload. `seal` installs it. A write `Tx` made by `run`, `run_on` or `serve` borrows the registry of its `Db` for its lifetime. `put` and `delete` look up the table id there, once per call. A table id the registry lacks (a `Table` from another `Declare` of this open) is `Stale(id)`. So there is no epoch: the catalog and the registry change together, at `seal`, and a handle names only an id. A `Follower`'s registry has no extractors, and its Tx cannot be a write Tx.

**What `Declare` does, by mode.**
- The catalog entry of a table holds its name, its key schema, its value schema list (D1, below) and, for each index, the index's:
  - name, kind, key schema and payload schema list;
  - `code.identity` of `by` and its **composite identity** (v2.172), 160 bytes in the catalog's length-prefixed `revision` field: `code.revision(by)` (32 bytes), then the storage fingerprints (SEM-10) of the table's key codec, its value codec, the index key codec and the payload codec, in K, V, J, P order, `std.codec.key_fingerprint`, `fingerprint`, `key_fingerprint` and `fingerprint`, 32 bytes each. So every codec the index decodes or encodes through is covered by what it stores: its rules and their versions, its declaration's field and variant order, defaults, tombstones and tags, and, for opaque and `via` codecs, the exact revisions of their code. A change in how std is lowered, or in what a codec charges, leaves every fingerprint that reaches no opaque part and no `via` node as it is. The composite still changes when such a change reaches the code of `by`, an opaque codec or a `via` body, since their exact revisions are kept. The catalog also keeps `code.identity` and `code.revision` of `project` if it has one. `covering_row` stores the table's own schema list as its payload schemas and no projection.
- The extractor and the projection keep their exact revisions because they are arbitrary code: their result is the index's content, and a nested `bound steps` refusal they catch can turn a charge change into a different key. A codec fingerprint never stands in for them. `index_revision`, the one helper that builds the composite, also builds it for aggregates (§1.2 "Aggregates") and for `hirsel.expiry`, so they follow the same rule.
- On a disk store, a declaration whose `code.revision` or fingerprint is unavailable is `Missing("revision")`. A memory store stores the composite as absent and compares identities alone. PROG-9's revision covers the function's whole reachable checked IR, so it sees a body edit that the identity keeps.
- **`Migrate`** stages, in order:
  1. `on_migrate`'s `Migration` operations;
  2. each declared table: created if absent, and a new value schema appended if it resolves (D1);
  3. each declared index: created if absent, rebuilt if its kind, key schema, payload schema, composite identity or projection revision differs, kept otherwise;
  4. each catalog index of a declared table that is not declared: dropped;
  5. each catalog table outside the reserved `hirsel.` namespace that is not declared and was not dropped or renamed in step 1: `Undeclared(name)`, and nothing commits.
  
  `seal` publishes all of it in one schema commit (§3.5), at version + 1. A refusal at any step changes nothing.
- **`Open`** checks without writing. An absent table or index is `Missing(name)`, a different key or payload schema is `Schema(0)`, a different kind, composite identity or projection revision is `Changed(name)`, a value schema the stored list lacks is `Missing("schema")` (only Migrate appends), and a catalog index or app table the declaration does not name is `Undeclared(name)`, reported by `seal`. So a release whose identity matches its store (RUNNER-SPEC §6) always opens.
- **`Follower`** makes `Open`'s checks over a follower's applied catalog or a read-only capture. `seal_follower` and `seal_read_only` check completeness against the captured base. `bind_read_only` declares, applies the schema callback and seals against that base.
- **Names.** A repeated table or index name within one `Declare` is `Exists(name)`. The reserved `hirsel.` namespace is the runner's, the projector's and the store's own (the index `hirsel.expiry` that `expire_rows` declares); an application name in it is `Missing(name)`. Reserved tables carry no indexes: each is created with none, and no declaration can add one, because `index` takes a `TableDecl` and no reserved table is handed out as one.

**Cutover to fingerprints (v2.172).** The catalog's field keeps its encoding; only its contents change. A store written before v2.172 holds 416-byte composites with four 96-byte codec revisions, and no fingerprint can be derived from them, so every one of its indexes, aggregates and expiries is `Changed(name)` once under `Open` and `Follower`, and the first `Migrate` rebuilds each through the ordinary path (step 3 above, §1.2 "The builder"), reads returning `NotReady` until it is Public. After that rebuild, a toolchain whose only changes are lowering or charges keeps Open every index whose codecs are structural and whose `by` and `project` reach no changed body. There is no equivalence check and no second reader: the 416-byte composite is only compared, by length, and found different.
- **Bounds.** The capture bound (`CATALOG_REVISION_MAX`), the projector's revision bytes and the inspection output keep admitting 416 bytes, so a store written before v2.172 can still be captured, inspected and migrated. The bound drops to 160 (`32 + 4 * 32`) at the next format-word change (§11.1 AP1), since a store that crosses it no longer opens with a pre-v2.172 catalog.
- **Inspection and dry-run.** `hirsel store inspect` prints an index's or aggregate's composite identity in hex, whatever its length, as it printed the revision; its byte layout is the one above. The dry-run's rebuild report splits a 160-byte composite at 32, 64, 96, 128 and 160, the ends `index_revision` returns, and reports a pre-v2.172 composite as `revision layout`.
- **Frozen corpus.** The build that implements this cutover refreezes the Directory and Bucket corpus once (`core/tools/store_freeze_corpus.py`), so its catalog holds v2.172 composites. Those bytes then stay fixed across every toolchain change that alters no rule version and no body that a corpus extractor, projection or opaque codec reaches: `test_frozen_format_corpus` opens them under `Open` and fails on a `Changed`. A change that does reach such a body refreezes the corpus as today.

**Index entries (DX Q3).** A `Many` entry is `ix u32 BE ‖ J ‖ K => payload`. A `Unique` entry is `ix u32 BE ‖ J => u32 LE len(K) ‖ K ‖ payload`. A payload is empty for `()`. Otherwise it is `u16 LE schema number ‖ codec bytes`, numbered by the index's own append-only payload schema list and read through its own `Readers[P]`, transcoded to the current P like a row (D1). A `covering_row` payload is the row's stored bytes, schema number included. The extractor's list is sorted by encoded bytes and deduplicated before staging. Extraction, sorting, deduplication, payload encoding and comparison, conflict probes and edit planning all run inside the write's byte and step bounds (MEM-19, MEM-30), with identical steps whether or not roots are retained (AP15's law extended: L74). A many-key extractor that returns n keys costs O(n log n) of the write's steps, duplicates included. An unchanged encoded key with byte-equal payload bytes is not rewritten. A changed payload at an unchanged key is rewritten. Each index entry is charged as its own row version (`62 + r8(key) + r8(value)`, §1.11) and its own COMMIT op bytes. No payload bytes are shared between a row and its covering entries, or between two indexes.

**Unique writes (DX Q3, Astra 9, Fable 11, 15).** `put(mut tx, t, k, v)` and `delete(mut tx, t, k)` build the complete edit before staging any part of it:
- the old row, from the staged view;
- each index's old and new key sets, with their payloads;
- the primary edit;
- the COMMIT op bytes and the resident charge (§1.1 limits, §1.11).

Then, for each `Unique` index in declaration order and each J in the new set but not the old (encoded order), it probes the staged view of `ix ‖ J`. An entry whose K differs from k is `Conflict(index name)`. A successful put records `Point(ix ‖ J)` for each probe. A transaction limit, `Limit(Key)` or `Limit(Value)` is found in the same preflight. Only a complete edit is staged. On any error nothing of it is staged, and on `Conflict` the Tx becomes **abort-only**:
- Every later `put` or `delete` in it returns the first `Conflict` with nothing staged, and reads continue.
- If the body returns `Error(a)`, F2 applies (the data is undone and a reply is kept).
- If the body returns `Ok(r)`, `run` and `run_on` answer `Failed(StoreFailure.Conflict(name))` and commit nothing, and `serve` answers `Failed(p, Conflict(name))`, which the runner concludes as `Failed(Conflict(name))` (RUNNER-SPEC v2.45 §1.1).
- A conflict that a helper swallows therefore cannot commit the writes before it.
- Delete and re-insert in one Tx is not a conflict, because the probe reads the staged view. To swap two rows' unique keys, delete one row, put the other, then put the first.
- `Stop` gains `Conflict(String)`. Re-execution compares it like any `Failed` reply.

**Index states (v2.115, Store 1.1).** Every index record carries a build state:

```hirsel
type IndexState = Backfilling(Option[Bytes]) | Public | Failed(Bytes, Bytes)
```

- **`Backfilling(cursor)`.** The index is being built. `cursor` is the last primary key whose entries are complete; `None` means no row is done yet. Every read of the index (`find`, `find_page`, `lookup`, the `Reader` forms) is `NotReady(name)`, with nothing read. Writes maintain it as they maintain a `Public` index, ahead of the cursor too, so a chunk that later re-extracts a row only overwrites entries the write already made.
- **`Public`.** The index is complete and serves reads.
- **`Failed(first, second)`.** The builder found one `Unique` key under two primary keys, `first` (the entry's owner) and `second` (the row that repeats it). Reads are `NotReady(name)`. `rebuild_index`, or a `Migrate` declaration of the index, restarts it from an empty index.

**Aggregates (v2.118, Store 2.1, D12).** `aggregate[G, K, V](mut d, mut t, name, by: StaticFn[fn(K, V) -> Result[List[(G, u64)], Capacity]], key: Key[G]) -> Result[Aggregate[G], Error]` declares an aggregate index over `t`. Each row gives the parts `(g, value)`; the row counts once in each distinct group it names, with the sum of the values it gave that group.
- **Rows.** The aggregate's collection holds one row per group with rows: key `id u32 BE ‖ G`, value `count u64 LE ‖ sum u64 LE`. A group whose count reaches 0 has no row.
- **Writes.** `put` and `delete` plan each changed group's new totals (the old row's part out, the new row's in) with the rest of the edit, before staging any of it. A sum past `u64` is `Limit(Value)`.
- **Claims.** A write changes the totals only where the aggregate claims the row: a `Public` aggregate, or a `Backfilling(Some(c))` one with the row's key at or before `c`. A row past the cursor is counted once, by the chunk that reaches it. This differs from an entry index, whose writes run ahead of the cursor: an overwrite there is idempotent, an increment is not.
- **Drift.** A claimed row whose old part exceeds its group's count or sum, or a group left with count 0 and a non-zero sum, is `Drift(name)` as in §I.3.
- **Reads.** `totals(tx, a, g) -> Result[Totals, Error]` reads `Totals(count, sum)` for group `g`, `(0, 0)` for a group with no rows, and records `Point` on the group's row. A read of an aggregate that is not `Public` is `NotReady(name)`.
- **Builder.** `index_build_step` and a `Migrate` declaration build an aggregate in the same chunks as an entry index: a chunk adds each of its rows' parts to the group rows and sets the cursor to its last row, in one schema commit. `rebuild_aggregate(mut db, a)` demotes it to `Backfilling(None)` over an empty collection.
- **Contention.** Each group is one row, so every write to a hot group touches the same key. The store's one writer serializes them; a hot group costs no aborts, but it is a single point every such write rewrites.
- **Overflow while building.** A write past the cursor is not counted, so a sum it would overflow is found by the chunk that reaches it: the step refuses `Limit(Value)`, commits nothing, and the aggregate stays `Backfilling` at its cursor until the rows change or it is redeclared. While it stays, `index_build_step` keeps refusing, and indexes after it in the step's order wait.
- **No terminal overflow state (v2.121, Store 2.2).** An overflow during a build keeps the stall above. Search form A, the aggregate's first user, cannot reach it from its term groups, whose sum equals their count. Its corpus sum needs more than 2^64 − 1 tokens in total. A terminal state would be a catalog format change for that case only. If an aggregate does stall, its reads stay `NotReady(name)`, and the remedy is the one above: change the rows or redeclare the aggregate.
- **Not built.** There is no `Reader` form of `totals` and no range read over groups. A reader calls `totals` inside `look`, and search form A reads its groups by key.

**Search form B (v2.144, Store 2.4; form A v2.121, D14 = A).** The `search@1` package ranks a table's rows by BM25. It uses only public store calls (D10).
- **Declaration.** `search.declare(mut d, mut t, name, stop_words, terms)` takes one extractor, `terms: StaticFn[fn(K, V) -> Result[List[(Term, u64)], Capacity]]`. Normally it is `search.analyze(analyzer, text)`: one `(Corpus, length)` part, then one `(Posting(term, tf, length), 1)` part for each distinct term. It declares:
  - `name.stats`, an aggregate whose group key codec writes `0` for `Corpus` and `1 ‖ term` for a posting. The corpus group's totals are the row count N and the token sum. A term group's count is its document frequency. A row with no terms is counted in N. The store records the extractor's revision, so a changed analyzer rebuilds it.
  - `name`, a projector over the table (§1.14) with the default cadence, whose fold writes four tables keyed by generation first: `name.blocks` (`(g, term, block)` → last key bytes, count, and per distinct tf the least token count of a posting with it), `name.postings` (same key → one `Bytes` value: the count, count + 1 key offsets, a tf and token count per posting, an eight-byte big-endian key head per posting, then the keys end to end), `name.heads` (`(g, term)` → the newest block number) and `name.mentions` (`(g, key bytes)` → the row's token count and terms, or a mask for a delete). Rows reach a generation in key order, so a fold appends each posting to its term's newest block, starting a block at 128.
- **Writes.** There is no search write call. The aggregate changes in the row's own transaction; the generations change only through `project_step`.
- **Query.** `search.query(tx, s, text, k, params, allows)` reads the corpus group and one group per distinct query term in `tx`. It takes no `waits`. It scores every tail row (`read_tail`) from the row itself, or every row when there is no base. Then for each generation, oldest first, it reads the query terms' block headers and moves through their postings in windows: a window ends at the least last key of the blocks the terms stand in. A window whose block bounds, summed in query order, cannot enter the heap is passed without reading a posting. Otherwise the terms whose bounds, taken from the least, cannot place a row alone are non-essential: they are read only at a row the essential terms hold, and only when that row's own contributions plus their block bounds can still enter. Every row read is scored with form A's arithmetic in query order. A block's bound is the greatest contribution over its frontier; each correctly rounded operation of the contribution is monotone, so no posting exceeds it. A bound equal to the k-th score prunes only where every row it covers has a key after the k-th hit's, which loses the tie. A row that would enter is checked against the tail's keys and each newer generation's mentions, then `allows(key)`. A query in a transaction sees that transaction's own writes. Equal scores rank in increasing order of the primary key's encoded bytes.
- **Cost.** At 1M rows, top 10, form B takes 5.5–41x fewer steps than form A on published and merged generations (v2.144). Each unprojected tail row costs about 8,600 steps, so the driver keeps the tail short by stepping the projector often.
- **Readiness.** If the aggregate is not `Public`, the query is `NotReady` with its name. Before the projector first publishes, the query scores every row. `search.rebuild(mut db, s)` demotes the aggregate and requests a rebuild of the generations.
- **Overflow.** A term group's sum equals its count, which is at most the row count, so it cannot overflow. A corpus sum past `u64` on a put to a `Public` aggregate is `Limit(Value)`, and the write stages nothing. During a build it is the stall described under "Aggregates".
- **Law.** `core/programs/search/tests.hirsel`:
  - Hand-computed Python BM25 scores for a six-row corpus that includes a row with no terms, with filters, ties, an abort and a retained snapshot.
  - `bm25_histories`: seeded put, overwrite, delete, rebuild and build-step histories, each checked against a brute-force BM25 ranking over the model rows.
  - `block_max_differential`: seeded histories over 2,400 rows with a skewed vocabulary, projector steps that stop mid-pass and mid-merge, rebuilds, filters, queries inside the writing transaction and through a look, and `k` from 0 to 129, each equal to the brute-force ranking exactly.

**Index key codec (v2.121).** `primary_key[J, K, V, P](ix: Index[J, K, V, P]) -> Key[K]` returns the key codec of the index's table.

**Hybrid fusion (v2.137, Store 3.4).** The `hybrid@1` package fuses ranked lists, such as a search form A and a vector query over one table, by reciprocal rank fusion. It is a pure library over the lists: it calls no store function and depends only on `std` (D10).
- **Call.** `hybrid.fuse(key, c, lists, k) -> List[Hit[K]]` takes the key codec of the rows (`key_codec(t)` or `primary_key(ix)`), the constant `c: u64`, the lists of keys, each best first, and `k`. A `Hit` holds the key and its rank in each list, from 1, with 0 where the list does not hold it.
- **Score.** A row scores `Σ 1 / (c + rank)` over the lists that hold it. Its rank in a list is its first position there; a later repeat adds nothing. `c + rank` is computed without overflow for every `u64` pair.
- **Order.** Scores are compared as exact fractions (numerators and denominators as limb integers, cross-multiplied), so the order never depends on rounding. Equal scores rank in increasing order of the key's encoded bytes, so one set of lists gives one order. The first `k` rows are returned.
- **Law.** `hand_fusions` in `core/programs/hybrid/tests.hirsel` checks orders and ranks worked out by hand: a three-way tie at `c = 1` with one tied score a sum of two lists (`1/3 + 1/6 = 1/2`); ranks `(1, 4)` above `(2, 3)` at `c = 60` and at `c = 2^64 − 1`, where the two scores differ by less than an `f64` resolves and every `c + rank` passes `2^64 − 1`; ties at `1 / (c + 1)` across lists ordered by key, not by list order; cuts at `k` inside a tied group; and a repeated key counted once. Red before this change, when `hybrid@1` does not exist.

**The builder.** An index is built in chunks of `INDEX_CHUNK` = 4,096 rows, in primary-key order after the cursor.
- **Each chunk reads the current head.** The chunk's rows come from main's roots at the moment it runs, never from the roots the build started at, so a row written between chunks is extracted as it now is.
- **A chunk commits atomically with its cursor.** The chunk's entries and the record's new state (`Backfilling(last key)`, or `Public` when the table has no row after the chunk) publish in one schema commit. A crash therefore loses at most the chunk in flight, and a reopened build resumes at the committed cursor.
- **Two paths run it.** `seal` in `Migrate` builds a created or rebuilt index inside the declaration's plan, so the declaration commits the finished index in its one cut. An entry index is built bottom up (AP13): one pass extracts every row's entries, charged to the workspace as they are kept, a sort orders them and `std.page.bulk` builds the collection, which replaces the one the record had; a `Backfilling` record is rebuilt whole the same way. An aggregate is built chunk by chunk until `Public`, because its group rows add up parts. A `Unique` duplicate there is `Conflict(name)` and the declaration commits nothing, as before. On a store holding a Tiered collection, `seal` and `run_migration` build each Tiered target under the build pin and publish it in the same one schema commit (§13.10a "Hot Tiered builds", v2.169, text only, not yet built). On a serving store, `index_build_step(mut db, limit)` runs one chunk of at most `limit` rows of the first `Backfilling` index this release binds, as one schema commit, and returns its name (`None` when nothing builds). A duplicate found there moves the index to `Failed` and commits no entry of that chunk.
- **`rebuild_index(mut db, ix)`** demotes a declared index to `Backfilling(None)` over an empty collection in one schema commit; `index_build_step` then rebuilds it while every other index serves.
- **Cost.** Each step is a schema commit, so one checkpoint per chunk (7 syncs, §3.2). The chunk bounds the step's memory and the work a crash loses.
- **Who sees it.** `attention(db).indexes` reports each index's state, and `Status.store` carries it to the runner's operator (v2.116).
- **Not here.** Catching a building index up with the journal suffix of its own build (Store 1.2). The runner's head drives `index_build_step` (v2.123, RUNNER-SPEC §12.5).

**Drift (§I.3).** A remove (an overwrite's old key or a delete) whose index entry is absent, on a row the index claims (`Public`, or `Backfilling(Some(c))` with the row's key at or before `c`), proves the index wrong. The transaction fails with `Drift(name)` and commits nothing; `run` answers `Failed(StoreFailure.Drift(name))` and `serve` refuses it before execution. The writer then counts the drift (`store.attention`, step one) and demotes the index to `Backfilling(None)` in one schema commit, so its reads refuse until a rebuild; that commit counts one in the index's `demoted` (v2.116). A crash before the demotion loses nothing: the next write of that row fails the same way. An absent entry on a row the index does not yet claim is not drift.

**The index walker (v2.123, Store 1.3).** `verify_step(mut db, mut walk, limit) -> Result[WalkReport, Error]` checks one slice of the walk that `begin_verify(mode)` starts. In `Repair` mode (the head's walk) a finding demotes its index as described here; in `Report` mode (§15.6, v2.127) the walk lists every finding, never demotes and never commits. A walk visits every index whose record is `Public` and that this release binds, in catalog-key order. It checks each entry index in two phases:
- **Rows.** Up to `limit` rows after the walk's cursor, read at main's head (through the pager when the table is Tiered). Each row's entries, extracted with the bound extractor, must be in the index collection with the row's payload. An absent entry is `Missing`; a present one with another payload is `Payload`.
- **Entries.** Up to `limit` entries of the index collection after the cursor. Each names its row: a `Unique` entry by the owner in its payload, a `Many` entry by the primary key after its index key. The row is read as a point read at the same head. No row, or a row whose extraction does not produce the entry's key, is `Extra`; a row that produces it with another payload is `Payload`.
- **One head per comparison.** Each entry-index slice reads both sides from main's roots at the moment it runs.
- **Aggregates.** The rows phase folds up to `limit` rows per slice into per-group counts and sums. The comparison phase merges the folded groups with the stored group entries, checking up to `limit` groups per slice. An absent group is `Missing`, an unexpected group is `Extra`, and a different count or sum is `Payload`. The fold and its comparison restart when a commit moves main's head, so the walk never compares totals from different versions.
- **A finding proves the index wrong.** The slice reports every finding it saw (`WalkFinding { index, entry, fault }`), counts the index's drift once (`store.attention`), and demotes it to `Backfilling(None)` in one schema commit, so its reads refuse until the builder rebuilds it. The walk then moves to the next index. Under an export lease the demotion is a step that catch-up ships to the preparation (§3.5a "Catch-up", v2.138).
- `WalkReport { checked, done, findings }`: `checked` counts the rows and entries read since `begin_verify`; `done` says no index is left, and the walk then starts again from the first index.
- **Not here.** A read-only walk for an operator's request (Store 1.4) and the Tiered location classes 3 and 4 on crash cuts (L41's walker, after 2010 S3–S5).

**Expiry (Store 4.1, plan §III.4).** `expire_rows[K, V](mut d, mut t, by: StaticFn[fn(K, V) -> Option[u64]]) -> Result[(), Error]` declares that `t`'s rows expire: `by` gives a row its expiry time in keyed-time milliseconds (`keyed_time`, §1.8), or `None` for a row that never expires.
- **No index kind of its own.** The declaration is an ordinary `Many` index on `key_u64`, named `hirsel.expiry` on that table: entry `id u32 BE ‖ at u64 BE ‖ K`, no payload. A row with `None` has no entry. Its record, composite identity, states, builder, drift, walker and catch-up are every index's, and no format changes. A table has at most one expiry; a second declaration is `Exists`. A release that stops declaring it drops the index under `Migrate` and is `Undeclared("hirsel.expiry")` under `Open`, as for any index.
- **The sweep.** `sweep_expired(mut db, limits: Limits) -> Result[Swept, Error]` reads `now = keyed_time(db)` once and deletes, in one commit at that time, the rows whose expiry is at or before `now`, in (table catalog order, expiry, key) order, through the ordinary delete: every index and aggregate on the table changes in the same commit and the change feed sees an ordinary delete. It takes at most `limits.rows` rows and, after the first, stops before the row bytes it takes would pass `limits.byte_limit`; the first due row always goes, so a row larger than the limit is not stuck. `Swept { rows, ticket }` gives the count and the commit, `ticket: None` when nothing was due. `limits.rows == 0` is `Limit(Transaction)`.
- **Which tables.** Only `Public` expiry indexes this release binds. While one is building, its table's rows wait for it.
- **No read-time filter.** No read consults a clock (SEM-8): an expired row exists, by point read, scan, index and `changes`, until the commit that deletes it. A program that must not act on a row past its time compares the row's time with its own clock.
- **Drift.** A due entry whose row is absent proves the index wrong: the commit stops with `Drift` and the index is demoted and rebuilt as for any write (§I.3), and the sweep returns `rows: 0`.
- **Driver.** The runner's head calls it on idle turns (RUNNER-SPEC §12.5), so a place needs no caller.
- **Not built.** A store with a Tiered collection refuses the sweep with `Missing("steps")`: deleting a Cold row reads it through an attempt, which a bounded store body does not yet take. Age-based Log retention (plan §II.5) is not here.

**Read handles (I3).** A table or index id names one incarnation: ids come from the `next_table` counter and are never reused, so a table recreated after `drop_named_table`, or migrated by `migrate_table`, has a new id.
- Every read (`fetch`, `range`, `count`, `lookup`, `entries`, the prefix forms, and the `Reader` forms of §1.5, also inside `look`) first looks up the handle's catalog key in the catalog tree of the roots it reads: the Tx's roots, or the Snapshot's. If the key is absent, or holds another id, the read is `Stale(id)`, with nothing read and nothing recorded. A catalog root byte-identical to the one-leaf root the handle was resolved against answers without the lookup (I3).
- So a handle from before a drop is `Stale` against a current Tx or a later Snapshot, and reads its rows from a Snapshot or pin older than the drop. A handle made after the drop is `Stale` against that older Snapshot.
- Cost: one catalog lookup per read call, not per row.

**Value schemas (D1).**
- **Schema numbers.** Each table's catalog entry lists the value schemas its rows were written in, as (number u16, schema bytes, fingerprint). The list is append-only, and a number is never reused. Every row value starts with its schema number (§2.4).
- `declare_table` computes the program's value schema (`codec.schema`) and finds it in the list (fingerprint, then bytes):
  - **found** as number n: n becomes the Table's current number, and new rows are written as n;
  - **not found:** in `Migrate`, it is appended as the next number and becomes current; in `Open` and `Follower` it is `Missing("schema")`.
- Every other live number m is resolved once: `codec.resolve(value, schema_m)`, which applies SEM-10 (fields matched by name at every depth; a field the writer lacks takes its literal default; a removed field's tombstone checked).
  - Any `Schema(i)` makes `declare_table` return `Schema(i)`. `i` is the offset into schema m.
  - The Readers are shared by one `Arc`, so a copy of a Table or Index never resolves again.
- **Reading a row:** tag = current number, then `codec.decode`. Tag = an older number, then `codec.read` with that number's Reader. A tag the Readers do not hold is `Stale(table id)`.
- The key schema must be byte-equal to the stored one. A change of key order is always `Schema`, and only `migrate_table` fixes it.
- `migrate_table` writes every row as one new number and retires all older ones. It is the only way to drop an old schema. It gives the table, and each of its indexes, a new id (I3).

**Schema commits.** `seal` in `Migrate` is the only declaration commit. The index builder (`index_build_step`, `rebuild_index`) and a drift demotion are the other schema commits (v2.115). A checkpoint makes each (§3.5), never a journal frame.
- It advances the branch version by one, so an unchanged version means nothing was committed (K1). A `seal` that finds nothing to change commits nothing and leaves the version unchanged. The runner's rule 12 relies on this.
- The catalog therefore changes only at a manifest swap, and every journal suffix is decoded under one catalog.
- `seal` admits its new trees against `resident_limit` before building them, using their accounted size (§1.11), else `Full`.
- Cost: a schema commit costs one checkpoint, which is 7 syncs (§3.2). Schema commits are rare.
- **Format.** The index kind, payload schema list and revisions are catalog fields of Format 5 (STORE-SPEC M3). A store whose catalog lacks them is `Unsupported(format)`, with no migration.
- **Format 11 (v2.166).** Every claimed head carries a 49-byte ORIGIN frame (kind `0x00E0`, §12.3 "ORIGIN"), and the MANIFEST loses its 36-byte `retired` root, so its fixed part is 280 bytes (AP14). A cut's carried removals stay in the writer's memory and are never persisted. A format-10 store is `Unsupported(10)`, and a format-10 binary refuses a format-11 store `Unsupported(11)`; there is no migration.
- **Format 10 (v2.141).** The MANIFEST records the store's limits (AP4a, AP14). A format-9 store is `Unsupported(9)`, with no migration.
- **Format 9 (v2.118).** An index record's kind byte is `0` Many, `1` Unique or `2` aggregate. An aggregate record has no payload schemas and no projection; one with either is `Corrupt(Malformed)`. A format-8 store is `Unsupported(8)`.
- **Format 8 (v2.115).** An index record (catalog kind 2) ends with its state after the projection: `0` Public; `1` Backfilling(None); `blob(cursor) ‖ 2` Backfilling(Some(cursor)); `blob(first) ‖ blob(second) ‖ 3` Failed. A blob is `u32 LE len ‖ bytes`. The tag is the record's last byte, so a reader can tell Public without decoding the rest. Any other tag, or bytes between the projection and the state, is `Corrupt(Malformed)`.

### 1.3 Transactions

```hirsel
pub opaque scoped type Tx                // VERIFY-5 B2: opaque (PROG-2). Base roots (views), working roots, op list, read Log view, scope, CallInfo
pub type StoreFailure = Raised(Causes) | Conflict(String) | Drift(String)   // Drift: v2.115, §1.2
pub type Outcome[R, A] = Committed(Done[R]) | Aborted(Undone[A]) | Failed(StoreFailure) | Refused(Capacity) | Stopped(core.OutOfTime)   // AC1
pub type Undone[A] { value: A, ticket: Option[Ticket] }   // F2: the ticket of the kept reply commit, if any
pub type Done[R] { value: R, ticket: Ticket, info: Option[CallInfo], reads: List[Read] }   // v2.152 F2: None on a skipped zero-mutation commit
pub type Read = Point(Bytes) | Span(Bytes, Bytes)   // data-tree keys (§2.4), the bytes of Change.tree_key; span [lo, hi) (I1)
pub type Bound[K] = Unbounded | Included(K) | Excluded(K)   // std.omap's names (D9); K need not be ordered

pub fn run[R, A](mut db: Db, steps: Option[u64], body: scoped[view] fn(mut Tx) -> Result[R, A]) -> Result[Outcome[R, A], Error] waits   // None: no step scope (AC1); v2.59 §13.3: plain fn + inert env, and None is Missing("steps") on a retry-capable call
pub fn run_on[R, A](mut db: Db, b: Branch, steps: Option[u64], body: scoped[view] fn(mut Tx) -> Result[R, A]) -> Result[Outcome[R, A], Error] waits

pub fn fetch[K, V](tx: Tx, t: Table[K, V], k: K) -> Result[Option[V], Error]       // a fresh value; F5
pub fn fetch_many[K, V](tx: Tx, t: Table[K, V], keys: List[K]) -> Result[List[Option[V]], Error]   // v2.108: fetch per key, in order; Cold misses batched (§13.3)
pub fn put[K, V](mut tx: Tx, t: Table[K, V], k: K, v: V) -> Result[(), Error]
// put_ordered: not built (failed ship gate in v2.162).
pub fn delete[K, V](mut tx: Tx, t: Table[K, V], k: K) -> Result[bool, Error]
pub fn pop_first[K, V](mut tx: Tx, t: Table[K, V]) -> Result[Option[(K, V)], Error]
pub fn pop_last[K, V](mut tx: Tx, t: Table[K, V]) -> Result[Option[(K, V)], Error]
pub fn range[K, V](tx: Tx, t: Table[K, V], lo: Bound[K], hi: Bound[K]) -> Result[TxRows[K, V], Error]   // v2.59: stepped by next_in (§13.4)
pub fn range_prefix[K, V, Q](tx: Tx, t: Table[K, V], q: Q, take prefix: codec.Key[Q]) -> Result[TxRows[K, V], Error]   // v2.57: keys whose leading components equal q
pub fn count[K, V](tx: Tx, t: Table[K, V], lo: Bound[K], hi: Bound[K]) -> Result[u64, Error]   // v2.57: one Span, O(log N) (AP11 subtree counts)
pub fn lookup[J, K, V, P](tx: Tx, ix: Index[J, K, V, P], lo: Bound[J], hi: Bound[J]) -> Result[IndexRows[K, V], Error] in tx   // J1: scoped to the Tx
pub fn lookup_prefix[J, K, V, P, Q](tx: Tx, ix: Index[J, K, V, P], q: Q, take prefix: codec.Key[Q]) -> Result[IndexRows[K, V], Error] in tx
pub fn entries[J, K, V, P](tx: Tx, ix: Index[J, K, V, P], lo: Bound[J], hi: Bound[J]) -> Result[IndexEntries[J, K, P], Error] in tx   // v2.57: index-only (J, K, P), no join
pub fn info(mut tx: Tx) -> CallInfo      // mut: only a transaction body has CallInfo; a look body cannot call it (G2, OWN-5)
pub type CallRecord: codec { key: Bytes, args: Bytes, stream: Bytes, revision: Option[Bytes], code: Bytes }   // F7; p and CallInfo come from the frame; revision: code.revision of the entry that ran; v2.30 AN1: code = u64 n ‖ u64 s (BE) ‖ replay identity (0 or 32 B)
pub type Plan { n_e: u64, s_e: u64, reply_max: u64 }   // v2.30 AN1: the body's byte and step allowances, and the longest reply
pub type Stop = Raised(u32) | OutOfSteps(u64) | OutOfBytes(Capacity) | Conflict(String)   // v2.30 AN1: Policy deleted; v2.57: Ok from an abort-only Tx (§1.2)
pub type Served = Committed(Receipt) | Kept(Receipt) | Failed(Pending, Stop) | NoRoom(Pending, Capacity)   // v2.56 §13.3: NoRoom may carry Cache; v2.29 AM1, AM3; ATTACK-4 B7: the refusal's Capacity
pub type Receipt { ticket: Ticket, reply: Bytes }   // v2.29 AM3: the first delivery, no read-back; v2.30 AN1
pub type ServeError = Before(Error) | After(Error)   // v2.29 AM4: Before leaves the position as it was; After is poison
pub opaque type Pending   // v2.29 AM1: not copy, codec or send; the Completion, the record, the run's CallInfo and base, and on NoRoom the outcome it would have stored
pub fn serve(mut db: Db, take c: Completion, plan: Plan, take rec: Option[CallRecord],
        body: scoped[view] fn(mut Tx) -> Result[Bytes, Bytes]) -> Result[Served, ServeError] waits   // v2.59 §13.3: plain fn + inert env; v2.30 AN1: one isolated execution, the body's; with `conclude`, the only writer of a reply and a record
pub fn conclude(mut db: Db, take p: Pending, take r: Bytes, reserve: Reserve) -> Result[Served, ServeError] waits   // v2.29 AM1, AM6: r with p's record, CallInfo and base, one streams-only commit, no code run; Reserve = Resident | Claim
pub fn untried(take c: Completion, take rec: Option[CallRecord], info: CallInfo) -> Pending   // v2.29 AM1: for a position that runs nothing (a gone key)
pub fn recorded(db: Db, b: Branch, version: u64) -> Result[Option[Recorded], Error] waits   // write barrier, then live segments; None once a taken cut covers the version (W2); v2.29 AM6 (ATTACK-4 M3): with its settle context
pub type StopKind = Raised | OutOfSteps(u64) | OutOfBytes | Conflict   // v2.59: settle 1's typed stop (format 5, AP1a)
pub type Recorded { record: CallRecord, settle: u8, branch: Branch, base: u64, at: u64, seed: u64, stop: Option[StopKind] }   // stop is Some exactly for settle 1; settle 0: the frame's own context; 1 a body fault, 2 an admission refusal: the attempted run's

pub opaque type Rows[K, V]: send         // Arc shares of a path + bounds + Key[K] + Codec[V]
pub fn next[K, V](mut r: Rows[K, V]) -> Result[Option[(K, V)], Error]   // v2.56 §13.4: takes a Reader and waits
pub scoped type IndexRows[K, V]          // index cursor, primary Table, View[Log[Read]] of its Tx (J1)
pub fn next_indexed[K, V](mut r: IndexRows[K, V]) -> Result[Option[(K, V)], Error]   // records the index gap it scanned and Point(table id ‖ Key[K]) per row returned
pub scoped type IndexEntries[J, K, P]
pub fn next_entry[J, K, P](mut r: IndexEntries[J, K, P]) -> Result[Option[(J, K, P)], Error]   // records the index gap only
pub scoped type I8Code = Lent(View[Bytes]) | Owned(List[i8])
pub fn next_i8_entry[K, T](mut r: IndexEntries[(), K, List[i8]], visit: scoped[view] fn(take K, I8Code) -> T) -> Result[Option[T], Error]   // v2.155: lends current-schema List[i8] codes from the page
```

**Single-open index entry scan (v2.155).** `entries` checks the index read (`Foreign`, `Stale`, `NotReady` and a malformed record, in that order), computes both bounds and takes the transaction's collection pages, exactly as before; it opens no cursor. The first `next_entry` or `next_i8_entry` opens one cursor on the index's collection, and every later step continues it. There is no probe, no second open and no outer cursor over the collection map. An index with no collection is exhausted at that first step.
- **Read spans and key order.** Rows come in the collection's encoded key order. Each step records `Span(low, id ‖ suffix ‖ 0x00)` and moves `low` there before the row is decoded, so the span is in the read set even when the step then returns an error. Exhaustion records `Span(low, high)` once. These are the spans of the copying range scan.
- **Key decoding.** Each step decodes the index key and the primary key with the index's key codecs before it reads the payload, as `next_entry` always has. A custom key decoder's error is returned at the same row and offset, before any payload check.
- **Lending.** `next_i8_entry` lends a row's code as `Lent(bytes)` when the index's current payload readers decode with the built-in `List[i8]` decoder (`std.codec.same_decoder`, a PROG-9 identity comparison made once when the `Index` handle is built, with no allocation, with or without compiler revisions) and the row carries the current schema number, a u32 count and exactly that many bytes. Each byte is one signed element. Every other row (an older schema number, a malformed row, another payload codec or no payload readers) is decoded as `next_entry` decodes it and passed as `Owned(list)`, or its error is returned. Values, errors and their order are those of `next_entry`.
- **Charges.** Neither entry point charges more bytes or MEM-30 reference steps than the copying scan of `c1595a59` on any input; the per-class deltas are in `core/programs/vector/README.md`. Building an `Index` handle costs 5 more reference steps and no bytes for the identity comparison.
- **Placement.** The public `IndexEntries`, `I8Code`, `entries`, `next_entry` and `next_i8_entry` stay in `"store"`. The private `EntryCursor`, `step_entry`, `entry_parts`, `lends_codes` and `lends_i8_rows` are `store-read.hirsel` privates and move with the `read` module in L11 of `MODULES.md` v3.

**Table edge pops (v2.146).** `pop_first` and `pop_last` delete and return the least or greatest row in the table's encoded key order, including writes staged in this Tx and its enclosing callbacks. An empty table returns `None`. Each pop records the same gap and row span as one unbounded forward or reverse range step, or the full table span on exhaustion. The value is returned through the table's current readers. The delete uses the same index, frame-limit, and rollback rules as `delete`. A resident table removes and reads the edge in one descent through its private page tree. A Tiered table resolves the edge through its attempt and stages the delete through the Tiered write plan. The private page tree does not enter the journal, whose rows still apply in encoded key order.

**Ascending ingest (v2.150; amended by v2.153, v2.159 and v2.162; source layout built in v2.163).** A run of ascending `put` calls keeps the draft ascending, which removes the sort, the slot map and the general page merge. `put_ordered(mut tx, t, rows)` is an **opt-in** checked batch over the same staging (v2.159, Sam 2026-11-26; design in `/workspace/code/hirsel-briefs/store-write-path-design-v2-3103/DESIGN-v2.2.md` §7). It defines its own deterministic contract: the `put` loop is not its oracle for refusal kind or charge. The candidate was **not built (failed ship gate)** in v2.162. Its design validated everything first, then wrote:
- **Handle.** `check_table_write(tx, t)` once. An empty `rows` returns `Ok(())` here and stages nothing (L91).
- **Phase 1 changes nothing in `tx`**, until it returns an evidence-class refusal. It makes three passes in input order, keeping nothing per row between rows except the previous key and the overlay below.
  - **A1:** encode each tree key (key codec errors here). Row 0 must be above `t`'s largest staged key in the draft and every frozen layer; each later key above the previous one. Otherwise `OutOfOrder`.
  - **A2:** per row, `Limit(Key)`; then the value encode (a codec error is `Limit(Value)`) and `Limit(Value)`; then each extractor and its payload's `Limit(Value)`, dropping each payload before the next.
  - **B:** per row:
    - the current state by `put`'s point lookup (Tiered as `put`);
    - the id total (`Limit(Ids)`); resident admission stays with `settle_draft` and uses AP15 and keyed credit;
    - the index plan as `put_impl` builds it, with both payloads dropped once it is planned;
