B pauses before fetching C20's MANIFEST. C completes its open at e + 1, advances its CLAIM at 21, cuts at 22 with `retain` 1 and reclaims C20 and its MANIFEST. B's fetch of that MANIFEST is NotFound, its witness GET sees C's head (e + 1, C's holder), and B returns `Superseded(C's pair)` without fetching C22's entry. **Lost witness:** B's fetch of C20's MANIFEST is NotFound because A itself cut C22 with `retain` 1 and reclaimed C20. B's witness GET sees A's pair at 22. Before B reads C22's entry, C claims, cuts C24 with `retain` 1 and reclaims C22, so that entry is NotFound. B's fresh head GET sees C's pair, and B returns `Superseded(C's pair)`. In both, the register history holds no head write by B, and C's next advance is Advanced. | register history | a claim that writes the head unconditionally, or conditions on the tag of a head other than the one it recovered and admitted; a loop that retries into a fresh claimant's epoch; a witness or rebase that adopts a head of another pair |
| **L53 a fenced holder never acks, and an idle one stops** | A advances, B claims, and A advances or polls. A gets `Fenced(eA)` and stays unhealthy, and no outstanding ticket of A returns `Ok`. In the register history, no head write after B's carries eA. **Idle:** with A's runner idle (an empty inbox), the first successful poll after B's replace sets health to `Fenced`, and the runner head ends abnormally with no clean report and no further reply. A failed poll before it changes nothing and is retried. **Comparison:** with an own advance in flight, a poll that sees A's own new bytes leaves A healthy. | register history; A's ticket results; the runner's end | a holder that conditions its head write on a fresh GET's tag ("refresh-then-CAS"); a poll that compares tags instead of (epoch, holder) (the in-flight case); a fence that never reaches an idle runner |
| **L54 Q5 resolution** | For each head write n of an advance, and for genesis, claim and an **activation**, the reply is lost with the request (a) applied, (b) dropped, (c) dropped and then overtaken by another holder's claim, (d) applied and then overtaken by another holder's claim, or (e) answered 503 then applied; or the bucket is unreachable for the whole budget. If the store says Advanced (or Claimed, or the install succeeded), the register history holds its exact bytes. In (a), (b) and (e) it says Advanced. In (c) and (d) it says `Fenced` (or `Superseded(actual)` naming the overtaking holder's pair, `Lost` for genesis, or an install's `Store(Fenced(e))`) and acks nothing outstanding. Under `Fenced` or `Undecided`, no outstanding ticket of the group is ever `Ok` for this open, and the overtaking claim's recovered history holds the group exactly when the register applied it ((d) yes, (c) no). For an activation in (d), the reconciliation (§12.7) reports installed and the host's selection becomes t. In (c) it reports not installed and keeps OLD's. **Witness cases (v2.48, Delta #3):** OLD's activation is 3 and the exported main head 9, so t = 10, and NEW's executable digest I differs from the attempt's PREPARED digest D. In (d) the reconciliation reads `releases[10]` with `prepared` = D and reports installed. A second attempt of the same image whose PREPARED differs (D′ ≠ D) and a standalone `Install` of the same executable, each landing at 10 instead, give `releases[10]` with digest I and `prepared` D′ or empty, and the reconciliation of the first attempt reports not installed. A head still at OLD's (epoch, holder) with no `releases[10]` reports unknown, and both roots stay. **Moved activation through a host restart (v2.49, Check #1; v2.55 Spec Q5):** OLD's and NEW's records run different code, so their identity digests id(OLD) and id(NEW) differ, except in (ii′); a standalone install "of NEW's code" runs an executable of NEW's code with `--hirsel-n-place=1048576`<!-- doc-ref: external -->, the records' allowance, so its binding is id(NEW). In each history below, OLD's activation head write is lost to its reply, then the host restarts, the standalone writer is stopped and the store is quiet. Its probe of NEW at `Current(10)` is refused `NotCurrent`, and its follower read of one capture decides. (i) D lands at 10 and a standalone `Install` of NEW's code lands at 11: the deploy is recorded Installed, the group serves NEW's assembly at 11 (never 10), and a collection keeps NEW's and OLD's assemblies. (ii) D is dropped, a standalone install of NEW's code takes 10 and another takes 11: the deploy is recorded failed (`releases[10].prepared` empty), the group serves NEW's assembly at 11, and a collection keeps NEW's and OLD's. (iii) D is dropped and a standalone install of NEW's code with another `n_place` takes 10: the deploy is recorded failed, no record of the group matches the head's binding, the group is failing with that cause, and a collection keeps both. (ii′) (v2.51, astra 1a; v2.55) OLD's and NEW's records share one identity, id(OLD) = id(NEW): two records of one executable whose recipes differ in a `Dir` binding (the same holds for one program assembled by Cranelift for one record and LLVM for the other). As (ii), with standalone installs of that code at 10 and 11: the read at 11 matches both, the deploy is recorded failed, so OLD's record serves at 11 and a collection removes NEW's (RUNNER §14.3 "What serves", "Roots"). As (i), with D at 10 and one install at 11: the outcome is Installed, so NEW's record serves at 11 with OLD retained. Installs at `PlaceConfig.n_place` (a bare `--hirsel-install`<!-- doc-ref: external -->): as (iii). With OLD and NEW one record, each history selects it at 11. With one standalone install only, at 10: the head is at 10 with binding id(NEW), so NEW's probe at `Current(10)` opens, finds `releases[10].prepared` empty, the deploy is recorded failed, and NEW's record, the one the probe opened, serves at 10 with OLD retained. **No-record recovery (v2.52, astra m2-v251-astra-1961 item 3; v2.53, astra m2-v252-astra-1965 items 1, 2 and 4; v2.54, astra m2-v253-astra-1967 items 1–4):** continue (ii′)'s bare history (one identity for OLD and NEW), with OLD's and NEW's records hosted at 1,048,576 bytes (`--hirsel-n-place=1048576`<!-- doc-ref: external -->) and the executable's `PlaceConfig.n_place` 524,288 bytes with `session` = `wire_defaults(65536, 524288)`, so the configured and hosted allowances differ, and a serving launch at 1,048,576 passes `session_problem` (peak 15,771,732 bytes against the 16,777,216-byte ceiling). The bare installs give no allowance, so they register and describe at 524,288 and their binding, id₅₂₄, is not id(OLD). The deploy is recorded failed with nothing selected; the group keeps OLD at 3, retains NEW, and carries the mark `Unmatched` (activation 11, id₅₂₄, 524,288); its cause is `No recovery candidate matches the store at activation 11: its release identity is <id₅₂₄-hex> at n_place 524288; candidates: <OLD-hex> with identity <id(OLD)-hex> at n_place 1048576, <NEW-hex> with identity <id(OLD)-hex> at n_place 1048576`, and stays so across retries refused at 3. Each retry reads 11 and id₅₂₄, matches neither and changes no selection. A retry that ends before any `PlaceCurrent` (exit 1 during recovery), and the same end recovered from the launcher's inventory after a host restart, leave `Status.failing[].last` as that cause followed by `; last start: exit status 1`. **A reported refusal across host loss (v2.54, item 3):** two histories from that mark, with the host down while generation g, launched at `Current(3)`, runs. In the first, g is refused `NotCurrent` at 11, its read fails (`Remote`), it sends `PlaceCurrent(11)` without a read and exits 1. In the second, g exits 1 during recovery before it sends anything. After the host restarts, the inventory lists g ended with exit status 1, launched at 3 as OLD's record, and in the first history only, the kept `PlaceCurrent(11)`, which the host applies before the end and before it sends `Acknowledge` for the end. `last` is the cause followed by `; last start: NotCurrent: the store is at activation 11; this start requested 3` in the first and `; last start: exit status 1` in the second; the mark, the selection and the catalog are equal in both. Then the operator runs, through the native entry point, `./place --hirsel-n-place=1048576 --hirsel-install`, which exits 0, registers and describes at 1,048,576 with binding id(OLD), takes 12 and closes, and the host restarts. The restart's start at `Current(3)` is refused, its read reports activation 12 and id(OLD), which both candidates match; the deploy is failed, so one transaction makes OLD current at 12 with index[12] = OLD and the mark `Adopted` at 12, leaving the deploy failed. The start's end relaunches at 12 at once. If that relaunch exits 1 before `PlaceOpened`, `last` is `exit status 1` alone (the `Adopted` mark has no cause) and the next start at 12 opens. **Back to `Unmatched` (v2.54, item 4):** if instead a bare `./place --hirsel-install` takes 13 before the relaunch opens, the relaunch at 12 is refused, its read at 13 matches neither candidate, the mark becomes `Unmatched` at 13 (id₅₂₄, 524,288) with OLD still selected at 12, OLD is the only candidate (the adoption applied "Roots" and dropped NEW), and `last` is `No recovery candidate matches the store at activation 13: its release identity is <id₅₂₄-hex> at n_place 524288; candidates: <OLD-hex> with identity <id(OLD)-hex> at n_place 1048576; last start: NotCurrent: the store is at activation 13; this start requested 12`. Otherwise the relaunch opens and serves at 12. In every branch the first accepted `PlaceOpened` clears the mark. A collection keeps OLD's record and removes NEW's (a failed deploy with OLD selected). Which record is adopted does not depend on how the install was launched, only on the identity it wrote and the deploy's outcome: here the deploy failed, so OLD (v2.55; v2.54's install named a record). - **Fixture.** Every case uses group commits of 1, no cut unless it names one, and `head_poll_ms` larger than the case's run time. Genesis is position 1 and the CLAIM is position 2, so commit i of the first holder is at position 2 + i.
- **Cases, not laws.** Each row is a case of the law it names, in the home it names. It is not a new law.
- **Runs.** Smoke runs 16 seeds within 15 s. Nightly runs 256.
- **Oracles.** Every expected value is hand-derived here or read from the sim. None is read from the store under test.

### 12.11 The Bucket host stream

The opt-in stream implementation includes streamed genesis and commits, attachment
and claims, re-election, pinning and collection, and the host janitor. It also
covers direct service after a refused cut, follower rounds over the stream, and
the export, backup and archival paths in §12.11.11.
The implementation lives in the `store-stream-*.hirsel` files. The
`bucket_stream_*laws.hirsel` files cover the shipped cases of L90. The L90 table
below specifies the full acceptance cases.

Ratified by Sam on 2026-11-26 (09:20 CET). The design history is outside the repo, in the research folder `hirsel-briefs/research-1126/shared-journal-batching/`: MOONSHOT-DESIGN (the first design), AMENDED-BUCKET-STREAM (the base protocol), ASTRA-SIGNOFF (cited "A1"–"A5") and FABLE-SIGNOFF (cited "M1"–"M12"), and FINAL-BUCKET-STREAM-BRIEF, which holds Sam's three rulings. Where those files and this section differ, this section is the contract. §12.11.16 maps every A and M item to the paragraph that closes it.

**What it is.** A host that opts in runs one **host stream**: one writer that packs the commit frames of every Place it serves into shared, create-only **batch** objects in the Places' bucket. It replaces each Place's two Class A writes per advance (entry and head) with one batch create shared by all of them, and each Place's idle head poll with one register read per batch. A Place stays a store of its own. It keeps its own `head`, its checkpoints, its packs, its cuts and its identity. The head references the stream tail; it never copies it.

**Scope.** objects@1, and sim@1 whose grant has no weak level (§12.11.1). log@1, memory@1 and a Disk stream are out of scope. A "batch" is one stream object, and "stream" here is never §1.8's stream position.

#### 12.11.0 Rulings, as applied

| Ruling | How this section applies it |
|---|---|
| **Zero cost when unused** | A program that never calls `journal_service` constructs nothing: no service, register, doorbell, poll or pin. An un-streamed Place writes the head bytes, keys and requests of v2.141 exactly, because ATTACH is a separate frame present only while a Place is attached and HEAD stays 136 bytes (law L90-Z0). `HEAD_OBJECT_LIMIT` and every holder's head buffers are unchanged, because a head with ATTACH still fits them (§12.11.2), so every Place plan is v2.141's. |
| **M2, the hold before H** (Sam, ruling 1) | A claimant of an **attached** Place writes one revocable `Held` row in the stream's register before its head replace H. A **standalone** Place keeps Q4 literally: its claim writes nothing before the replace (§12.3). The substance of Q4 holds for both: a claimant that refuses or crashes never writes H, and the incumbent resumes (§12.11.5, §12.11.6). |
| **No batching default** (Sam, ruling 2) | `StreamPlan.batching` is a required `Batching` value. The library has no default value, constructor or fallback for it. Every program that streams chooses its latency against its Class A cost (§12.11.1). |
| **Typed API** (Sam, ruling 3; Fable §4) | `platform.local`'s `Config.journal: Option[StreamPlan]`, and `store.streamed(a, slot)`, which takes the slot `journal_slot` returned. "Streamed without a journal" cannot be written. The stream reference in the head is the **attachment** (ATTACH), so HEAD's release `binding` keeps its name and bytes. |
| **Cut for good** | A Disk stream and `StreamPlan.Both`, headless genesis, claims across sleep, inline pointer frames, sharded streams, a public `settle`, `Backing.*.journal` and rewrite batches. A frame too large for the open batch closes it and goes into a batch of its own, because open checks that the Place’s recorded frame limit fits a one-row batch. |
| **Two exits** | A Place leaves the stream only by a **cut** (§12.2, "When a cut runs"), which consumes every tail into a checkpoint, or by a **close settle**, which writes the tail as GROUP entries and drops ATTACH (§12.11.11). Direct service after 8 sealed tails (§12.11.5 step 6) is not an exit: the Place stays attached until its cut. |

#### 12.11.1 Names and API

- **Host stream** S, named by `sid` (16 bytes). **Incarnation** `inc` (u64) is the stream's epoch, raised by each election (§12.11.7). **Holder** (16 bytes, `Random`) is the service process that holds `inc`. The service's identity is the pair (inc, holder).
- **Stream root.** Every stream object sits under `<root>/s-<sid>/`, where `root` is the deployment's `StreamPlan.prefix` in the Places' bucket. Every host and every reader of one deployment names the same root.

```hirsel
pub type Batching: cross { max_wait_ms: u64, max_batch_bytes: u64 }   // no default (Sam 2026-11-26); max_wait_ms 0 sends each batch as soon as the previous one is decided
pub type StreamLimits: cross {
    max_slots: u32, max_pins: u32, hold_ms: u64, idle_poll_ms: u64,
    index_every: u64, pin_ttl_s: u64, slot_bytes: u64 }
pub type HostStreamId: shareable + cross { hi: u64, lo: u64 }   // a stream's 16-byte id; never a Place's StoreId
pub type StreamPlan: cross { sid: HostStreamId, prefix: String, batching: Batching, limits: StreamLimits }
pub opaque type JournalService                                   // not send: holds the service task's handle
pub opaque type JournalSlot: cross                               // one Place's data connection client and its slot number
pub type StreamRoot: cross { prefix: String }
pub fn stream_service_bytes(plan: StreamPlan) -> u64
pub fn journal_service(tasks: Tasks, take a: Authority, plan: StreamPlan, budget: u64, c: Clock, r: Random) -> Result[JournalService, Refusal] waits
pub fn journal_slot(mut s: JournalService) -> Result[JournalSlot, Error] waits
pub fn streamed(take a: Authority, take slot: JournalSlot) -> Result[Authority, Error]   // a writer Authority whose opens attach
pub fn stream_reader(take a: Authority, root: StreamRoot) -> Result[Authority, Error]   // a read-only Authority (§12.11.9)
pub fn close_journal_service(take s: JournalService) -> Result[(), Error] waits
```

- **Platform.** `platform.local`'s `Config` gains `backing: PlaceBacking` (`DiskBacking` or `BucketBacking(LocalBucket)`) and `journal: Option[StreamPlan]`. `None` is v2.141's behavior, byte for byte: a `BucketBacking` host then starts each Place on its own standalone Bucket store under `<prefix>/<name>/`. `Some(plan)` on a `BucketBacking` host makes the actor start one `journal_service` and hand each Place start job a `JournalSlot` (a `cross` value), which the job passes to `streamed`. `Some(_)` on a `DiskBacking` host is refused `Configuration` (a Disk stream is out of scope, §12.11.0).
- **There is no default `Batching`.** `max_wait_ms` is the window in which the service gathers frames after the first one arrives (0: none). `max_batch_bytes` must fit a minimum-sized Store frame plus the encoded one-row batch envelope and be at most 2³². Before sending an attachment, the writer checks that its recorded frame limit plus that envelope fits. The envelope is HEADER, INDEX with one row, and FOOTER. Either bounds violation returns `Stream(Bound(MaxBatchBytes))`. The caller supplies `StreamLimits`.
- **max_rows is derived.** The register holds at most `max_rows = 2 × max_slots` rows. `max_slots` is 1 to 10,698, so `max_rows × 49 + 110 ≤ REG_LIMIT` (1 MiB). A value outside is `Stream(Bound(MaxSlots))`. There is no separate `max_rows` setting (M8).
- **Refusals before any request (M12).** Each is typed and writes nothing:
  - `journal_service`: a `prefix` over 1,024 bytes is `Limit(Name)`; `Stream(Bound(field))` for a limit outside its range (`HoldMs`: `hold_ms` ≥ 4 × the authority's `op_ms`; `IdlePollMs`: 1 ≤ `idle_poll_ms` ≤ `hold_ms`; `IndexEvery` ≥ 1; `SlotBytes` ≥ 4,096; `MaxPins` ≥ 2; and the two above). The `sid` is typed, so it has no length refusal, and any value, zero included, names a stream; a budget below the service's fixed part plus `max_slots` slot charges (§12.11.12) is `Full(Allocation(c))`; an authority that is not objects@1 or sim@1 is `Unsupported(authority)`; sim@1 with a weak level is `Stream(WeakLevels)` (M7).
  - `journal_slot`: `Full(Slots(c))` when every ordinary slot is taken (one slot is the janitor's, §12.11.8); `Full(Pins(c))` at `max_pins` pins.
  - `streamed`: `Foreign` unless the Authority's endpoint, region and bucket are the service's; `Stream(Overlap)` when the Place's `prefix` and the stream root overlap (one is a prefix of the other at a `/` boundary, or they are equal), so the stream's keys are never inside a Place prefix (genesis's LIST would refuse them, §12.3) and no Place key is inside the stream root; `Stream(WeakLevels)` for a sim@1 grant with a weak level.
- **These refusals are configuration errors.** `streamed`'s `Foreign`, `Stream(Overlap)` and `Stream(WeakLevels)`, and `stream_reader`'s `Unsupported(authority)`, `Stream(Overlap)` (the Authority's Place prefix against the root) and `Stream(WeakLevels)`, are fixed only by changing the Config, so both consume the Authority and the slot and return a bare `Error`, unlike `open`'s `Refusal` (v2.70 D1), which hands the Authority back for a retry. **A dropped slot is freed:** when a `JournalSlot` is dropped unused, or the Db holding it is dropped or closed, its data connection closes and the service returns the slot to the free set; its pin stays until the release rule clears it.
- **A streamed open** is an ordinary writer `open` (§12.3) through the Authority `streamed` returned. It attaches the Place: genesis (§12.11.5, "Streamed genesis") or a claim (§12.11.5). Its commits go to its slot, and the service acks them (§12.11.4).

**Changed types.**

```hirsel
pub type StoreCapacity = … | Slots(Capacity) | Pins(Capacity) | Register(Capacity)   // gains three cases; every earlier case (§11.16, §13.3's Cache) stands
pub type StreamField = MaxBatchBytes | MaxSlots | MaxPins | HoldMs | IdlePollMs | IndexEvery | SlotBytes
pub type StreamRefusal = WeakLevels | Overlap | Bound(StreamField)
pub type StreamLatch = Superseded | Batch | Register | Unreachable
pub type Error = … | Attached(Option[HostStreamId]) | Stream(StreamRefusal) | Latched(StreamLatch) | …   // Attached: a non-streamed opener found ATTACH; the value is `live`'s sid, or None under direct service. Latched: the Place's host stream latched (§12.11.10)
pub type Why = … | Regressed                                                   // a register body with a lower rev than one already seen
pub type Health = Ok(u32) | Fenced(u64) | Undecided | Poisoned(IoError) | Remote(std.object.Error) | Latched(StreamLatch)
```

#### 12.11.2 Objects and frames

**Stream objects** extend §12.2's names. Each is a file in the store's current format word (§11.1 AP1) whose HEADER carries the Place authority's `authority` value, identity = `sid`, the role below, `seq` as below and `epoch` = the writing incarnation's `inc`. Numbers are decimal, zero-padded to 20 digits, as in §12.2.

| Key under `<root>/s-<sid>/` | Role | Write rule | Body |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reg` | 11 REGISTER | Created once with `Absent`, then only `If-Match`. Never deleted or recreated. A 404 after the stream's creation is `Corrupt(Fault{file: reg, offset: 0, why: Absent})`, which latches the stream (§12.11.10). | HEADER(seq 0) ‖ REG |
| `b-<inc>-<seq>` | 12 BATCH | Create-only (`If-None-Match: *`). A 412 is resolved by one GET: exact bytes are Applied; a TERM body is the terminal fence (§12.11.7), and the writer latches `Superseded`; any other bytes are `Corrupt(Fault{file, 0, Malformed})` and latch `Batch`. | HEADER(seq) ‖ INDEX ‖ the frames ‖ FOOTER, or HEADER(seq) ‖ TERM |
| `x-<k>` | 13 XINDEX | Create-only, with the batch 412 rule (no TERM). `k` rises across incarnations. | HEADER(seq k) ‖ XINDEX |
| `probe` | 14 PROBE | Created once, with `Absent`, before `reg`. Never written with other bytes. | HEADER(seq 0) only |

**Frames** (new kinds under §2.7's rule 1; the reviewed numbers are kept, so 0x0102 is TERM):

| Frame | Kind | MUST | Limit | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ATTACH | 0x0100 | 1 | 512 | `settles u64`; `live` (a u8 tag 0/1, then `sid [16] ‖ inc u64 ‖ from_seq u64 ‖ from_frame u32`); `count u8` (0–8), then `count` sealed entries `sid [16] ‖ inc u64 ‖ from_seq u64 ‖ from_frame u32 ‖ cutoff u64 ‖ at u64` (52 B). At most 8 + 37 + 1 + 416 = 462 bytes. |
| INDEX | 0x0101 | 1 | **727,480** = 4 + 8 + 4 + 68 × 10,698 | `byte_len u32 ‖ seen_rev u64 ‖ count u32`, then `count` rows `store [16] ‖ epoch u64 ‖ offset u32 ‖ len u32 ‖ frames u32 ‖ digest [32]` (68 B), one per Place with frames in the batch, ascending by `store` |
| TERM | 0x0102 | 1 | 32 | `sid [16] ‖ inc u64 ‖ seq u64`: the terminal fence of incarnation `inc` at `seq` |
| REG | 0x0103 | 1 | **`REG_LIMIT` = 1,048,576** | the register (below) |
| XINDEX | 0x0104 | 1 | 16,777,216 | for each (store, epoch) with rows in `[low, covers_through]`, the batch seqs that hold its frames; then the pins in force when it was written (§12.11.8) |
| FOOTER | 0x0105 | 1 | 32 | `body_digest [32]`, SHA-256 over HEADER through the last frame before FOOTER |

- **ATTACH** is the frame after AUTHORITY in `head`, present only while the Place is attached. `live` names the stream that holds the Place's current tail, from the position `(from_seq, from_frame)`: frame index `from_frame` of the Place's slice in batch `from_seq` (M4). Each `sealed` entry is an earlier tail that a claim froze: the Place's frames of `(sid, inc)` from `(from_seq, from_frame)` through the end of its slice in batch `cutoff`, which are immutable. `at` is the entry position at which the tail was frozen. `settles` rises by 1 on every settle head write (§12.11.6), so two settles never write the same head body (M1). ATTACH rules, each `Corrupt(Malformed)` otherwise: `sealed` is in non-decreasing `at` order, each `at` ≤ HEAD `position`; each sealed entry has `cutoff ≥ from_seq`; `count ≤ 8`. That a sealed entry with `cutoff = from_seq` has a frame at `from_frame` or later in its slice is not a head check: the tail read checks it when it reads that slice, and a slice with fewer frames is `Corrupt(Fault{file, 0, Malformed})`.
- **A non-streamed opener refuses an attached head.** A writer, genesis, import or export whose Authority is not from `streamed`, that reads a head carrying ATTACH, returns `Attached(live)` (`live`'s sid, or `None` under direct service) before any write (§12.1). A follower, `open_read_only`, scrub or verify without a stream root returns the same; with one, it reads the tails (§12.11.9).
- **`HEAD_OBJECT_LIMIT` stays 65,776.** It bounds the head object. AUTHORITY's payload is at most 1 + 2,050 + 66 + 65 + 1,026 + 1 + 16 × 67 = 4,281 bytes (§12.2's field limits; leftover bytes are `Corrupt(Malformed)`), so a head is at most 72 + 16 + 136 + 16 + 4,281 = 4,521 bytes, and with a full ATTACH (16 + 462) at most **4,999**. No head buffer grows on any holder or follower, streamed or not, and every Place plan is v2.141's. AUTHORITY's 65,536-byte frame limit is never reached, and ATTACH fits in the room it leaves.
- **INDEX's limit is a constant** (727,480: the largest `max_slots`, 10,698, times 68, plus INDEX's 16-byte head), so every reader accepts every writer's batch. `max_slots` bounds only what a writer writes. A claimant applies its own `max_rows` when it adds a hold to a foreign register; that is harmless, because every register buffer is `REG_LIMIT` + 88 and every reader checks a body against `REG_LIMIT`, never against `max_rows`.
- **A Place's frames in a batch are sealed under the Place's own context.** Each frame in a slice is sealed as §2.7 seals a frame, with `DiskContext(store: the Place's store, role: BATCH, seq: the batch's seq)` at the frame's byte offset within its slice. The Place sends its frames unsealed over its slot; the service seals them when it packs the batch, so a frame moved to another slice or batch fails its check.
- **INDEX** is the first frame after HEADER. A reader range-GETs the first 4 KiB, which holds HEADER, INDEX's head and its first 58 rows, and issues a second range GET only when `byte_len` says INDEX is longer. A full read checks FOOTER's `body_digest`; a slice read checks its row's `digest` (SHA-256 of the slice).
- **REG**:
  ```
  rev u64                   every applied write sets the read rev + 1
  sid [16], inc u64, holder [16]
  kind u8                   0 Serving, 1 Collecting (a janitor's GC-only incarnation, §12.11.7)
  low: (inc u64, seq u64)   batches below low may be deleted; it never falls
  index: u8 tag, then { k u64, len u64, digest u64 (xxh3-64), covers_through: (inc u64, seq u64) }
  count u32, then count rows { store [16], epoch u64, token [16], rev_hold u64, state u8 (0 Held, 1 Abandoned) }   49 B each
  ```
  The fixed part is 110 bytes. A REG write is valid only if `rev` is the read rev + 1 and none of `inc`, `low` or `index.k` falls; a reader checks it. REG is MUST = 1 because its limit is over `UNKNOWN_LIMIT` (§2.7 rule 3, M8).

#### 12.11.3 The provider contract, extended to the register

§12.2's provider contract also names `reg` in items 1–3 (a linearizable conditional PUT and GET, and a non-recurring validator), and batch, TERM, XINDEX and `probe` objects in item 4. Item 5 is unchanged. These rules are added:
1. **Rising rev.** A reader that has seen rev r refuses a body with a lower rev as `Corrupt(Fault{file: reg, 0, Regressed})`. It is the client's guard against an old body seen again.
2. **No 304 evidence.** The client sends only unconditional GETs of `reg`. A 304, or a response whose body and tag do not come from one response, is a failed read. A failed or cached read, a cached 404 included, decides nothing and permits no ack. The stream uses the Places' endpoint under §12.2's endpoint rules.
3. **Q5 on the register, with merge.** `Applied`: done. `Uncertain`: resend the same bytes with the same `If-Match`. `Mismatch`: GET `reg`; exact bytes are done; the intent already present is done (a hold: its own token is there with the `rev_hold` stored; a removal: the tokens are gone); otherwise rebuild from the new body and retry within the budget. A rebuild only adds or edits the writer's own rows, removes the rows the writer is entitled to remove (§12.11.6, with M1's fixed set), or raises `low` and `index` when the new body's values are still lower. It never drops a row the writer did not remove by right.
4. **Concurrent rows never overwrite each other.** Two claimants of one (Place, epoch) each add their own token, and both rows stand.
5. **Bounded.** A hold that would pass `max_rows` refuses `Full(Register(c))` with nothing written, and the claim returns it. A claim never elects (§12.11.7).
6. **Rotating the incarnation reauthorizes nothing.** A service whose register read shows another (inc, holder) latches `Superseded` for good (§12.11.10).
7. **Probes on an immutable key (M12).** At stream creation the service creates `probe` with `Absent`, then `reg` with `Absent`. At every election, before its CAS, it sends `probe`'s exact bytes to `probe` twice: with `If-None-Match: *`, and with `If-Match` on a tag no object carries (`"hirsel-store-condition-probe"`). Both must be refused (412, or the provider's 304), else `Endpoint(IgnoresIfNoneMatch)` or `Endpoint(IgnoresIfMatch)`. `probe` is immutable, so an endpoint that ignores the condition rewrites identical bytes. A streamed genesis on that endpoint skips §12.3's step 5a, because the service probed this endpoint.

#### 12.11.4 Writer cycle and the ack rule

The service is strictly sequential, with at most one batch create outstanding, so `seen_rev` never falls as `seq` rises.

```
loop:
  gather slot frames until max_wait_ms passes after the first, or max_batch_bytes is reached
      (a stalled or latched Place contributes nothing)
  seen_rev := the rev of the last successful register GET
  CREATE b-<inc>-<seq>        (Q5: Uncertain → resend exactly; 412 → GET and §12.11.2's rule; budget gone → latch)
  GET reg, issued after the create completed        -- 1 Class B per batch
  decide the batch; seq += 1
```

**The ack rule.** After batch n's create is Applied, the service acks X's frames in n only when a register body R satisfies all of:
- R comes from a GET issued after n's create completed, or is the Applied result of the service's own CAS issued after then;
- `R.inc` and `R.holder` are the service's own;
- R holds no row (Held or Abandoned) for (X, e_X), where e_X is the epoch at which the service serves X;
- every earlier batch is decided, and X is not latched.

A response authorizes only batches whose create completed before its request was issued. A delayed or failed response never unlatches anything.

**The second authority: a sealed cutoff.** When X's head shows an epoch above e_X and `sealed` holds (S, inc, …, cutoff k), X's outstanding frames in batches ≤ k end `Ok`, and those in batches > k end `Fenced`. **Missing evidence (A3).** When X's head shows an epoch above e_X and no sealed entry for (S, inc), because a cut consumed it before A observed it, A cannot learn k, and X's outstanding frames end `Undecided`; the next claim's head decides whether they are in the history, exactly as for an `Undecided` advance (§12.3). No other evidence decides an X frame.

**Stall.** A row for (X, e_X) stalls X: its frames in unacked batches stay outstanding; X goes into no later batch and its new commits wait in its slot; no cut of X starts; X's head task GETs X's head every `hold_ms / 4` and reports each result to the service (§12.11.12). §12.11.6 says how X resumes.

**Lemma 1 (an acked frame lies under every cutoff).** If a hold for (X, e) applies at rev h, and its H later applies, then every batch whose X frames were acked at epoch e by a register body has `seen_rev < h`, and its create completed before h applied. *Proof.* Let R_n ack batch n. If R_n linearizes after h, the row was removed first, by a rule of §12.11.6, and none lets this hold's H apply afterwards: (a) the service's Applied settle changed the head body (it raised `settles`), so H's `Match` fails; (b, e) a row is Abandoned only when its claimant will never send H for it; (c) the service already saw X at a higher epoch and latched X; (d) the old incarnation acks nothing more; (f) X's head no longer names (S, inc) as `live`, so the head bytes H matched are gone. M1's fixed set means no token added after the settle's head write is issued is removed by (a) or (b). So R_n precedes h, and `seen_rev(n) = rev(R_{n−1}) ≤ rev(R_n) < h`. ∎

#### 12.11.5 Claim of an attached Place (Q4 as amended for attached Places)

This replaces §12.3's claim steps 3–5 for a Place X whose head carries ATTACH. Standalone Places keep §12.3 unchanged. The cases:
- `live = (S_A, inc_A, from)` and `inc_A` equals S_A's current register inc, with `kind` Serving: steps 1–7 below.
- `inc_A` below the register's inc: the old incarnation never acks again. Use §12.11.7's **no-hold rule**, which skips steps 3 and 4.
- No ATTACH (a standalone head opened through `streamed`): §12.3's claim, unchanged, and its replace writes ATTACH{`settles` 0, `live := (S_B, inc_B, (next seq, 0))`, `sealed := []`}.
- `live = None` (direct service, step 6): §12.3's claim with no hold. The CLAIM is an entry, ATTACH is copied, and the open-time cut is forced.

The claimant keeps the **settled part** (the history up to the live tail, §12.11.9) and the **overlay** (the live tail applied copy-on-write over it). They are never merged before step 6.

1. **GET head.** §12.3 steps 1–2 unchanged: the pair check, §12.1's checks and the ClaimAuth check (§12.3 "ClaimAuth", v2.166), all before the hold. The claim's pair (e, holder) is fixed.
2. **Private recovery and pre-scan.** Recover the settled part in history order (§12.11.9). Build the overlay from the live tail: GET `reg`, read `x-<k>` when `covers_through ≥ from`, then the INDEX of each later batch, until the first batch §12.11.8's 404 rule calls *not yet created*, or earlier when half of `o.claim_ms` runs out (only the delta needs a bound). **Admit** both against `resident_limit` (AP15), and **reserve** §12.9's fixed buffers here, before the hold; an allocator refusal is `Full(Allocation(c))`, returned with nothing written.
3. **Hold.** CAS `reg` to add `{X, e, token: Random, rev_hold: rev + 1, Held}`, with §12.11.3's merge. `Full(Register(c))` returns with nothing written. If the merge finds `inc` above `inc_A`, write no row and switch to the no-hold rule.
4. **Delta scan and admission.** From where step 2 stopped, include batch m while it is present and `seen_rev(m) < rev_hold`; stop at the first batch absent or with `seen_rev ≥ rev_hold`. **k** is the last batch included. *Bound:* with D the batches present when the hold applied and not yet scanned, the delta is at most D + 1 batches: at most one batch with `seen_rev < rev_hold` completes its create after the hold applies. Apply X's slices to the overlay and **re-admit**. **On any failure** (`Full(Resident(c))`, `Corrupt`, `Remote`) mark the row `Abandoned` (rule e) and return the failure. Nothing was fenced, and the incumbent unholds (§12.11.6 b) and keeps serving. **The same holds for every fallible step after the hold and before H's send (v2.166, O2a):** building the new `sealed` list, the next ATTACH, the claimed head with its ORIGIN, the authority span and the encoded body all run while the claimant still owns the hold token, and a failure among them abandons the row and then returns the failure. H's own send is outside that handler (step 6). An abandon whose request fails is only attempted: the row then ages to `hold_ms` and the service or janitor removes it.
5. **Final head GET.** Another pair: abandon the row, `Superseded(actual)` for a validated successor (§12.3 "ClaimAuth"; `Lost` only for a head that is not this Store's). The claim's pair at another position or with other ATTACH bytes (the incumbent advanced, settled or cut): abandon the row, discard the overlay, catch the settled part up from the new head, or rebase when its checkpoint or `sealed` changed, and re-dispatch among the cases above; a new hold has a new token, each repeat bounded by `o.claim_ms`. Exactly step 1's bytes: go on with tag t.
6. **H** with `Match(t)` writes HEAD{e + 1, holder, every other field copied}, ORIGIN{e + 1, the auth's attempt and class} (§12.3 "ORIGIN") and ATTACH{`settles` copied, `sealed := old.sealed ++ (S_A, inc_A, from, cutoff k, at p_A)`, `live := (S_B, inc_B, (S_B's next seq, 0))`}. It is the one authoritative publication; the tail is referenced, never copied, and nothing beyond k is published. Q5 resolves it as §12.3 step 5 does; a Mismatch at the claim's pair goes to step 5's second case. **No empty tail is sealed** (Fable §3): when X has no frame of `(S_A, inc_A)` at or after `from` up to k, H appends nothing to `sealed`. **Sealed overflow:** H still appends the incumbent's tail, because its acked frames are in no other place; when that append leaves `sealed` with 8 entries, H writes `live := None` instead of `(S_B, …)`. So `sealed` holds 0–8 entries, 8 only with `live` None, and ATTACH's 462-byte bound (8 + 37 + 1 + 8 × 52) bounds every head. With `live` None, B serves X **direct**, with commits as entries through X's head task as in §12.3, and the forced open-time cut consumes `sealed`; that cut's head write sets `live := (S_B, inc_B, (next seq, 0))` and `sealed := []`.
7. **The CLAIM rides S_B** (as an entry when `live` is None) as X's first frame there. `open` returns once it is acked; `Fenced` makes `open` return `Lost`. The open-time cut is forced when `sealed` names a stream other than S_B, or when `sealed` has 4 or more entries. A sealed tail of S_B's own earlier incarnation does not force it, because S_B's release rule clears that pin itself (§12.11.8). A refused cut does not fail the open (AP16).

**Q4 for attached Places (M2, Sam's ruling 1).** A claimant of an attached Place writes exactly one thing before H: its revocable `Held` row. It never writes H after a refusal: steps 2 and 4 both admit before H, so a claimant that cannot serve the head is refused with no head byte written, and **a healthy incumbent is never deposed by a claimant that turns out unable to serve it**. The residual is stated: a claimant that fails admission or crashes after its hold pauses that one Place's acks (its other Places are unaffected). On a refusal the incumbent resumes by rule (b) once it reads the Abandoned row. On a crash it resumes by rule (a) after up to `hold_ms` (about 2 s), at the cost of one settle head write.

**Lemma 2.** If H applies, the claimant's state holds every frame acked for (X, e), and every frame for (X, e) acked afterwards (by the sealed cutoff) is in it. *Proof.* By Lemma 1 every frame acked before the hold lies in a batch with `seen_rev < rev_hold` that completed before the hold; `seen_rev` is monotone in seq, so such a batch has seq ≤ k; the release rule (§12.11.8) deletes no batch X's head still contains, so the scan read it, or the 404 rule restarted the attempt. A batch above k was absent at the scan or has `seen_rev ≥ rev_hold`, so its X frames were never acked. ∎

**Ticket outcome at A.** A's stall poll shows epoch > e with `sealed ∋ (S_A, inc_A, …, cutoff k)`: frames in batches ≤ k end `Ok`, those above end `Fenced`, for good (`sealed` is copied by every later claim until a cut consumes it). With no such sealed entry, they end `Undecided` (§12.11.4). A latches X in memory and removes its rows for (X, e₀ ≤ e) by rule (c).

**Streamed genesis.** §12.3's genesis with three changes: step 5a is skipped when the service probed this endpoint (§12.11.3 rule 7); step 6 creates `head` with `Absent` and ATTACH{`settles` 0, `live := (S, inc, (next seq, 0))`, `sealed := []`}; step 7's CLAIM is X's first frame in S, and `open` returns once it is acked. That is 4 Class A: LIST, MANIFEST, entry 1, head. A crash before the CLAIM is acked leaves a head whose tail is empty, which a later claim reads as §12.3 reads a head with no CLAIM.

#### 12.11.6 Unhold, and who may remove a row

The service unholds X at epoch e in one of two ways.
- **(b) Every row for (X, e) is Abandoned.** One CAS removes exactly the tokens of the register body that showed every row Abandoned. Its Applied result is the R that acks X's stalled batches (§12.11.4), and X resumes.
- **(a) The oldest Held row for (X, e) was first observed `hold_ms` ago** on the service's monotonic clock (liveness only).
  1. The service asks X's head task (§12.11.12) for a **settle**: GROUP entries carrying X's live tail from `live.from`, stalled frames included, each entry's head write moving `live.from` past exactly the frames that entry holds and raising `settles` by 1. With an empty tail it is one head write that changes only `settles`. It runs even when `sealed` is non-empty (the entries come after the sealed tails in history order, §12.11.9), except under archival (§12.11.11). It is never a cut, so a refused cut cannot block it.
  2. Once its last head write has Applied, CAS the register to remove the **fixed set**: the tokens for (X, e) in a register body whose GET completed before the settle's first head write was issued.
  3. The Applied result of that CAS is the R that acks the stalled tickets, provided it holds no row for (X, e); otherwise X stays stalled.

  If the settle gets Mismatch and then the head shows another pair, a claimant's H won: end the tickets as in §12.11.5 and remove by (c). If the settle applied, any H in flight gets Mismatch and its claimant follows §12.11.5 step 5.

**The orphan-row head poll (A2).** A row for (X, e) on a Place the service does not serve at epoch e makes the service GET X's head on its read lane every `idle_poll_ms` until a rule removes the row: (c) once the head shows an epoch above e, (f) once it shows epoch e with `live` not naming (S, inc), or the janitor's close below. Like a follower's GET it decides no advance. It is the poll that applies (f) after A has closed X and so serves it no more.

**A Held row with no head task (A4).** When X has no connected head task (a close whose cut was refused, or a Db dropped without close, while the service lives) and the orphan-row poll shows epoch e with `live` naming (S, inc), no settle can run for rule (a). The host's janitor then opens X streamed through the reserved slot (§12.11.8) and closes it, once the oldest Held row for (X, e) was first observed `hold_ms` ago on the service's monotonic clock. The janitor's open is a claim of X at epoch e: its own H raises the epoch, and rule (c) then removes every row for (X, e), the janitor's own included. **Binding (v2.166).** The janitor's ask carries the StoreId and the head pair (e, holder) the service observed; its open sets `expect` to that StoreId and `ClaimAuth(expect = that pair, a fresh attempt, Continue)`. So a Place that moved to another host is refused `Superseded(actual)` with no write to X's head and no `Held` row on any stream, and a different Store at the prefix is refused `Foreign`. Just before the open the janitor rechecks the ask's cause on its own service (the Held row, or the pin, is still there); a cause already gone ends the ask `JanitorCleaned` with zero writes, distinct from `JanitorClosed`. The host drops a stale ask. A row's `first_seen + hold_ms` deadline arms one poll; once that deadline is past, the row waits at the idle cadence, so a past deadline never re-arms the service at the same instant. So every Held row on a Place whose head names this service as `live` is gone within `idle_poll_ms` (the register poll that first shows it) + `hold_ms` + one claim (at most `o.claim_ms` of the janitor's open), while the service lives. With `idle_poll_ms ≤ hold_ms` (§12.11.1) and the janitor's `o.claim_ms` below `2 × hold_ms`, that is under another host's `4 × hold_ms` election age (§12.11.8). A janitor open slower than that is the availability residual §12.11.8 states, never a safety loss.

**The fixed set (M1).** Under (a) and (b) the service removes only the tokens it observed in that one completed GET. On a merge retry it never removes a newer token, and a settle whose head write did not apply removes no row.

**Removal rules.** Only these remove a row:
- **(a)** the service, after its own Applied settle of X's head, the fixed set only;
- **(b)** the service, when every observed row is Abandoned, the fixed set only;
- **(c)** the service, for (X, e₀), after it observed X's head at an epoch above e₀ and latched X;
- **(d)** an election (§12.11.7), which ends the old incarnation;
- **(e)** a claimant, which only marks its *own* row Abandoned, and only when it will never send H for it: before sending H, or after H resolved as Mismatch. A claimant whose H is Undecided never abandons its row;
- **(f)** the service, for (X, e), once it has observed X's head at epoch e with `live` not naming (S, inc): X closed or was cut and settled away from S, so the head bytes any claimant's H could match are gone (A2, M1).

No claimant, janitor or reader removes another's row.

| Event | State left | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| B crashes after its hold, before H | Held row; head unchanged | A unholds by (a) after `hold_ms`. |
| B refuses at step 2 or 4 | Abandoned row | A unholds by (b). |
| B crashes after H, before its CLAIM is acked | Head at e + 1; S_A's tail sealed at k | The next claimant copies `sealed`. A ends its tickets. Nothing is applied twice. |
| H is Undecided | As §12.3 step 5 | `open` returns `Undecided`; the row stays Held; A's (a) settle applies (H lost) or is fenced (H won). |
| A closes X after B's pre-scan; B's hold lands; B crashes | Held row; X's head has no ATTACH | A removes it by (f) at its orphan-row head poll (above). |
| A's close of X had its cut refused, or X's Db was dropped; B's hold lands; B crashes | Held row; X's head still names (S, inc) as `live`; no head task | A's janitor opens and closes X once the row is `hold_ms` old; its H raises the epoch and A removes the rows by (c). |
| A's settle Applied, removal CAS lost | Rows remain | A retries the fixed set (§12.11.3 rule 3). B's H already failed. |
| B and C claim at epoch e | Two rows | At most one H applies at tag t. The loser abandons its row. |

#### 12.11.7 Election, incarnations and the terminal fence

**Election** (service start, on the configured `sid`):
1. GET `reg` (at stream creation: create `probe` and `reg`).
2. Run §12.11.3's probes.
3. CAS `{rev + 1, inc + 1, holder: Random, kind: Serving, low, index, rows: []}`, with `low` and `index` copied from the body read at step 1. **On Mismatch** the elector GETs `reg` and goes on only if the fresh body still has the incarnation it read at step 1 and still meets its precondition (for a janitor, §12.11.8's trigger); otherwise it stops and elects nothing (A4). It never rebuilds an election over a fresh winner.
4. **Terminal fence (A5).** Before its first batch, ack or `low` move, the new incarnation fences the old one: starting at the old incarnation's first seq not known to exist, it creates `b-<old_inc>-<term>` with the TERM body `{sid, old_inc, term}` (`If-None-Match: *`). A 412 whose GET shows a batch means a late batch of the old incarnation landed: `term += 1` and repeat. A 412 showing the same TERM bytes is done (another fencer wrote it). The fence is the old incarnation's durable end: no batch at or above `term` can ever be created, so pin rebuild and every no-hold claimant see one terminal sequence.
5. Rebuild the old incarnation's pins from durable state (§12.11.8) before the first `low` move.

**The zombie.** The old process's next register read shows another (inc, holder), and it latches `Superseded` (§12.11.10). Its batch create at or above the fence gets 412 with TERM bytes and latches `Superseded`. By Lemma 1 with h = the election's rev, every frame it acked lies in a batch that completed before the election.

**After `Superseded` (M9).** The service serves no more Places on that sid. If its owner reopens Places in the same process, the service draws a fresh `sid` (`Random`), creates that stream and serves them on it. The next process start uses the configured `sid` again and elects on it.

**The no-hold rule.** A claim of X whose `live.inc` is below the register's inc skips the hold and delta. Its cutoff k is the last batch of `live.inc` below the terminal fence. If the claimant finds no TERM where it meets the first 404, it creates it there itself (step 4's loop). So it never takes a cutoff the fence does not also bound. It is sound because a frame the zombie acked lies in a batch completed before the election, so below the fence; a zombie batch can land only below the fence, and then the claimant's scan, which runs to the fence, reads it; and the rows the election cleared belonged to an incarnation that can never ack again.

**Claims never elect (A4).** A claimant whose hold meets `Full(Register(c))` returns it. Only a host's janitor elects on another host's stream (§12.11.8), and only on its trigger. A service never re-elects after `Superseded`; only a latch caused by its own uncertainty re-elects, on its own sid.

#### 12.11.8 Retirement, GC and the janitor

**Invariants.** `low` only rises. A batch, TERM or XINDEX object is deleted only after the register CAS that raised `low` above it has Applied. `(inc, seq)` and `k` only rise, so names are never reused. **Containment:** batch (sid, inc_b, seq_b) lies in a `sealed` entry when that entry has the same sid and inc and `from_seq ≤ seq_b ≤ cutoff`, and in a `live` ref when it has the same sid and inc and `from_seq ≤ seq_b`.

**The release rule.** `low` passes batch b only once every Place with an INDEX row in b has a head, observed after the row was written, in which neither `live` nor any `sealed` entry contains b. For its own attached Places the service uses the head summary each Place last reported (§12.11.12).

**Pins come from durable state.** INDEX rows and XINDEX lists record which Places have frames in which batches. A Place attached with no frame yet pins nothing. After an election the new incarnation rebuilds the pins of `[low, the terminal fence)` before its first `low` move, reading `x-<k>`, then the INDEX of every old-incarnation batch past `covers_through` up to the fence. For a Place whose state is not in memory (sealed-pending, or held by the old incarnation), the service GETs its head on its own read lane every `idle_poll_ms` until the release rule holds. Like a follower's GET, it never decides an advance; it does apply rules (c) and (f). It is a different trigger from §12.11.6's orphan-row poll, which runs while a row stands even when the release rule already holds; one GET serves both when both are due.

**Index checkpoint**, every `index_every` batches: create `x-<k+1>`; CAS `reg` with the new `index`, `low` at the highest seq the release rule allows, and the rows rules (c) and (f) drop; then delete the objects below the new `low`. 2 Class A.

**A 404 is never an end of stream by itself.** On a 404 for batch (inc, s), the reader GETs `reg` and then X's head, both issued after the 404:

| Case | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `(inc, s) < low`, head unchanged | Retired, empty for X | Skip to `low`; use XINDEX or INDEX to find X's next batch. |
| `(inc, s) < low`, head changed | Retired; the history moved | Restart the whole attempt from the new head. |
| `(inc, s) ≥ low`, and `≤ covers_through`, or in a sealed range, or below a batch already seen present | Possibly a create that raced the first GET (A5) | **Re-GET the batch once.** Present: continue normally. Still 404: `Corrupt(Fault{file, 0, Absent})`. |
| `(inc, s)` at or above a TERM of `inc` | The incarnation's end | Stop: no batch exists there. |
| otherwise: `inc` is the live ref's inc and `s` is above every seq known | Not yet created | A valid stop for §12.11.5 steps 2 and 4, the no-hold rule (which then fences, §12.11.7) and followers (§12.11.9) only. |

**Forced settle of a straggler (M9).** A pin older than `pin_ttl_s`, or any pin once the count reaches `max_pins`, is cleared by the host's janitor **only when X's head names the janitor's own stream as `live`**: it opens X streamed through the reserved slot (a claim with the open-time cut forced, bound to the observed StoreId and pair as §12.11.6's janitor binding says) and closes it, which settles. When another stream is `live`, that host's forced open-time cut owns the pin, and `Full(Pins(c))` is the backpressure. The janitor also opens and closes X, through the same reserved slot, for §12.11.6's Held row with no head task, after `hold_ms` rather than `pin_ttl_s`. **Headroom (A5):** one slot and its pin are reserved for the janitor, so `journal_slot` never gives them out and `max_pins` never refuses the janitor's own open. **Its charge:** only that slot and pin are part of the service's budget. The janitor's open of X is an ordinary Place open on its host, with the Place plan §12.9 and §12.11.12 give any streamed open, charged to the host's Place budget like any start and refusable there (`Full(Allocation(c))`, after which the janitor retries at its next trigger).

**Dead and collecting streams (M9).** A host's janitor may elect on another stream S′ under the deployment's root, as a **Collecting** incarnation (`kind` 1) that serves no Place, writes no batch and acks nothing, only when:
- it holds, or has just cut, a Place whose head names S′ in `live` or `sealed`, so S′ holds a pin it needs cleared; and
- S′ is Serving and a row on it has carried the same token for at least `4 × hold_ms`, as seen by GETs of `S′/reg` every `idle_poll_ms` while the janitor's host holds such a Place, measured from the janitor's first observation of that token on its own monotonic clock (a live service removes an Abandoned row at once and a Held one within `idle_poll_ms + hold_ms` plus one claim, §12.11.6), or S′ is Collecting and its `rev` has been unchanged for at least `4 × hold_ms` from first observation.

The Collecting incarnation fences, rebuilds pins, then raises `low` and deletes as the release rule allows. Once every batch is gone only `probe` and `reg` remain. Rule (d) makes the election safe. Its residual is availability only, and is stated: a Serving S′ that is alive but paused for `4 × hold_ms` with an unremoved row latches `Superseded` when it resumes; its outstanding tickets end `Undecided` and no acked commit is lost (§12.11.10). A Collecting incarnation that dies is replaced by the next janitor that needs its pins.

#### 12.11.9 History order, recovery and readers

- `HEAD.position`, LINK and a CHECKPOINT's `c` count **entries only**. Batches, ATTACH and stream frames never take an entry position.
- **History** is: checkpoint c; the entries through `at₁`; sealed tail 1; the entries in (`at₁`, `at₂`], then sealed tail 2, and so on; the entries in (`at_n`, position]; then the live tail from `live.from`. `at` never decreases along `sealed`.
- **Every recovery applies the history in exactly that order (A3)**: a writer's recovery (§12.3), a claim's settled part (§12.11.5), direct service (`live = None`), a follower's start and catch-up, export, scrub and verify. Recovery never applies the entries before a sealed tail that precedes them, and never runs entry-only while `sealed` is non-empty.
- **`Position{store, branch, version}`** (§1.8) is unaffected, because versions are per commit. The reader checks per-branch continuity across entries, sealed tails and the live tail, and a gap is `Corrupt`.
- **The reader handle (M10).** `stream_reader(a, root)` gives a read-only Authority for a follower, `open_read_only`, scrub or verify. It never elects, takes no slot and never writes the register. It reads a sealed tail's slices directly; it reads `reg` only to follow a live tail. With `live = None` it reads the sealed tails and entries in history order, and it reads `reg` only after a 404 on a sealed-tail batch, because §12.11.8's 404 table decides by `low`.
- **A follower's round.** At exact head bytes Hd with epoch e and `live = (S, inc, from)`:
  1. read X's slices of batches from `from`, stopping at the first not yet created (§12.11.8);
  2. GET `S/reg`, issued after the last batch read completed;
  3. GET X's head, issued after step 2's response;
  4. act on it:
     - same inc, no row for (X, e), head bytes exactly Hd: publish X's frames from every batch below the stop; `fresh` advances to them;
     - head at epoch > e with `sealed ∋ (S, inc, …, cutoff k)`: apply through k only, then **every later sealed tail in order**, then follow the new `live`. A follower that missed several migrations never skips an intermediate sealed tail (A3);
     - head at epoch > e with no sealed entry for (S, inc), or at epoch e with other bytes (a settle, cut or advance): re-follow from the new head in history order, skipping every commit whose (branch, version) is at or below what it already published on that branch;
     - otherwise (a row is present, or inc changed, with head Hd): publish nothing new. The follower is `Behind` until the claim resolves or the head moves.

  *Why it is sound.* Suppose a batch completed before a register read R showing no row and the same inc, and a head read after R showed Hd. No H had applied when the head was read. Any later hold has `rev_hold > rev(R) ≥ seen_rev`, and every removal rule is preceded by a head change (a, c, f), a dead incarnation (d) or no H at all (b, e). So every later cutoff includes the batch, and a published frame is never rolled back.
- **`fresh` (M3).** `fresh(f)` on an attached Place shows every commit whose batch the stream acked before the call, by one round. While a row for (X, e) is present, or inc changed, `fresh` returns `Behind(applied)` at its deadline. So its contract ("every commit Advanced before the call") holds for an attached Place only once no hold is active.
- **`fresh_snapshot(db)` on an attached holder** first drains `durable` (each outstanding frame ends `Ok`, `Fenced`, `Undecided`, or latched). Its stall-free answer is one register GET and one head GET, issued in that order between batches: own (inc, holder), no row for (X, e) and its own pair return the durable version. A row present waits for the stall to resolve until `deadline_ns`, then returns `Behind(position)` with the holder's durable main position. Another pair is `Fenced(e)`; another (inc, holder) is the latch.

#### 12.11.10 Latch, tickets, recovery rate, quarantine

**The latch belongs to an incarnation (inc, holder).** It never clears; a new incarnation this process wins starts unlatched. It is raised by: a batch create whose budget runs out after possible delivery (**Unreachable**); a 412 on a batch create whose GET shows bytes that are neither its own nor TERM (**Batch**); `reg` missing, malformed or regressed (**Register**); a register read showing another (inc, holder), or TERM at its own batch key (**Superseded**).

**Tickets at the latch.** An acked ticket stays `Ok` at the level it reached. Every outstanding ticket of every attached Db ends `Undecided`, under `Superseded` too, because a later no-hold claim may include an unacked batch, so `Fenced` would be wrong. Each Db's health becomes `Latched(cause)`, `on_unhealthy` fires (§12.3), every later commit returns `Latched(cause)` until the Place is reopened, and blocked senders wake. The pending batch has one completion owner, the service, even if a Place disconnects.

**Recovery after a self-latch.** Re-elect on its own sid (§12.11.7), then reopen the Places, up to 16 at a time in this schedule, by the no-hold claim: per Place H (1 A) and about 4 B; the CLAIM rides the new incarnation; the open-time cut runs only when `sealed` has 4 or more entries, because the sealed tail names the host's own stream. For N = 500 at about 0.2 s per claim that is about 6.3 s, at most 80 A/s, 500 A in total.

**Quarantine.** A slice whose row digest fails quarantines that Place only (`Corrupt` at its open). A batch whose FOOTER fails affects only the Places with rows in it. A corrupt XINDEX sends readers to the INDEX frames from `low`. A corrupt register latches the stream.

#### 12.11.11 Exits: cut, settle, close, export, backup and archival

- **A cut** (AP16, paused) drains X's slot and consumes every sealed tail and the live tail into the checkpoint. Its head write sets ATTACH to `sealed := []`, `live := (S, inc, (next seq, 0))`. That write also ends direct service.
- **A settle** writes GROUP entries carrying the live tail from `live.from` at the next positions. Each entry's head write moves `live.from` past exactly the frames that entry holds and raises `settles` (M4). It keeps ATTACH, except a close's settle (below). With an empty tail it is one head write; otherwise it is one entry and one head write per GROUP entry.
- **Close** with `sealed` empty runs a settle whose last head write drops ATTACH, so a close is 2 A when its tail fits one GROUP entry and 1 A when the tail is empty (§12.11.14 prices 2 A). With `sealed` non-empty it cuts and then drops ATTACH; a refused cut keeps ATTACH and the pin, and the janitor retries (§12.11.8). Close is the only operation that drops ATTACH.
- **Export and backup (M5)** with `sealed` empty run the settle (which keeps ATTACH and is never refused for memory) and then export from the settled head. With `sealed` non-empty they run a cut and return its refusal if it is refused. So `P_x` and the exported history are §12.7's, and the holder keeps serving.
- **Archival (M6).** While `archive_on` ≠ 0 (§13.9), an attached Place keeps every commit a chain entry before its cut seals a window:
  - every cut first settles: it writes each sealed tail, in `sealed` order, and then the live tail as GROUP entries, so the archive segment names them. This is the one case where a sealed tail is rewritten as entries.
  - while `sealed` is non-empty, no other entry is written above `sealed[0].at`: a settle (unhold, close or export), a direct-service entry or a CLAIM entry first writes the sealed tails as GROUP entries in order and so empties `sealed`. **The sealed cursor (M4 for sealed tails):** each such entry's head write moves that sealed entry's `(from_seq, from_frame)` past exactly the frames the entry holds, sets `at` of every remaining sealed entry to the new head position, and drops the sealed entry with its last frame. A crash between two of these head writes leaves a head whose history (§12.11.9) holds each commit exactly once. So every `at` equals the head position whenever a sealed tail is rewritten, and history order is kept. A claim's H still appends to `sealed` (H is not an entry), so 8 claims with refused cuts still reach direct service; its first entry, which is its CLAIM, writes the sealed tails first, so under archival direct service always starts from `sealed := []`.

#### 12.11.12 Connections, head ownership and charges (CONC-17)

The service runs in the actor's unit (CONC-17; RUNNER §14.11: only `cross` values cross a unit boundary).
- **Per slot**, one data connection created by the service, with room `slot_bytes`, charged once to the service's budget at `journal_slot` and never to the Place's shard. The slot queues two items. The sender chunks frames at half the room rounded down to 8 bytes, and rings before blocking on a full slot.
- **The doorbell** is one shared connection of `max_slots` u32 items. A Place rings it after a send only when its slot's `rung` flag is clear, and the service clears the flag when it drains the slot, so at most one ring per slot is pending and a ring never waits (M11).
- **Acks never wait on a Place (M11).** Each slot has one latest-value ack item, `{acked_through: u64 (batch seq), outcome: Option[StreamLatch or a sealed-cutoff verdict]}`. The service sends it with `try_send` on the Place-owned reply connection. A full connection coalesces: the newer value replaces the pending one. A slow Place never stalls the service or another Place.
- **Per-Place admission.** Each batch takes at most `max_batch_bytes / active slots` from a slot, rounded up to one whole frame. A full slot blocks only its own Place.
- **Head ownership (§12.3, "One owner per advance").** X's head task owns X's head tag and every write to it: a CLAIM entry, cuts, settles (including §12.11.6's unhold settle, which the service *requests* over the reply connection) and direct-service entries. The service never writes a Place's head. After each of its head writes and each stall poll, the Place sends the service a head summary over its slot: epoch, position, `live`, and the `sealed` cutoffs.
- **What stays charged (M11).** A streamed Place's open reserves §12.9's entry buffers, head buffers and history key as any holder does, so direct service, settles and cuts need no new charge; it builds a GROUP in the entry buffers, and a frame over `group_bytes` takes the on-demand buffer as on any holder. It does not reserve the journal worker task's group buffers (`4 × group_bytes`), its timer task or its group channel: those are the per-Place frame journal the stream replaces, and the slot's room is the service's.
- **The service's budget** is a fixed part (a batch buffer of `max_batch_bytes`, a register buffer of `REG_LIMIT` + 88, the XINDEX buffer, its client lanes, the doorbell, and the task charges) plus one budget per slot for the data connection, its typed items, a held chunk and the service slot state including its unsent ACK. `journal_service` refuses when it does not fit. The Place owns the reply connection. The memory and handoff savings are measured, not claimed.

#### 12.11.13 Liveness timers and polls

No safety rule reads a clock. §12's clock rule names these liveness timers for the stream, each on the local monotonic clock and each only triggering an action that a CAS or a head write decides:
- `max_wait_ms`, the batching window;
- `hold_ms`, after which the service runs the unhold settle (rule a), and `hold_ms / 4`, the stall poll;
- `4 × hold_ms`, a janitor's election age, from first observation (§12.11.8);
- `pin_ttl_s`, a straggler pin's age before the forced settle;
- `idle_poll_ms`, the idle register poll, the orphan-row head poll (§12.11.6), the pin poll (§12.11.8) and a janitor's poll of a foreign register;
- `hold_ms` again, the age of a Held row on a Place with no head task before the janitor's close (§12.11.6).

**No idle head poll for an attached Place (M3).** §12.3's idle head poll does not run while a Place is attached. The service instead GETs `reg` every `idle_poll_ms` when no batch was decided in that interval. A row for one of its Places makes that Place stall and poll its head (§12.11.4), and another (inc, holder) latches the stream, so a fenced attached Place learns it within `idle_poll_ms + hold_ms / 4` plus two request deadlines. That is its bound for §12.3's "Local reads". Health's `Ok(n)` counts consecutive failed register reads for an attached Place.

#### 12.11.14 Cost

Fable's benchmark: 6 hosts, 1,000 commits/s, 166.7 activations/s, $13.14 per Class A/s·month and $1.0512 per Class B/s·month. Per batch the stream costs exactly 1 Class A (the create) and 1 Class B (the register GET). The rest is per Place: genesis 4 A; close 2 A when its tail fits one GROUP entry (its settle's last head write drops ATTACH, §12.11.11), 1 A with an empty tail; a hold 1 A and H 1 A per migration, plus the forced open-time cut (3–4 A) when the stream is foreign; an index checkpoint 2 A per `index_every` batches.

| Item | v2.141 | Streamed, `max_wait_ms` 100 |
|---|---|---|
| Commit writes | 2,000 A | 35 A (batches) |
| Commit-path reads | 10,000 B (head polls) | 35 B (one `reg` GET per batch) |
| Genesis | 8 A each = 1,333 A | 4 A each = 667 A |
| Genesis head GET | 167 B | 167 B |
| Hosted genesis cut | 500–667 A | 500–667 A (unchanged) |
| Close | in commit writes | 2 A each = 333 A |
| Index checkpoints | — | 12 A |
| **Total per month** | **$61.1k–63.2k** | **$20.5k–22.7k** |

Without the hosted genesis cut the streamed column is about $14.0k, 1.9% from Fable's $14,246 at W = 100 ms. The figure holds only with no idle head poll (§12.11.13) and M8's register size. `max_wait_ms` 0 gives about 86 batch A/s instead of 35 (+$0.7k/month). That is the price of the choice §12.11.1 makes every program state.

#### 12.11.15 Laws L90

The L90 laws use `std.sim.s3`'s holds and request log (§12.10). The implemented cases are in `bucket_stream_laws.hirsel` and the adjacent stream law files. The oracle of each is the request log, the register's rev history and the set of acked tickets, never the store under test. Smoke runs 16 seeds within 15 s and nightly runs 256.

| Law | Must hold | The bug only it catches |
|---|---|---|
| **L90-Q4** (Astra's decisive case) | A acks X's frame in n after B's pre-scan; B's `resident_limit` fits n − 1 and not n. B returns `Full(Resident)`, the log has no H, the row ends Abandoned, A unholds by (b) and acks X's next commit, and a fresh reader sees n. | writing H after a failed delta admission; a cutoff at the pre-scan point |
| **L90-F** (follower) | A follower that saw n + 1 absent publishes through n only, and publishes n + 1 only after a clean round or a sealed cutoff ≥ n + 1. | a reader that skips the register read or the head GET after it |
| **L90-H** (hold, abandon, unhold) | (i) A's settle and B's H race at one tag, each order. Exactly one head write applies. If A's, B goes to step 5 with nothing applied twice. If B's, A's tickets end `Ok` through k and `Fenced` above it. (ii) **M1 token pinning:** after A's settle applies, C's hold lands before A's removal CAS. A's retry keeps C's row and X stays stalled: A acks no batch of X until C's row is gone. If C's H applies, every frame A acked is at or below C's cutoff. If C stalls past `hold_ms`, A's second settle applies and C's H gets Mismatch. (iii) **M1 idle settle:** with an empty tail, A's settle still changes the tag (`settles`), and a slow claimant's H gets Mismatch. | removing a row without a prior applied settle; removing a newer token on retry; a settle that writes identical bytes |
| **L90-O** (orphan hold, A2 / rule f; A4) | B pre-scans, A closes X (ATTACH dropped), B's hold lands, B crashes. A removes the row by (f) at its orphan-row head poll, within `idle_poll_ms` of the hold, and the register never reaches `Full`. Variant (no head task): A's close of X has its cut refused (or X's Db is dropped), B's hold lands, B crashes. A's janitor opens and closes X once the row is `hold_ms` old, the row is removed by (c), and a janitor of host C that holds a Place sealed on S never sees the row reach `4 × hold_ms`, so it never elects and A never latches. | a row no rule removes; a healthy stream deposed over a row its own host could clear |
| **L90-8** (direct service, A3) | Eight migrations with refused cuts; version 1 in sealed tail 1; direct service commits version 2 as an entry; crash. The next open and a cold follower recover versions 1 then 2. A follower that missed two migrations applies the middle sealed tail. A's stalled ticket, whose cutoff B cut away before A's first stall poll, ends `Undecided`. | entries applied before sealed tails; a follower that skips a sealed tail; a ticket decided without evidence |
| **L90-T** (terminal fence, A5) | An old-incarnation batch m with X frames is held across the election, in two orders. **Order 1:** the fencer's probe meets m absent, m is released and lands, the TERM create at m gets 412 showing a batch, the fence is m + 1, and the rebuilt pins and a no-hold claimant's cutoff both include m. **Order 2:** TERM lands at m first; m's create is released and gets 412 with TERM bytes, the zombie latches `Superseded` (not `Batch`), and the pins and the cutoff both end at m − 1. In both, `low` never passes a batch X's head still contains. | pins and a no-hold cutoff that disagree; a TERM read as corruption |
| **L90-B4** (404 cases, A5) | **Retired, head unchanged:** batch 10 holds only Place Y's frames and batch 11 holds an acked X frame; B's claim of X scans from 10; B's GET of batch 10 is held until A has raised `low` from 10 to 11 and deleted 10. B gets 404, skips to `low`, and B's state holds X's acked frame from 11. **Head moved:** as above, but X has frames in 10 and a cut of X moves its head before the delete; B restarts the whole attempt from the new head. **Sealed range:** X's head carries a sealed entry whose range contains 10 while X is attached with `live.from` above 10; `low` never passes 10, so the 404 never occurs. **Racing create:** a reader's 404 for n, then n created and checkpointed with `low ≤ n`; the re-GET finds n and the read continues. None ends in `Corrupt` or an end of stream. | treating a 404 as an end of stream or corruption without the reread |
| **L90-Z** (zombie election) | A's GET is held across A′'s election; A created batch m before it. A latches `Superseded`, m is never acked, A's outstanding tickets end `Undecided`, and the no-hold claim's history holds every frame A acked. | reauthorization by a dropped row or a stale GET; a `Fenced` outcome |
| **L90-R** (register Q5) | B's and C's holds from one rev, B's reply lost. The resend gets 412, the GET shows its token with its stored `rev_hold`, and the write is done. Both rows stand, and each rev in the history is its predecessor + 1. | a non-idempotent resend; a merge that drops another row |
| **L90-C** (capacity and the janitor, A4, M9) | With `max_slots` 2 (`max_rows` 4), the fifth concurrent claim returns `Full(Register)` with no write of its own and no election. Variant: A dead with aged rows; only a janitor that needs A's pins elects (Collecting), and every frame A acked is in the history. Variant: A paused, not dead, for 4 × `hold_ms`: it resumes latched `Superseded`, its tickets end `Undecided`, and no acked frame is lost. Variant: two janitors race; the loser's recheck stops it. | a claim that elects; an unbounded register; a stranded dead stream; a second election over a fresh winner |
| **L90-N** (blast radius) | 32 Places; every batch create attempt dropped until the stream latches `Unreachable`, and none dropped after it. Acked tickets stay `Ok`, outstanding ones `Undecided`, and all 32 reopen within ⌈32/16⌉ rounds with at most 32 A for H. | re-election storms; unbounded recovery |
| **L90-X** (crash at each step) | A crash after each claim step 1–7 and each unhold step: each outcome is §12.11.6's table row, and every acked frame is present after the next open. | any step that writes before admission |
| **L90-E** (exits, M5, M6) | Export with `sealed` empty settles and keeps ATTACH; with `sealed` non-empty it cuts or returns the cut's refusal. With archival on, a cut's segment names every commit of the window, sealed tails included, in history order. Crash point: with archival on and two sealed tails, the first of which needs two GROUP entries, crash after the first entry's head write; the next open's history holds each commit of the window exactly once, and a cut then archives it. | an export that drops ATTACH; an archived window missing stream commits; a sealed tail rewritten with no cursor |
| **L90-P** (plan and refusals, M7, M12) | A `max_batch_bytes` below the minimum one-row batch, an overlapping prefix, a sim@1 grant with a weak level, and a slot for another bucket each return their typed refusal, and the request log holds no request issued after the refused call. | a hidden default or a refusal after I/O |
| **L90-K** (cost) | 32 Places on one host, 1,000 commits over a fixed schedule, `max_wait_ms` 0 and 100. The request log has exactly one batch PUT and one `reg` GET per batch, no idle head GET from an attached Place, and the batch count is as hand-derived for each window. | stream traffic that grows with Places, not batches |
| **L90-Z0** (zero cost) | No `journal_service`: a Place opens, commits and closes. The request log is the sequence §12.3 states: genesis steps 1–6 (GET `head` 404, the LIST, the MANIFEST create, the entry 1 create, step 5a's two refused probes of entry 1, the `head` create: 6 Class A, the LIST included, and 1 Class B; with the CLAIM's two writes that is §12.11.14's 8 A), then per advance, the CLAIM included, one entry create and one head replace, and the idle head polls of §12.3 at `head_poll_ms`; with that, the head bytes are §12.2's HEADER, HEAD and AUTHORITY with no ATTACH, and no `s-` key appears. The Place plan's head buffers are 2 × (72 + 16 + 136 + 16 + 65,536) = 131,552, derived from §12.2's frame limits, and the plan equals the one `sizes.hirsel` gives with that figure. | stream machinery in the default path; a head-buffer growth paid by every holder |

## 13. Tiered collections

A **Tiered** collection can be larger than RAM. Its sealed pages live in packs. RAM holds its dirty pages, a bounded cache and the pins of calls in flight. Directory stores (log@1) support Tiered collections through `set_residency`. Tiered collections on objects@1 and sim@1 remain planned. §11 covers the page layout and §12 covers the authorities.

### 13.0 Scope and the choices that shape it

- **Steps are not an observable across residency (Q1).** A body's steps (MEM-30) follow the layout and the residency it reads. AP2's "steps are a per-build fuel bound" covers this: the same body at the same root may end `Stopped` on one run and finish on another, and nothing else about its outcome may differ. `reexecute` (§12.8) treats an `OutOfSteps` mismatch on a Tiered read as `Unknown`, never as a divergence.
- **Eviction is never program-visible (v2.59, astra 1990 #6).** A call's result, its reads, its writes, its refusals and their `Capacity` values are functions of the root it reads and its body, never of what the cache, the NVMe tier or another call left behind (§13.3). Within one root object on one build that includes steps: the deciding attempt reads Cold frames only through its private pin map, which demands fill in a root-determined order, so a nested `bound steps` or a caught `rollback_writes_on_overrun` sees the same fuel from a warm and a cold cache and cannot turn residency into a committed value. Across builds and across loads of different layouts, steps stay a per-build fuel bound (Q1, v2.55): a top-level `OutOfSteps` mismatch is `Unknown` in replay, and a body that turns nested fuel into a value may reach a different value on another layout. That residual is FOR-SAM M3-F2.
- **One core primitive, net zero (Q1, amended by Sam's ruling 1A, 2026-11-24).** The resolver, the cache and the pager are pure Hirsel, charged by MEM-30, MEM-19 and MEM-20 like any std code. M3 adds one core primitive, the task-local `core.Cell[T]` (MEM-29), which holds an attempt's state outside the driver's isolation. Once part 2 of the ruling retires `Log[E]` as a core primitive, `Log` is a Hirsel type in core's `log` module over a cell, with the same name and functions, and the count of core primitives does not grow. `core.Cell` is not this spec's `Cell[V]` collection kind (§14). M3 relies on no new ordering rule: cell operations are not events, and M3 neither adds to nor depends on the CONC-10, SEM-8, CAP-8 or CAP-9 order.
- **One read API (Q2).** Every Snapshot read waits and takes a per-task `Reader` (§13.4), on every store and every residency. Zero-copy views come only from `look(r, s, ..)` with `fetch_bytes(tx, ..)`. Bare-Snapshot `get_bytes` and `scan_bytes` are deleted. There is no `PinnedView` and no `Error(Cold)`.
