  - a live-head fork `beta` keeps T Memory while main changes it;
  - a Hot Tiered page. Main writes Hot leaf H (stamp 60) into Tiered T, captures S′, then runs `set_residency(T, Memory)` and then `pin(S′)`. The head's H becomes a fresh image with a fresh stamp in class 0, and T2 seals S′'s H with stamp 60 in class 3, once. Under a rule that re-stamped only load steps, stamp 60 would land in both classes;
  - the reverse direction. T is Tiered with Cold leaf L (stamp 30) in pack 7, pin P is taken, and then `set_residency(T, Memory)` runs. The loaded leaf takes a fresh stamp in class 0, and P keeps (7, L). The old root is a `deferred_frees` row, and its drain files L into P's holder cell, so `live[7]` keeps its 12,000 bytes (pack 7 holding 12,000 live payload bytes, L among them).

**Self-attack (v2.96).** The brief asked for these five, and rows S6–S9 attack the new rules themselves.

| # | Attack | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | Fork of fork. `beta` forks main at w₀ = 100, and `gamma` is a cut-path fork of a historical Snapshot of `beta` | The lookup roots are every head, so `gamma`'s slots take the locations main or `beta` already use. A frame copied from behind a cursor keeps its stamp s. When s < 100 it is inherited by both, and `gamma`'s kill of it goes into its origin cell, which never subtracts: an over-count ("What drifts"). A residency change on `gamma` re-stamps above every watermark, and the copy belongs to `gamma` alone ("Origins") |
| S2 | Crash between the candidate queue's added rows and T2 | Everything is still in the paused writer's RAM, and nothing is written. The old MANIFEST and the journal recover. The pin or fork never returned, and its Snapshot is `Foreign`. Copies and re-stamped frames written before a later crash are orphans that Remove clears. Drawn stamps stay consumed. The lost cursor restarts the probe, which is one of the two reset events |
| S3 | Mandatory-only retry at a promotion or residency cut | Resolution, copies from behind a cursor, materializations and re-stamping are all in the mandatory candidate, so the retry publishes them. It keeps the installed cursors, and every in-place reference is at or after them. It advances no probe and is not counted toward the progress bound |
| S4 | Replay determinism | Pins, cut-path forks and schema commits are cut-made, so no journal frame carries a promotion or a residency change. Whether a frame is copied or kept in place depends on the writer's cursor, which is not journaled, but the choice rides the MANIFEST that publishes it, and replay never makes it again. The re-stamp draws come before `next_stamp` is captured, and replay's FORK raise is unchanged |
| S5 | MEM charges for the walk | Lookups hold one path at a time as cut pins on K. A key read, or a copy from behind a cursor, is one more frame, released before the next. Walk state, the copied pages and the 8-byte re-stamp entries are on the paused writer's own limit. A refusal refuses the cut and loses nothing (§13.11). No new partition, and no `Capacity` a call can observe |
| S6 | A promotion and the compaction of the same pack in one cut | Item 3 runs after the promotions, from the installed cursor and against the published generation, the promoted root included. So a frame referenced in place at or after the cursor is matched and moved with every path to it, and frames behind the cursor were copied |
| S7 | A long run of retries | Only cuts that run item 3 advance a probe. A store whose every cut retries makes no compaction progress, as under AP16 before v2.96. That is not a promotion effect, and the bound is stated in item-3 cuts |
| S8 | `set_residency` and a pin of a pre-change Snapshot in one cut | The pin's T is Memory, which the record map places. The head's T is Tiered and is re-stamped by T2. Their stamps are disjoint |
| S9 | Tiered → Memory while a probe of the old tree's pack is running | The old root's queue row is a participating root, so the probe matches the frames through it. Pins of the old descriptor match through their own roots. Nothing they reach retires |

### 13.7 Lazy open (AP21-T)

**What open validates (Fable F14, astra #6).** On a store with a Tiered collection, AP21 runs steps 0–11 with these changes:
- **Step 0, metadata, in full.** It validates every list tree, including `lineage`, `deferred_frees` and the `archive` index (its range rows are disjoint and ascending, and each segment name is well formed; v2.59; each anchor row's `start` is a range row's `start` or `archive_on`, and its id names a kind-4 Tiered Log in that branch's catalog at the anchor's `catalog`; v2.61), every class-2 pack, the pack inventory, and (objects@1) the locator's exact coverage L ∪ C (§12.2, §13.1), exactly as AP21 does. A damaged list, retirement entry, fork row, cell or queue entry is `Corrupt` at open. **`lineage` (v2.91):**
  - every branch other than main has exactly one non-adopted fork row;
  - parent chains are acyclic;
  - every cell's (k, side, m) is valid against B derived from the generation, with bytes > 0.

  Any failure is `Corrupt(Malformed)`.
- **Tiered pages are not decoded.** It decodes no class 3 or class 4 frame, and builds no incoming list or location record for one.
- **Steps 4 (Validate) and 6 (Rebuild)** run in full for Memory collections only.
- **Step 5 (Cleanup)** deletes only names that are absent from the inventory just validated, and runs only after step 3's O1, which on objects@1 means after the claim. Open never deletes a pack that a validated list names.
- **Step 6 (Apply) reads no Cold frame (v2.63).** Memory collections, the streams tree and the catalog replay as AP21 says. A data op on a Tiered collection applies its prior to the descriptor (§13.1 "COMMIT data ops carry their prior row") and goes into that branch's replay overlay of the collection (below). Replay never resolves a Cold slot, never calls `put_page_row` on a Tiered tree, and never fetches a Tiered page to learn whether a key was present.
- **Step 8 (Account), one rule per class (v2.64).**
  - `account_memory` is the exact Memory-class account of the recovered roots, by AP15's walk (**Open**, "How the exact account is computed") over every tree and descriptor that class counts. The walk reads no Tiered page, so it needs no Cold read. It can be lower than the figure the crashed writer held, which may carry conservative charges after its last settle, and it is never higher, because the writer's figure bounds the union from above (AP15). A durable history that fit at publication still never reopens `Full` (AP15 **Open**).
  - `account_tiered` is the MANIFEST's figure plus the replayed commits' Tiered charges from their priors, in the mode replay tracks (§13.1). Between cuts `account_tiered` changes only by commit charges, because no commit settles it (§13.8). So after replay it equals the figure the writer held after the last recovered commit, and in exact mode that figure is the exact Tiered account. Open never refuses for `account_tiered`, because resident admission counts the Memory total alone (§13.8).
  - v2.63 carried `account_memory` forward by charges too. That fails AP15's proposed-root admission: a commit that settled to a lower exact union replays as an added charge, and can reopen `Full(Resident)` at the ceiling it fit (§13.1, L68's retained-root case).

**The replay overlay (v2.63).** Replay leaves each Tiered collection that the suffix wrote as its MANIFEST tree, which is Cold, plus an overlay of the suffix's ops on it:
- **Shape.** For each (branch, Tiered collection) the suffix wrote, the overlay is a persistent ordered map from logical key to an entry `{base: u32, now: Put(stored value) | Absent}` (v2.93 removes v2.64's `first`, which only the withdrawn ownership rule read). A Log's overlay also holds a floor (the largest replayed trim bound, or none) and its ordered **trim evidence** (below). `base` is the prior of the suffix's first op on the key, so it describes the Cold tree. A later op replaces `now` and keeps `base`. A trim removes the overlay's entries of that Log below its bound and raises the floor, as §14.4's mask does.
- **Trim evidence (v2.64).** A Tiered trim (id, b, d) applies to a head descriptor (f, n). Let n_c be the `next_seq` of the Cold tree the overlay sits on. The rows the trim removes are [f, min(b, n)) (§13.1). Of those, the rows at or above n_c are suffix appends, which are overlay `Put` entries, and their charge s is the sum of entry(12, |v|) over those entries. Replay knows s, because it holds the entries it removes. The rows below n_c are Cold, in [lo, hi) = [f, min(b, n, n_c)), and their charge is c = d − s. Replay checks at once that s ≤ d, and that c = 0 when lo ≥ hi; either failure is `Corrupt(Malformed)`. It then appends the row `{lo u64, hi u64, c u64}` to the Log's evidence, in suffix order, 24 bytes (v2.93 drops the ordinal and branch, which only the withdrawn ownership rule read). A trim that masks earlier suffix appends is covered: their charge is in s, checked against the values replay holds, and the Cold part is checked by the fold. Two trims whose charges err by +8 and −8 leave the final descriptor right and each intermediate wrong, and the fold refuses them, because it checks each row against its own interval. A floor alone could not.
- **Sharing.** Each branch owns its overlay by `Arc`. A journaled FORK in the suffix shares its source's overlay, and a later op on either branch copies the map's path. Replay also keeps the overlay version that the FORK shared, the child's **fork-time overlay** (one more `Arc`, v2.93), for the fold's ownership rule below. It costs only the entries and evidence that both later versions replaced, charged as entries are. The collection map's entry is a Memory row: replay rewrites it with the new `rows` and `bytes` and re-stamps the map path (AP6), while the entry's root PagePtr still names the Cold tree.
- **Charge.** Each entry costs its key, its value and 24 bytes, and each trim evidence row 24 bytes (v2.93; v2.64 charged 36 for `first` and the evidence row's ordinal and branch). It is paid from the opener's limit, like the other recovered state (a refusal is `Full(Allocation(c))`, U11), and it counts in the resident account and toward `dirty_bytes`. Open never refuses for `dirty_bytes`. The overlay is bounded by the suffix it was rebuilt from, which U bounds.
- **Reads.** A tree with an overlay is read as AP9 reads a staged layer over a head. A point read takes the entry's `now` when the key has one, and otherwise descends the Cold tree through the resolver (§13.3). A range read merges the two in key order, with the overlay winning, and a Log read is clipped to the descriptor's bounds. That is how every consumer reads such a tree: Tx reads (`fetch`, `range` and `next_in`, index reads, `log_fetch`, `last`, `log_range`), Snapshot reads (§13.4's `get`, `scan`, `find`, `next`, `count`, the pages and their resumes), `changes`, `changes_page`, `span_changes` and `window_changes`, AP15's n-way walk, the probe, and `reexecute`. A bounded `count` adds, for each overlay entry in its range, 1 when `now` is a Put and subtracts 1 when `base` > 0, to the Cold tree's count from its branch entries. Overlay entries are Hot and touch no page: an overlay hit adds nothing to the touched-page counter, and its steps are the staged-layer lookup's under MEM-30, the same on holder and follower because both overlays are built from the same suffix. Cold pages are counted, pinned and fetched by §13.3 as usual, so post-open reads resolve through the resolver like any other.
- **Sharing by stamp.** A tree with an overlay never shares a subtree by stamp with a root that lacks that same overlay. AP15's walk, `changes` and the probe treat each overlay key as a divergence, and compare `now` with the other root's row there. The probe also descends to each overlay key, so it still matches the Cold frames the overlay sits over.
- **Snapshots.** A Snapshot captured while an overlay exists shares it by `Arc`. The overlay never changes after open: commits do not write into it (§13.3 "A write into a replay overlay waits for the fold").

**The fold cut (v2.63).** When replay leaves any overlay, open's last step queues a cut, and the writer starts it before it admits any commit to an overlaid collection. Every cut is the fold cut until one publishes. It is AP16's paused cut with one addition. For each (branch, collection) with an overlay, it applies the overlay to the Cold tree in key order, as a commit's apply would: a Log's floor first, by §14.5's trim, then the entries. It reads the paths it needs as cut pins on the cut pin quota K (v2.74, §13.8), never on a caller's partition, with §13.2's coalesced GETs. The paused writer waits for each delivery, which is part of its pause (AP16). It seals the result like any dirty page.
- Each Cold edge the fold replaces goes into the cut's replaced list (§13.6), and each subtree a floor detaches goes into its dropped list (§14.10). So the cut's deadlist cells, `live` and `deferred_frees` match the trees the fold publishes. Those trees, and so the lists, can differ from the ones live would have built (L50, v2.93). The replaced list lost with the crashed writer's RAM is rebuilt here.
- **Ownership follows the actual replacements, inherited at FORK (v2.93, astra 2207; withdraws v2.64's earliest-entry rule).** Live, a branch records a Cold edge when one of its own commits, applied to its own tree, replaces that edge or detaches the subtree under it, merges and borrows included. A tree that a journaled FORK shares is inherited: what the parent replaced before the FORK is the parent's, and the child records only its own later replacements of Cold edges still in its tree. The fold applies that rule to the trees it builds:
  - **A branch that no FORK in the suffix made.** The fold applies its overlay to the Cold tree the overlay sits on. It records each Cold edge that application replaces or detaches against that branch.
  - **A branch c that a journaled FORK in the suffix made.** The fold first applies c's fork-time overlay (above) to the Cold tree c's overlay sits on, which is its parent's, and records nothing: those replacements are the parent's, and the parent's own fold records them. It then applies, to the tree that results, what c changed after its FORK: a floor raised after it, by §14.5's trim, then the entries c's ops replaced or added, in key order. It records each Cold edge this second application replaces or detaches against c. An entry already in the fork-time overlay was `base`-checked by the first application. The fork-time overlay of a FORK made from c in turn is applied to c's tree in the same way, so nested forks need no further rule.
  - **No fold page is shared across a fork.** The child builds its own copy of the pre-fork path. Its pages take fresh stamps after the replayed FORK's watermark (§13.1), so they are c's own frames (§13.6 "Origins"). The parent's copy is the parent's own frame.

  **What each branch records.** The fold never re-adds a Cold frame, so for each branch the recorded edges are exactly the Cold frames of its starting tree that its folded tree no longer reaches. For a child, the starting tree is its parent's tree at the FORK. An inherited replacement is therefore recorded once, with the parent, and a merge's consumed sibling is recorded with the branch whose tree lost it.

  **Parity with live is not claimed.** The overlay keeps each key's last value, not the order of its edits, so a fold can merge, split or borrow where live did not, and the reverse. L50 already lets live and replay form different trees from one suffix: B5's live leaves are [1,2,3] [4,5,6], and replay's are [1,2] [3,4,5,6]. The rebuilt lists follow the published trees, which is what the deadlist must describe. Keeping byte parity with the lost lists would need each op's physical effects in the journal, which this design does not take.

  **Examples.**
  - main puts K under Cold leaf L at ordinal 1, FORK `beta` at ordinal 2, and `beta` puts K2 under L at ordinal 3. main's fold replaces L and records it. `beta`'s first application also replaces L, which it records nothing for. K2 then lands in `beta`'s fresh copy, so `beta` records nothing, as live does.
  - AP3's leaf merge: Cold leaf L holds two rows and its Cold right sibling R holds three. main deletes one of L's rows at ordinal 1, leaving L underfull, and the delete merges L and R. Then FORK `beta` at ordinal 2, and the writer crashes. main's fold merges and records L and R. `beta`'s first application merges as well and records nothing. v2.64's rule recorded R against no branch, because no overlay key lay under R (L87 (d)).
- Its working set is the root-to-leaf path being merged, plus the pages written since the current pack's last close. It never holds a whole tree, and it charges the overlay's bytes to `dirty_bytes`, not the folded pages, until the cut publishes.
- **Payers (v2.74).** The Cold pages it reads are cut pins. At each overlay key it pins at most the path and each path page's left and right sibling under its parent, which is what a split, merge or borrow reads (3h). Read-ahead goes through §13.2's hints, unpinned. A floor's trim pins at most §14.5's 4h touches, and an evidence row its two boundary paths. Pins are released before the next key or row (§13.8). The merge stack, the rebuilt replaced and dropped lists, and the folded pages are on the paused writer's own limit (C2). The overlay's `dirty_bytes` charge does not cover the folded pages, because one key can rewrite up to 3h pages. A refusal there refuses the cut with its `Allocation` cause and loses nothing.
- At each overlay key it checks the entry's `base` against the Cold leaf (0 when the key is absent, else 1 + |v|). For each trim evidence row, in order, it sums entry(12, |v|) over the Cold rows [lo, hi), from branch entries and the two boundary leaves, as §14.5's cut sums a trim, and checks the sum against c. That reads O(h) pages per row, through the same partition. A mismatch fails the cut with `Corrupt(Malformed)`, and nothing is published. That failure is not a capacity refusal: the calls waiting on the fold take the store error path (§13.3), and the overlay stays. Every later cut attempt is the fold cut and fails the same way, so no cut publishes past an unfolded overlay. The journal cap (AP15) then bounds the frames that collections outside the overlay can still add.
- **Applying is not charging, and publishing settles (v2.64).** The fold writes no journal frame and changes no version or row. It does not charge the overlay's ops again, because replay already applied their priors to the descriptors and to `account_tiered`. Like every cut it settles (AP15, N1): it publishes X, the exact account of its generation's roots, for both classes, with `exact` true. In exact mode X equals the replayed figures. With retained roots, a conservative replayed figure can be above X, as at any cut: take a pin holding A at K and the head holding B at K in a Tiered table, and a suffix put of A on the head. Replay and the crashed writer both carry `account_tiered` = M + 86, and the fold publishes M − 86, because B has left the union (L68). v2.63's "changes no account" conflated the two.
- When the cut publishes, every overlay is released, and each head's Tiered trees are plain Cold trees again. A refused or interrupted fold cut publishes nothing. The overlay stays, and a crash leaves the old MANIFEST and the journal, from which the next open rebuilds the same overlay.

**An overlay H supersedes (v2.156, D-D7-5, store-d7-demote-replay-3143).** A schema cut is the fold cut too, and its H can change an overlaid collection. H classifies each (branch, collection id) that holds an overlay. It names its **superseded** set itself, and the cut never infers it from root identity:
- **Kept.** H leaves the branch's `CollectionRoot` at the id naming the Cold tree the overlay sits on. The fold applies the overlay as above, with every check. This covers every collection of a cut that is not a schema cut.
- **Superseded.** H removes the id from that branch's map, or redefines it with a tree it built without reading the old one: a demotion's empty root (`demote_index`, reached from `rebuild_index`, `rebuild_aggregate`, a repair and a drift demotion). A removed declared index (`remove_declared_index`, run only under `Migrate`), a dropped table and its indexes, `migrate_table`'s source and retired ids, AP13's finished bulk build at the id, and an install's replaced range follow the same rule once M3b-S5 lifts `Tiered(Migrate)` and `Tiered(Install)` (v2.161, 3150 F2). A hot Tiered build's publish names the same ids, and its build cuts may already have folded their overlays (§13.10a "Hot Tiered builds", v2.169). Until then no overlay reaches them. The fold applies nothing from that overlay and checks nothing against it. Its Cold base root is a released root of what H drops: §13.6a step 3 takes it, and T8 step 3 enqueues it in `deferred_frees` with its branch, also when H redefines the id. The published root is the one H built.
- **Transformed.** H rewrites the collection's rows and keeps their content. `set_residency` runs after the fold in the same cut (§13.8 "Who pays for the load"), so it loads or re-stamps the folded tree. An `index_build_step` chunk that writes a Tiered index holding an overlay first runs the fold cut with no head change, as `checkpoint` does, and plans its chunk at the head that cut publishes. A refused or corrupt fold returns what that chunk's own cut would have returned: the cut's `Full(..)` cause, or the store error path of §13.3. The chunk then never plans over an overlay of its target.

The discard happens on the cut's candidate. The head's overlay is not edited, so a refused, failed or crashed cut leaves it for the next cut or open, and AP16's redo carries H's superseded set unchanged. **No epoch is needed.** A schema commit is a cut, never a journal frame (§1.2 "Schema commits"), and every cut captures `first_live` = n + 1 with its roots (§3.5 step 3). So on holder reopen and in a log@1 follower capture, no live journal frame predates a supersession, and an overlay always describes the MANIFEST's tree. **The prepare child is the exception (v2.161, 3150 F1).** The export lease keeps every segment from its `first` (§3.5a "Copy the tail"), so a catch-up round replays frames from before and after a step over one base. A step therefore carries H's superseded ids, and `apply_steps` applies this same rule to the child (§3.5a "Replay", D-CU-1).
- **Kills.** No fold replacement is filed for a superseded id. The drain of the base root files each of its frames once, as the branch's replaced edge (§13.6 "Deferred frees"). A FORK child that shares the overlay applies its own fork-time overlay as above. Filing is accounting: a pack leaves only by its probe, over every participating root (§13.6), so a frame the child still reaches is never retired. Parity with live's lists is not claimed, as for any fold.
- **What is not checked.** The `base` and evidence checks of a superseded overlay never run. They compare a prior our writer encoded with a tree our cut wrote. Media damage is still caught by the journal frame checksum at replay and by AP20's checks on every frame the drain loads.
- **Charging.** Superseding costs less than folding on every input: no K pins, no fold pages, no stamps. Kept and Transformed overlays are charged as before. A Tiered descriptor that H removes subtracts 126 from the Memory account, never its `row_bytes`, which are `account_tiered`'s. The cut then settles both accounts exactly. Without the rule, a demotion's fold compares an old delete's prior 1 with the empty root and fails `Corrupt(Malformed)` on a valid store, or folds an old insert into the empty root, so the index is non-empty under `Backfilling(None)` (L68 (f), (g)).

**Followers (v2.63).** A follower's catch-up applies a Tiered collection's ops into its own overlay by the same rules, and never folds. It makes every check replay makes at apply, the suffix part of each trim included. It keeps no Cold check of its own. A live holder writes those priors and charges from its plan's pins (§13.3), a holder that reopens over the same frames checks them at its fold cut, and the follower drops its overlay at its next re-base. Its overlay covers the GROUP entries after the CHECKPOINT it last installed. When it installs a newer CHECKPOINT (a re-base, §13.5), it rebuilds the overlay from the GROUP entries above that CHECKPOINT. When the overlay passes `dirty_bytes`, it re-bases onto the newest retained CHECKPOINT at or below its applied position, if one is newer than its own. Otherwise it keeps applying, charged to its own limit, until the holder's next cut publishes one.

**Every later load of a Tiered frame checks:**
- AP20's five checks;
- the location order rule (AP20). No stamp order is checked: a parent may carry a lower stamp than its child (AP10), and a store's own page is never refused for it (v2.59);
- stamp < `next_stamp`;
- AP3's bounded decode.

A failure is `Corrupt` for that read. It is never a value, and nothing is deleted because of it.

**What lazy open cannot see.** A flipped byte in a frame no read has touched is found at its first load or by scrub (§11.17). A scrub tour covers class 3 and class 4 packs, and checks each pack's `frames` and `bytes` totals and its PACK_INDEX against its frames. Open is O(list trees + locator + Memory collections + journal suffix), not O(1).

### 13.8 Accounting and options

- **Two exact totals (astra #20).** AP15's logical account is `account_memory` + `account_tiered`. Each has its own exact or conservative mode, and the resident admission (AP15) admits against the Memory total alone.
- **The resident account** is: Memory images and blobs, plus dirty Tiered images, plus `cache_bytes` and the cut pin quota K (both reserved at open), plus the pager's and the readers' own state, plus the writer's growing metadata (§1.1's writer plan, v2.76). `resident_limit` must cover `cache_bytes` + K + `dirty_bytes` + `pager_task_bytes` + 64 MiB (v2.60, astra 1995 #14: dirty images and pager state are in this account too; v2.74: K), else `Missing("cache_bytes")` at open, before anything is reserved or claimed. This is the Tiered floor; §1.1 "The Tiered plan" solves for it. From v2.76 the floor is checked with C's guaranteed part, W + U. The `cache_bytes` that `open` reserves is §1.1's remainder rule, so at the default floor the cache is 52,232,192 and r is 182,375,272.
- **The cut pin quota (v2.74).** Every Cold frame a cut reads is a **cut pin**. That covers the fold and materialization walks (§13.5, §13.7), a promotion's resolution lookups, key reads and copies (§13.5, v2.94), compaction's copies, the probe's PACK_INDEX and interior reads (§13.6), drain reads (§13.6, §14.10), and a Tiered → Memory `set_residency`'s load (v2.74.2, below). The Db task owns the quota and admits each cut demand against it. K is reserved once inside r at open, beside `cache_bytes`, on a store with a Tiered collection, and it backs the pager's allocations of cut-pinned frames (§13.2). A cut pin is never charged to `writer_pin_bytes`, the shared side or a Reader, so a cut's reads succeed with every other partition full. Its size is a constant:
  - K = `CUT_PIN_BYTES` = 4 × `HEIGHT_MAX` × `PAGE_PIN` + `INDEX_PIN` + `BLOB_PIN` = 4 × 65 × 8,400 + 1,048,592 + 16,711,704 = **19,944,296**. The terms are: `PAGE_PIN` = 8,384 + 16, the largest PAGE pin (AP3's payload limit plus the frame head, §13.2); `HEIGHT_MAX` = 1 + ⌈log₂(2⁶⁴ − 1)⌉ = 65, AP3's occupancy bound on the height of a tree of fewer than 2⁶⁴ rows; `INDEX_PIN` = 1,048,576 + 16, one PACK_INDEX pin (§13.1); and `BLOB_PIN` = 16,711,688 + 16, one BLOB pin (the BLOB payload limit, §11.1).
  - **Why it is enough.** A cut works one **step** at a time, and **a cut pin never outlives its step**. Whatever a walk carries to its next step it copies into its own state on the paused writer's limit: its keys, the stamps and parent entries it compares, and the values it compares. A step is one of: one overlay key or trim evidence row of a fold or materialization; one trim of a Log's floor; one probe descent; one drained page; one frame of a closure or compaction copy; one frame of a residency load; or one cursor advance of the cut's settle. Within a step the cut pins pages of one root in one Tiered tree, at most 4h of them with h ≤ `HEIGHT_MAX`, plus at most one PACK_INDEX frame and one BLOB frame. The 4h covers each kind of step:
    - a merge step pins the root-to-leaf path and each path page's left and right sibling under its parent, at most 3h. That is the commit plan's set (§13.3);
    - a trim pins at most 4h touches (§14.5), and a trim evidence check two boundary paths (2h);
    - a probe, closure or compaction descent pins one path (h), a drain step one page, and a residency load step one PAGE or one BLOB frame;
    - **the settle** (AP15's n-way walk, AP16 item 2) keeps one cursor per participating root as walk state. Each step advances one root's cursor: it pins that root's path (h) and the one BLOB it compares, and copies out what the next comparison needs. So R participating roots cost R cursors of walk state on the writer's limit, never R paths of pins;
    - the Hot-share walk pins nothing.
    Read-ahead goes through §13.2's hints into the shared cache, unpinned. The collection map, `streams`, `catalog` and the class-2 lists are Memory trees, so they take no pins. So a cut's pins never exceed K. `probe_budget` and `free_budget` bound how many steps a cut takes, and so its pause, but never what it pins at once.
  - **Over quota: never.** Exceeding K would need a frame over its kind's payload limit, or a tree taller than `HEIGHT_MAX`. The first fails its load checks before it is pinned (§13.7). A frame that passes AP20's checks is our writer's output (§2.8), and every tree our writer emits obeys AP3's occupancy, so the second cannot arise. So a cut has no `Cache` refusal, and no `StoreCapacity` names K. A cut can still be refused for its walk state, queues, lists and fresh pages, which are on the paused writer's own limit (C2). That refusal is `Allocation`, and it loses nothing (AP16).
  - **Each step's peak (v2.76).** A cut step charges two payers, and neither of them is a pin grant:
    - **On K:** at most 4h PAGE pins, one PACK_INDEX pin and one BLOB pin, which is ≤ K for every h ≤ `HEIGHT_MAX` (the list above).
    - **On the paused writer's limit:** what the step copies into its own state, at most one key (≤ 4,096) and one compared value (≤ V) for each cursor it advances, plus the walk state it already holds. The working bound 2⌈r / 11⌉ + 64 KiB (Q1a) is already spent on the cut's per-node records, so the copy gets a term of its own: `CUT_STEP_BYTES` = `KEY_LIMIT` + V = 4,096 + 16,711,680 = 16,715,776. It belongs to the cut phase of every writer plan, Directory and Bucket alike (§1.1). The walk state a cut carries between steps (R cursors, each with one key and one stamp) is per-node state inside the working bound. A refusal on this payer refuses the cut and loses nothing (v2.74).
    - **What it never touches:** `writer_pin_bytes`, the Readers' reservations and the shared side of C. A cut runs at its peak with every outstanding pin grant full, because §1.1 keeps C ≥ W + U.
  - A store with no Tiered collection reserves no K. A Memory → Tiered promotion counts it (§1.1). A Tiered → Memory `set_residency` load is a step of its schema commit's cut and pins on K (v2.74.2, "Residency changes" below). K is not an `Options` field, so the 0x0081 stored-options layout (AP1b, C-1) is unchanged.
- **The dirty bound (Fable F19).**
  - Dirty Tiered page bytes since the last cut reaching `dirty_bytes / 2` start a cut (Options `dirty_bytes`, default 67,108,864).
  - A commit whose apply would take them past `dirty_bytes` is `Refused(Resident(Capacity { requested, available }))`, which `serve` maps to NoRoom. A cut's install then frees them as Cold edges.
  - The replaced list (§13.6) is charged with the dirty bytes (v2.91), 24 bytes per row: `branch u32, pack u64, len u32, stamp u64`. `len` is the payload length: `PagePtr.len` for a page, and 8 + `BlobRef.len` for a blob.
  - **A Log trim's dropped list (§14.10, v2.91)** is the writer's own memory, not format. It is a list of fixed slots, one per row, and every row is charged `DROPPED_ROW` = 48 bytes, whichever variant it holds. A slot is `kind u8, branch u32` and then the variant's payload, and the largest variant fixes the slot size:
    - **Page**, a detached Cold subtree: its AP20 PagePtr (36 bytes). It uses 41 bytes of the slot.
    - **Blob**, a removed Cold blob: its full AP8 BlobRef (42 bytes), which names the BLOB frame by (pack, offset, len, checksum) and carries the blob's stamp. It uses 47 bytes. v2.89's 40-byte figure, a 36-byte PagePtr plus the branch, could not hold it.
    - **Hot**, a detached Hot subtree: one share of its root page image (an 8-byte handle). It uses 13 bytes. The images it keeps alive are dirty Tiered pages, already in `dirty_bytes`, so the row charges only its slot.
  - **A removed Hot blob takes no row.** Its blob was never written to a pack, so there is no frame to free. Its image goes with the last share of the leaf that held it, and its bytes leave `dirty_bytes` then.
  - **The queue is a separate format.** At the cut, a Page row becomes a `deferred_frees` row of 41 bytes and a Blob row one of 47 (§13.6). A Hot row never reaches the queue: the cut walks it (§14.10). Queue rows are class-2 list rows, counted with the list pages, never in `dirty_bytes`. So the slot size and the queue's wire length are independent, and changing one never changes the other.
- **Between cuts (v2.63; v2.64).** `account_tiered` changes only by each commit's charge (§13.1 "COMMIT data ops carry their prior row"). A cut's settle is the only step that recomputes it, and it sets both class accounts with their modes. **A commit's settle recomputes `account_memory` alone** (AP15 "Settle"). It is triggered by the Memory admission, the only resident admission, and it walks no Tiered tree. That is why replay's `account_tiered` equals the crashed writer's, while open recomputes `account_memory` (§13.7 step 8). A replay overlay's entries (§13.7) are in the resident account and count toward `dirty_bytes` until the fold cut publishes.
- `Accounts` gains `tiered: u64, dirty: u64, cached: u64, pinned: u64, leased: u64, rerun_steps: u64`. Its `logical` remains the sum.
- **New `Options` fields**, with defaults: `cache_bytes` 268,435,456; `writer_pin_bytes` 67,108,864; `dirty_bytes` 67,108,864; `prefetch` 8; `prefetch_max` 256; `get_streams` 8; `rebase_levels` 2; `lease_ms` 300,000; `lease_generations` 8; `probe_budget` 65,536; `free_budget` 4,096; `compact_ratio` 0.5; `repair_cuts` 64; `pager_task_bytes` 16,777,216. A store with no Tiered collection reserves no cache and starts no pager. (v2.60) `sized` derives `cache_bytes`, `writer_pin_bytes`, `dirty_bytes` and `pager_task_bytes` from one equation inside `resident_limit` (§1.1 "The Tiered plan"); the values above are its figures at q = 64 MiB.
- **Residency changes.** `set_residency(mut db: Db, id: u32, r: Residency) -> Result[(), Error] waits`, with `Residency = Memory | Tiered`, is a schema commit.
  - Memory → Tiered takes effect at the next cut, whose install publishes the collection's sealed pages as Cold.
  - **A residency change re-stamps (v2.96, astra 2242 #3).** In both directions, every page and blob of the changed collection, on the branch that commits the change, takes a fresh stamp drawn at the cut. So no stamp is reached in two class families (§11.4 B3).
    - **Why.** A pin, a fork's parent side, an anchor or an unpinned Snapshot captured before the change keeps the old descriptor. Its pages stay in the old class, under the record map (Memory) or the probe (Tiered). If the stamps were kept, the new class would place the same stamps again, and §13.1 forbids either class from naming the other's pack, so the generation would reach one stamp at two locations (L88 (g)). The other fix, resolving every historical descriptor at the change, would rewrite frozen holder trees and load a Tiered holder's whole Cold tree for Tiered → Memory. It is not taken.
    - **Memory → Tiered.** T2 re-stamps as it emits (§13.6a T2 "Re-stamping"). The old Memory pages leave the head, and the record map frees them once no holder reaches them, as for any replaced Memory page.
    - **Tiered → Memory.** Each load step gives its fresh Hot image a fresh stamp, and its parent's edge takes that stamp. A loaded blob takes one too, and its value bytes are copied once, as the load already does. **The collection's Hot pages and Hot blobs are re-stamped too:** a dirty page or a folded root that was never sealed. Each becomes a fresh image with a fresh stamp, never an in-place edit, because an unpinned Snapshot may share its `Arc`. Otherwise a pin of a Snapshot captured before the change, whose Tiered tree holds the same Hot page, would have T2 seal that stamp in class 3 while the head sealed it in class 0 (L88 (g)). The copies are at most `dirty_bytes`, on the paused writer's limit. The load runs after the fold and before the candidate queue's added rows (§13.6a mandatory candidate). The head's old Tiered tree is then released as a dropped collection's is: a Cold root is one added `deferred_frees` Page row for its branch, and a Hot root is walked as a Hot share, whose Cold edges become added rows (§13.6 "The probe", "Deferred frees"). So the probe of the same cut sees them, and their drains file each frame against the branch's holders. A pin of the old descriptor keeps its frames in cells.
    - **Cost.** Memory → Tiered draws one stamp per page and blob and writes the same frames it would have written anyway. Tiered → Memory adds the old tree's queue rows and copies its Hot pages, at most `dirty_bytes`. `changes(a, b)` across the change finds unequal root stamps, so it walks the whole collection and reports no row whose value is equal on both sides (§1.5). Two branches that each change one shared collection end up with two copies. When both copies participate in the same class family, their stamps are disjoint, so each later AP15 settle descends both trees in full even when the rows are equal. This also applies after a residency round trip while a holder of the original tree remains (2251 M2).
    - **Replay.** A schema commit is cut-made (§11.12), so no journal frame carries the change, and replay has nothing to reproduce. A crash before the rename publishes nothing and leaves the drawn stamps consumed (AP6).
  - Tiered → Memory first loads every page and blob of the collection through the pager. It is admitted against `resident_limit` from `account_tiered`'s figure for that collection before any change, and a shortfall is `Full(Resident(..))` with nothing changed.
  - **Who pays for the load (v2.74.2).** A schema commit is cut-made (§11.12), so the load runs inside that cut while the writer is paused (AP16). If the collection holds a replay overlay, the cut is the fold cut, and the fold applies the overlay first (§13.7), so the load reads the folded tree. The load walks the collection's Cold tree top-down, one **load step** per Cold slot. Each step pins one PAGE or BLOB frame as a cut pin, copies its verified payload into a fresh Hot image, rewrites the Hot parent's slot, and releases the pin before the next step. Its payers, with the same refusals as §13.11's cut rows:
    - **Pins: K.** A step holds one frame, at most `BLOB_PIN` = 16,711,704 < K, so the load never exceeds K and has no `Cache` refusal. Read-ahead goes through §13.2's hints, unpinned.
    - **GET range buffers: the pager task**, as for every cut demand.
    - **Images, descent stack and slot rewrites: the paused writer's own limit (C2).** They are the cut's fresh pages, bounded by the collection's bytes, which the admission above counted. An allocation refusal refuses the cut with `Full(Allocation(c))` and loses nothing: the collection stays Tiered.
    - A Cold load that fails §13.7's checks is `Corrupt` for that read; `set_residency` returns it and the cut publishes nothing.
    - No term of §1.1 or of this section changes. The plan's C + K + D + P stay reserved as open reserved them. `probe_budget` and `free_budget` do not bound the load, so its pause grows with the collection's Cold bytes.
    - On a memory store there is no Cold slot, so nothing is loaded or pinned.
  - On a memory store, Tiered is `Tiered(Memory)`.

### 13.9 Archival retention (opt-in, default off)

**What it keeps.** On objects@1 and sim@1, a store may keep committed history past reclaim. It keeps every **chain** entry whose position lies in an archived range: GROUP, CLAIM and CHECKPOINT objects, and the immutable CALL records of §12.2. It also keeps the archive segments that name those entries. It keeps no MANIFEST or chunk. It keeps packs only through anchor rows: a Tiered Log's archived history is its anchored packed leaves with their blob closure, the sequence index in the segments, and the ops of the kept GROUP entries (§14.10, D-Q2-8; v2.61, astra 1998 #12).

```hirsel
pub fn archive(mut db: Db, on: bool) -> Result[(u64, Ticket), Error] waits      // the cut position where it takes effect; Tiered(Authority) on log@1 or memory
pub fn drop_archive(mut db: Db, below: u64) -> Result[Ticket, Error] waits      // request erasure of archived entries below `below`
```

**The archive index (v2.59, astra 1990 #3).** Archive membership is durable MANIFEST state:
- `archive_on` is 0 when archival is off. Otherwise it is the cut position from which archival is on.
- The `archive` root is a class-2 list tree of disjoint half-open position ranges. Each row is keyed `start u64 BE` and its inline value is 40 bytes: `end u64`, then the segment's `position u64, epoch u64, digest u64, len u64`. The segment is the create-only object `a-<position>-<epoch>-<digest>`.
- Rows are disjoint and ascend by `start`. An overlap, `start ≥ end`, or a segment whose `position` is not the row's `end` is `Corrupt(Malformed)` at AP21 step 0.
- **Anchor rows (v2.61, §14.10)** share the tree under 16-byte keys `start ‖ branch ‖ id`, which sort after the range row keyed `start` and before the next. They hold a Tiered Log's root at the cut `start`.
- Archive traversal and reclaim read this index from the current MANIFEST. They never follow a chain of CHECKPOINT entries, so a run of checkpoints taken with archival off cannot cut the route to an older segment.

**Toggles are cuts.** `archive` and `drop_archive` each make a checkpoint cut, as `pin` does (§1.9). The returned position c is that cut's CHECKPOINT position, and the ticket is its generation. So a toggle and its effective position become durable together in one MANIFEST, and a restart after `archive` returns sees the new state. A failed or refused cut changes nothing. Archival is durable MANIFEST state, not an Option, so a restart with other Options cannot purge the archive. A store that never turns it on has `archive_on` = 0 and an empty index, and only the sweep below applies to it.

**Every cut seals what it covers.** A cut at position c, whose previous cut was at c′, does this before it writes its CHECKPOINT entry:
1. If `archive_on` was non-zero at c′, or this cut turns archival off, the window [c′, c) was archived. The window includes c′'s own entry.
2. The cut writes one segment `a-<c>-<e>-<digest>` (role 15). It is a HEADER, then kind `0x00E1` frames of rows (position u64, epoch u64, digest u64, len u64), at most 32,768 rows per 1 MiB frame. It names every chain entry in the window, which the holder knows exactly from recovery's walk and its own advances. Then come the window's sequence rows for archived Tiered Logs (§14.10), at most 21,845 per 1 MiB frame.
3. The cut adds the index row [c′, c) → that segment.
4. The cut then sets `archive_on` to c (turning on) or to 0 (turning off), or leaves it unchanged.
5. If archival is on after the cut, it writes the anchor rows for c (§14.10, v2.61). The anchors, the segment and the index row become durable in this generation, before it publishes the coverage they give.

**An attached Place (v2.142, §12.11.11).** A commit carried in a host stream's batch is not a chain entry, so while `archive_on` ≠ 0 a Place attached to a host stream first writes its stream tails as GROUP entries: every cut settles each sealed tail, in `sealed` order, and then the live tail before step 2, so the segment names every commit of the window; and while `sealed` is non-empty, no other entry is written above `sealed[0].at` until the sealed tails are written as entries, each entry's head write moving its sealed entry's cursor past exactly its frames (§12.11.11, v2.143). Under archival, direct service's first entry writes the sealed tails first, so its own entries never precede them.

So a disabling cut still seals the part it covered. An off-then-on sequence appends a new range and leaves the earlier rows unchanged. Turning archival on at a cut with no prior cut since genesis starts the first window at that cut.

**Reclaim: the sweep (v2.59, astra 1990 #12).** v2.56's rule 1 listed only [pf, f), so it missed whole intervals when `retain` = 1 and when cuts passed without a reclaim pass. Rule 1 of §12.6 is replaced on every objects@1 and sim@1 store, archival or not, by this bounded sweep, whose cursor is durable:
- **One page per pass.** A pass with captured floor f and epoch e lists `e-` once, starting after the MANIFEST's `sweep` key, for at most one LIST page (1,000 keys). It examines the keys in order, and stops at the first key whose position is ≥ f.
- **What it erases.** It erases an examined key of epoch ≤ e unless the key is **kept**. A key is kept when an index row [s, end) holds its position q, q ≥ D′ (below), and the row's segment names exactly that (position, epoch, digest). So off-chain entries inside an archived range go too, including a fenced holder's `e-150`.
- **Progress.** The next cut records, as `sweep`, the last key of the longest examined prefix whose erases all succeeded. A failed DELETE leaves the cursor before that key. A crash repeats deletes, which is harmless because a name never holds two contents (§12.2). A position with more than 1,000 keys resumes at its exact next key.
- **Wrapping.** When a pass reaches a key at or above f, or the end of the listing, the next cut sets `sweep` to zero, and the next pass starts again from the first `e-` key. So a fenced holder's late PUT behind the cursor is removed within one more cycle, and no orphan below the floor stays forever. A cycle takes ⌈(keys below f) / 1,000⌉ passes.
- Rules 2–5 of §12.6 are unchanged. A segment is erased only as below, never by rules 3–4 while an index row names it. A segment that no published index names (a crash before its cut published) is an orphan of epoch e or lower, erased by rule 3 or 4 like a MANIFEST.
- **Recovery and followers are unaffected.** §12.3's fetch-hint LIST starts after `e-<c>` with c ≥ floor, so kept entries below the floor are never listed or read by recovery.

**Dropping the archive (v2.59, astra 1990 #2).** `drop_archive(db, below)` raises `archive_drop` to `below` at its cut. It is monotone: a lower `below` changes nothing. `below` may be any value, including one above the head. The watermark only releases archive ownership. It never authorizes erasing anything that reclaim would otherwise keep:
- **The drop boundary** of a pass is D = min(`archive_drop`, the pass's captured floor f). The sweep erases only below f, so the current CHECKPOINT, every retained checkpoint, the chain above the floor and every leased name stay live whatever `below` is.
- **The kept boundary (v2.61, astra 1998 #12).** D′ is the `start` of the range row that holds D, or D when no row holds it. A partial drop never cuts a range: the range's anchors are the base its surviving entries replay from (§14.10).
- **Index trimming.** The cut after a pass trims the index up to D′. A row with `end` ≤ D′ is removed with its anchor rows, which stop being holders (§13.6's last-holder rule decides which boundaries go), and its segment is erased after that cut is Advanced. The row that holds D is kept whole, with its segment and anchors. Rows at or above D′ are unchanged.
- **Operators.** Operators erase archive data only through `drop_archive`. Out-of-band deletion of `e-` or `a-` names is not supported.

**Stragglers.** A segment row below D′ names entries that may be gone, and a reader of the archive treats them as erased.

### 13.10 What M3 refuses (Q4)

```hirsel
pub type TieredRefusal = Memory | Migrate | Export | Install | Authority | Tail | Shared | Scan   // Tail: v2.130; Shared, Scan: v2.148 (text only, not yet built)
// Error gains:  | Tiered(TieredRefusal)
```

- **A hot Tiered build is `Tiered(Migrate)` (v2.170, M3b-S5).** On log@1 `export` (M3b-S4) and `Migrate` and `install` (M3b-S5) of a store holding a Tiered collection are lifted (§13.10a "Lifts"). A hot `Migrate` (a `Migrate` declaration, `run_migration`, `stage_migration`, `declare_migration` or `preview_migration` on the serving store, not the prepare child) still refuses each step that would build a Tiered collection: `migrate_table` from a Tiered source, a new index on a Tiered table, a changed index on a Tiered table or of Tiered residency, and the resumption of an unfinished or `Failed` Tiered index. The step returns `Tiered(Migrate)` before it changes the plan, so the declaration's other steps and every byte are unchanged. §13.10a "Hot Tiered builds" (v2.169, M3b-S5b, not yet built) specifies the hot mechanism; until it is built such a release runs through prepare and install.
- **In-place index repair is not refused (v2.115, D6 narrow lift).** `rebuild_index`, `index_build_step` and a drift demotion run on a store with Tiered collections: the builder reads a Tiered table through the pager (`snapshot_tiered_span_step`), one chunk per schema commit.
- `Tiered(Memory)` is the answer for Tiered residency on a memory store.
- `set_residency` on an objects@1 store is `Tiered(Install)`, before any admission or change, until Tiered is built on the bucket (v2.114).
- `Tiered(Authority)` is the answer for `archive` on log@1 or memory.
- Because install is refused, astra #21's Fenced or Undecided install has no M3 case.

### 13.10a Tiered export and install (M3b) and Tiered indexes (D7) (v2.154, text only, not yet built)

Design: `store-m3b-d7-design-3106/DESIGN-v2.md` (v2.154 replaces v2.151's text after review 3125). The slice order, the owners and the decisions log are there. This section is the contract.

**M3b. One image, one opener.**
- **The image.** A Tiered export or backup image is §15.1's image. The copy takes every pack the lease names, class-3 and class-4 packs included, each byte for byte under its own name. So every Cold `PagePtr` and every PACK_INDEX row stays valid, and none is rewritten.
  - The pager's NVMe cache files are never copied.
  - An image never refers to the source's packs. A backup outlives its source.
- **The lease names every listed class-3/4 pack (v2.157, store-zero-live-pin-3142).** It is today's `live_pack_sequences` set (one u64 per positive-live pack) plus every class-3/4 pack that the installed generation lists, with the existing 16 KiB copy buffer and capture's existing two-pass inventory. So every pack the copied MANIFEST lists is in the image: class 0/1 packs are listed exactly while their `live` is positive (`edit_pack_list` delists them at 0), and class 2 is as before (L51 (j′)).
  - **`live` is not a reachability fact.** §13.6 keeps it advisory, and its under-count drift lets a historical pin or cut-path fork reference in place a frame whose bytes already left `live` (§13.5 step 2). v2.154 let a listed zero-live class-3/4 pack be absent from an image on the premise that it held no reachable frame. That premise is false: with `probe_budget` 0, cut a Tiered table's only leaf A into pack P, capture Snapshot S, overwrite the row and cut (`live[P]` = 0, P listed), then pin S. The pin reaches A in P (L100 (a)). v2.157 withdraws the premise, the absent-pack rule, R4's exception for it, and the zero-live skips of the probe, the scrub tour and `check_capture`.
  - **Charge (v2.157, D-ZL-2).** An export of a store that lists a zero-live class-3/4 pack while no holder is Tiered pays one more u64 and one more file copy per such pack than before v2.154. No sound rule avoids it: an absent pack must later be delisted or marked durably before the restored store leaves Tiered-idle (§13.6), a list edit the budget-0 store never makes, and dropping the row on the copy path re-encodes the MANIFEST. Every other existing input keeps its lease.
  - The probe, the scrub tour, `check_capture` and the offline capture read every listed pack as before. An image never lists an absent pack.
  - A cut or probe that retires a leased pack of any class keeps it on disk until `release_export`.
- **The opener.** The prepare opener (`open_export`), restore's R4 and the offline capture validate an image with the ordinary lazy open (§13.7, AP21-T), never by decoding every pack. The opener reuses the read-only recovery core with the export's replay boundary (`terminal`, `end`) and its option and refusal order. It never runs the ordinary writer open, which checks stream quotas, cleans files and rotates the journal.
  - Memory collections are loaded and admitted against `resident_limit` exactly as before, with the same `Capacity` fields.
  - Tiered collections stay Cold behind a pager over the image's own packs.
  - The Tiered plan reserve C + K + D + P (§1.1) is taken exactly when the image holds a Tiered collection.
- **R4 and prepublication: the reachable graph.** Three paths run AP21 step 3 class-aware: R4 on an image holding a class-3/4 pack, every cut under an export lease (v2.133, the import pin's cuts included), and the install cut. Ordinary cuts are unchanged, and no store that can hold a lease or install before M3b reaches the walk. From every holder root and referenced blob, each Cold edge must name a listed pack of its class (3 for a page, 4 for a blob). The frame at its offset must have the edge's `len`, checksum and stamp, and its PACK_INDEX row must name it. The walk then descends.
  - The walk uses one buffer of at most 1,048,576 bytes or one frame: the restore task's at R4, K at a cut. It holds no pin across frames.
  - At a cut, an edge into a settled pack ends the descent with the class check (§11.12 "Settled packs"). R4 settles nothing.
  - The offline walker (`store-capture-check.hirsel`) takes the same traversal.
  - `require_unarchived_manifest` still runs first on every path.
  - **Every listed class-3/4 pack is present (v2.157, store-zero-live-pin-3142).** R4 checks that each listed class-3/4 pack's file exists (a directory lookup, no read). An absent one is `Unsupported(0x0023)`, the refusal any image listing a class-3/4 pack gets before M3b-S4 (`store-list-read.hirsel:185`). An image exported before v2.157 from a store that listed a zero-live class-3/4 pack lacks that file, and its refusal kind does not change. A restored store therefore never lists a class-3/4 pack without its file, so the Tiered-idle step's erase, the reading probe and the scrub tour never meet a missing listed pack.
  - A frame that matches its own PACK_INDEX but not its incoming edge is `Store(Corrupt(_))`, with `to` still holding `EXPORT`.
- **PREPARED is bound by its completion witness.** `write_prepared` writes and syncs `PREPARED` under its final name, as before. The witness is the SHA-256 the runner records only after `write_prepared` returns. The release row and the cutover request carry it, and `accept_cutover` compares it with the kept import's digest. A `PREPARED` with no recorded witness is an interrupted prepare: the runner removes it before preparing again, and OLD never validates a file without a named digest. A prefix (a cut before an intended 0x0085 frame) has another digest and never binds. Memory prepares add no I/O (§3.5a).
- **Residency of a shipped range is derived on OLD:**
  - An untouched collection is not shipped, and its descriptor is carried byte-equal.
  - A **replaced** id keeps OLD's residency for that id, with a descriptor rebuilt from the replacement's root, rows and bytes. This includes a same-id Backfilling or Failed index the preparation finished.
  - A new index takes its table's residency.
  - A new table is Memory.
  - A `migrate_table` target takes the residency of the source that PREPARED's **source-map frame** names. That frame is kind 0x008B, role 6 (0x008A is `SCRUB`'s round history): a value-codec `List[(target u32, source u32)]`, limit 1,048,832. It sits after the last 0x0083 frame and before the first 0x0084 row. The child writes it from the `Migration`'s own record of each `migrate_table(from, to)` call. It is present exactly when the image holds a Tiered collection and the delta has a `migrate_table` target, so a Memory-only PREPARED is byte-identical to before v2.154. M1–M3 refuse it with `ImportMalformed` unless:
    - targets are strictly increasing;
    - each target is a new table of the delta;
    - each source is a table of OLD's base catalog.
  - A new table the frame does not name is Memory. OLD cannot check that every migrate target is named, since that is the fact it lacks; the frame names only base tables, so it never overrides a residency OLD's own facts fix. A chained migrate (A → B → C in one release) names base table A as C's source. The frame names a source, never a residency byte.
- **Transfer.** OLD reads PREPARED twice, sequentially.
  - **Pass 1** checks the frame grammar, every range's digest, the source map and the file's SHA-256, and counts each range's rows, bytes and over-inline values. It holds a Memory range's rows as before, and nothing of a Tiered range (one frame). It binds the SHA-256, each range's (id, count, digest), the target and the export attempt in `KeptImport` before pass 2 starts.
  - **`reserve_import` admission:**
    - Memory ranges' row charges plus 126 per descriptor, as before;
    - Tiered ranges charge `account_tiered`;
    - the Tiered plan reserve when OLD has no Tiered collection yet;
    - stamps from pass 1's counts.
  - **Pass 2** runs for Tiered ranges only and writes no pack outside a cut. A second sequential read feeds a bottom-up builder that makes each Tiered range Hot pages of the import pin's tree, under the reserved stamps. When they reach `dirty_bytes`, the chunk ends with a `hold_import` cut, which emits them into class-3/4 packs as any cut emits a Tiered collection; the leased-cut walk and the settled-pack rule apply. Its workspace is one leaf per level plus the chunk's Hot pages. It re-derives each range's digest, and a mismatch is `ImportMalformed`: the import is forgotten and its pin becomes an orphan. Pass-2 bytes are listed only under the import pin, which no reader sees, and activation requires every pass-2 digest to equal pass 1's.
  - The target validator admits `account_memory` plus the plan reserve when the target holds a Tiered collection, against `target.resident`.
- **Three durable states before activation:**
  - (i) A chunk cut wrote packs but has not renamed MANIFEST: they are unlisted, and cleanup removes them at the next open.
  - (ii) A chunk, keep or round cut renamed MANIFEST, listing them under the **import pin** while OLD serves. A crash reopens OLD with that pin as an orphan. The first holder-free cut drops it (§3.5a "Crash cuts"), and the probe retires its packs.
  - (iii) The activation cut's MANIFEST rename publishes NEW and drops the pin. It is the point of no return.
- **Catch-up.** A round:
  - **Finishes the Tiered diff.** It finishes every deferred Tiered range diff (`ChangeOutput.deferred`) at the two captured roots through the child's pager, before patching index ranges. The compare continues past a Tiered collection to every later one, skips every superseded id (v2.167, 3177 F4: its content is replaced whole, and its entries arrive as step rows, so the round never reads a before-root handed to `deferred_frees`), and a deferred range the round cannot finish is `Drift`, never dropped (v2.161).
  - **Steps supersede in the child (v2.161, D-CU-1; v2.167, 3177 F4).** Each step carries H's superseded ids and its own rows, recorded at its cut, and `apply_steps` applies D-D7-5 to the child (§3.5a "Replay"): dropping main's overlay share only (a `FORK` in the tail keeps its own `Arc`), dropping a superseded Tiered descriptor's `bytes` from exact replay `account_tiered`, and refusing `Drift` for any superseded id whose new root is not empty. `export_step` diffs no roots. Built in M3b-S3 before M3b-S5 lifts `Tiered(Migrate)` and `Tiered(Install)`.
  - **Keeps the account.** It starts the replay's Tiered account at the source's exact `account_tiered`.
  - **Resolves Tiered ops.** OLD applies each op on a Tiered range by resolving its key's path and siblings (≤ 3h pages) from the import pin's root through OLD's pager, as a call attempt on the writer partition pinned against `writer_pin_bytes`; a miss reruns it. The resolved pages become Hot pages of the held tree, and at `dirty_bytes` the round ends a chunk with a `hold_import` cut. Memory ranges keep their resident path. The totals check reads the rebuilt descriptor's row count.
  - **The child's side.** The child applies the rounds to its own Tiered ranges with the same resolver through its own pager and writer partition, cutting at `dirty_bytes`: `patch_index_ranges`, `round_ops` and `range_totals`.
- **`stage_rewrite` on a Cold row.** The header is unchanged.
  - **Staging.** On a row in a Tiered range, `stage_rewrite` runs the checks that need no row and queues the rewrite unchecked.
  - **The consuming call checks.** The queued checks run in the `waits` call that consumes the staging: `write_prepared` in the prepare child, `install_activation` in a standalone install. They run as one writer call attempt over every queued rewrite, charged to `writer_pin_bytes`, and a miss reruns the whole attempt. Edits apply only after all pass.
  - **Refusals:**
    - a missing row is `Missing("row")`;
    - a changed index entry is `Changed(<index name>)`;
    - an attempt over the grant is `Full(Cache(Capacity))`.
  - **OLD's leased-base check** runs the same way in pass 1, at the lease's captured roots, as a call attempt on OLD's writer partition. `reserve_import` keeps no Cold read.
  - **The activation cut's own read** stays a cut read on K (v2.102).
- **Lifts (v2.170, M3b-S5, built).** `Tiered(Export)` is lifted on log@1 with L96. M3b-S5 lifts on log@1, with L97 and L70 revised:
  - `Tiered(Install)`: `install_activation`, `install_bound_activation`, `reserve_import` and `perform_cutover`, and the runner's explicit and implicit install checks (`activation_install_allowed` is deleted);
  - `Tiered(Migrate)` in the prepare child: `declare_export` with or without a `Migration`, including chunked Tiered `migrate_table` targets (`run_deferred_migrates`) and Tiered index builds (`write_prepared`);
  - in a hot `Migrate`: `drop_named_table`, `rename_table`, `list_collections`, removing an index, and every step on a Memory collection.
  - **Superseded ids (3150 F2).** `remove_declared_index`, a dropped table and its indexes (`stage_drop_table_key`), and a `migrate_table` source and its retired indexes record their ids in the plan's superseded set and discard their replayed overlays (D-D7-5); a Tiered migrate source's overlay is discarded after the child reads its rows.
  - **Kept: the hot Tiered build.** A hot `Migrate` step that would queue a `DeferredMigrate` or a deferred Tiered index build returns `Tiered(Migrate)` before it changes the plan (§13.10). Only the prepare child, whose `write_prepared` and `run_deferred_migrates` cut the build through the export directory's own pack sequence, defers one (`SchemaPlan.defer_tiered`). `seal` no longer builds deferred indexes on the live directory: that build wrote packs under the installed `next_pack`, which the publishing cut then reused (a reopen was `Corrupt`). It lifts with M3b-S5b and L102, under "Hot Tiered builds" below (v2.169, not yet built). `preview_migration` keeps it for such a plan (see below).
- **objects@1.** `set_residency` there stays `Tiered(Install)` until Tiered is built on the bucket, so no Bucket store holds a Tiered collection.
  - When it is built, the object export reads the named class-3/4 object versions through the verified pack cache (3082), refetching on a miss or a damaged entry.
  - Its log@1 reseal replaces the 72-byte header, so a resealed pack is identical in the bytes after it, with every frame at its offset and length.
  - That lane deletes `Export`, `Migrate` and `Install` from `TieredRefusal` in one public-type cutover. Until then the type is unchanged.

**D7. An index is a collection with its own residency.** Built through D7-S4 (v2.168): `set_residency` on an index, Tiered index reads, writes and builds, and Format 12.
- **Residency 1 is legal on `CollectionRoot` kind 2.** `set_residency` accepts an index id, under the table rules of §13.8:
  - Memory → Tiered re-stamps the index (v2.96);
  - Tiered → Memory loads it in load steps on K inside its schema commit's cut (v2.74.2), refused `Full(Resident)` before the cut.
- **Creation and reopen.** A new index on a Tiered table is created Tiered, and one on a Memory table Memory. An existing index keeps its residency at every open, rebuild and repair, and only `set_residency` moves it.
- **Reads: each side by its own descriptor.** An index entry and its primary row are each resolved by their own collection's descriptor, in one Snapshot or one deciding attempt, including staged and replayed changes. This holds for:
  - Tx `lookup`, `lookup_prefix`, `entries` and `next_index_page`;
  - Reader reads;
  - both `verify` phases, Sums included;
  - repair and rebuild, which keep the index's residency;
  - demotion.
- **The read log is unchanged.** It records one Span per consumed step, exhaustion included, then a primary Point per observed row. An unused cursor reads nothing.
- **The Tx index cursor chooses residency at open (D7-S1, v2.160; D7-S4, v2.168).** It uses `std.page.collection_residency`, which returns the root slot and the descriptor's residency byte (offset 53) from one map search without building a descriptor view. An empty range returns before the lookup. `collection_child` returns only the child page and fails on Cold roots. Slot type alone cannot identify residency, since a dirty Tiered root may be Hot.
- **Memory cursor charging (L98(d)).** On the L98(d) fixture, D7-S1 allows 20 additional MEM-30 steps on hit, miss, prefix, partial and exhausted cursors in either a Memory-only or a mixed store. An empty range takes 10 fewer steps. The logical byte boundaries are unchanged. D7-S4 (v2.168) replaces the full descriptor lookup with a slot and residency-byte accessor from one map search and restores the end-state bound: every case takes no more steps and bytes than the parent.
- **Writes and build.** An index edit on a Tiered index resolves its key through the commit plan (≤ 3h pages, pinned against `writer_pin_bytes`) and carries its prior row (v2.63). Building into a Tiered index (`rebuild_index`, `index_build_step`, a new index in the prepare child) uses `index_build_step` commits within `dirty_bytes`. AP13 builds Memory targets only.
- **A Tiered `migrate_table` target in the prepare child** is built in chunked commits, not by AP13 (`migrate_build` is resident-only): each chunk reads the next source span through the child's pager, converts it and writes target rows within `dirty_bytes`, and the child's cuts emit them to class-3/4 packs. Its indexes build the same way. A hot `Migrate` builds its Tiered targets under the build pin instead (below).
- **M1: windows.** A Tx attempt's window starts at eight and doubles per delivered demand in the current pin set, with siblings bounded by their parent and by room (v2.109). One logical range can span several demands, attempts and I/O windows. D7 adds no read primitive.
- **IVF.** IVF stores its cells in projector tables and needs no D7 index. On a Tiered source it needs M3b's Migrate lift for declaration and `read_tail` over a Tiered source, which today refuses it.
- **Format 12** (§11.1 rule 6; built v2.168). Formats 10 and 11 accept kind 2 with residency 1. A previous-word reader attaches a nonzero Tiered index root as `ColdPage`, and a nonempty lookup then fails in `std.page.hot_child`. A zero base root with replayed entries looks empty. So D7 takes Format 12 alone, after 3048's Format 11. It lands with the first slice that can emit residency 1 on kind 2. Its list roots are 3048's three: pack list, lineage and `deferred_frees`. There is no dual reader.


**Hot Tiered builds: the build pin (v2.169, store-hot-tiered-build-spec-3224; amended v2.171, store-hot-tiered-spec-fix-3231 after review 3228; text only, not yet built).** A hot `Migrate` is `seal` in `Migrate` or `run_migration` on the serving `Db`. On a store holding a Tiered collection it builds every Tiered target the way install holds an import: off-root under a pin, through the writer's own cuts, then grafted onto main in one schema commit that drops the pin. Design: `store-hot-tiered-build-spec-3224` (DESIGN-v2 §4.4a, slice M3b-S5b).
- **What needs a build.** A plan needs a hot Tiered build when it holds any of these:
  - a `migrate_table` target whose source is Tiered (the target is Tiered, as under "Residency of a shipped range" above);
  - a created index on a Tiered table, including a redefinition, which takes a new id (D-D7-1);
  - a `Backfilling` Tiered index that the declaration rebuilds whole at its own id.

  An aggregate on a Tiered table is an index here; its group parts are combined by group key as AP13 combines them (`merged_groups`). A hot build rebuilds an aggregate whole from an empty tree, never from its stored cursor, so its old parts are superseded with the id (v2.171). A Memory target whose source is Tiered (a `Backfilling` Memory index that D-D7-2 kept on a table later made Tiered) needs no pin: AP13 builds it in the call, after staging and before the stamp handover and the first build cut, and its source read goes through the pager one chunk at a time (`snapshot_tiered_span_step`) at main's head, which no cut has moved yet (v2.171, review 3228 F3). The declaration stager takes no `Db` and cannot wait, so it defers every index on a Tiered table to `pending_indexes`; the call runs this case first. L102 (g) checks it.
- **Why not chunked publishing commits.** Publishing each chunk as a commit (an index as `Backfilling(None)` finished by `index_build_step`, a target table filled through publishing cuts) is rejected for a hot `Migrate`:
  - The call holds `mut db` from staging to publish, so publishing chunks lets no commit run sooner.
  - A `Migrate` is one schema commit, and a refusal commits nothing (L17, L31 (b)). A `Unique` duplicate found after earlier chunks published would leave a `Failed` index behind a declaration that reported success, which is the opposite of the Memory rule.
  - A table record has no build state (Format 8 gives state to index records only), so a half-filled target would be a visible table holding part of its rows.
  - The converter is an in-process closure with no recorded revision, so no reopen could resume it. A crash would leave a half-migrated catalog that the next run's `migrate_table` meets as `Exists`.

  `rebuild_index` and `index_build_step` stay the online path on a serving store (§1.2), and they publish per chunk because commits do run between their steps.
- **Why not the prepare child.** The prepare path copies every pack into an export image, runs NEW's code in a child, and has OLD read PREPARED twice. That exists so NEW's code can build while OLD serves. A hot `Migrate` already runs the declaring release's code in the writer, so it takes only install's OLD-side half: the off-root pin, the chunk cuts, the orphan rule and the graft with `drop_pin`.
- **Order.** The call stages the plan with every check that needs no build (§1.2's staging order, `Exists` included, and AP13's Memory builds above), runs AP13's Memory builds over Tiered sources, hands its stamp counter to the writer (below), then builds:
  1. each Tiered `migrate_table` target, in the call order of the `Migration`;
  2. each Tiered index build, in catalog-key order.

  A chained migrate (A → B → C) reads B from the working map. An index on a migrate target reads that target from the working map.
- **One working map (v2.171, review 3228 F1).** The build's **working map** is its current collection map: the tree the last build cut packed, plus every Hot page the build has written since. Every read of a built collection (a chain's B, an index's migrate target) reads the working map. The graft takes built roots from the working map at the publish, under the writer, never from an earlier cut. So no row inserted after the last build cut can be left out.
- **One stamp authority (v2.171, review 3228 F2).** Staging draws stamps from the plan's copy (`SchemaPlan.next_node`), as every schema plan does. Before the first build draw, the writer takes it: `next_node` becomes the plan's figure, which is at least the writer's, because no writer draw runs during staging. From then on the plan holds no stamp counter. Every later stamp comes from the writer's: the build's pages, each build cut's list pages (§11.4 S1), and the pages the publish rewrites when it forms H. The publish passes the writer's `next_node` as it stands after its own draws, so it never lowers it. A refused build leaves every draw consumed; the counter never rolls back (§11.4). So every MANIFEST of the call publishes a `next_stamp` above every stamp it reaches, and a stamp lives in one class family (§11.4, v2.96). **Table ids stay with the plan.** Every id the build uses (each target's and its two scratch ids) is drawn from the plan's `next_table` at staging and published with the roots at the publish, as today. A build cut's MANIFEST carries the writer's `next_table`, which may be below ids that only the build pin's map holds. Those ids are private to the pin, and a refused build consumes none.
- **The build: sorted runs, then bottom up (v2.171, review 3228 F4).**
  - The targets are collections of a fresh collection map, the working map. Their stamps come from the writer's `next_node` (as `keep_import` does).
  - Each step reads the next source span after its cursor, by key, from the tree that holds the source: main's head as the last cut published it, or the working map.
  - **Runs.** Each produced row or entry is kept in a run workspace, charged as AP13 charges it (entry(k, v) + 8; aggregate parts merged by group as kept). A run ends when its charge would pass `dirty_bytes`, or at the source's end. The run is sorted (`sort_bulk_rows`) and streamed through the pass-2 bottom-up builder (`store-tiered-transfer.hirsel`, as PREPARED pass 2 uses it). The workspace is admitted before the first build step (below) and reused by every run.
  - **One run, or ordered runs.** While each run's first key is above the previous run's last key, the runs stream straight into the target's builder, so an identity `migrate_table` and any build of at most one run write each page once. The first run that is not above its predecessor turns the build to the merge: the target tree built so far moves, as one map-slot edit with no page copied, to a second scratch id as run 0, and the target's slot starts empty.
  - **Merge.** Otherwise each run is appended to one **scratch collection** of the working map, keyed by run number (u32 big-endian) then key, so the scratch tree is itself built bottom up. The two scratch ids are drawn from the plan's `next_table` at staging for each Tiered target; they are never in the catalog and never grafted. A merge pass appends its output runs to the same scratch collection under higher run numbers. When the source is exhausted, an R-way merge reads the runs through the writer's pager, one leaf path per run pinned on `writer_pin_bytes`, and streams the merged keys into the target's builder. A `Unique` index's duplicate is two adjacent equal keys (`Conflict(name)`), a migrate target's is `Exists(target name)` as AP13 says, and equal aggregate group keys combine. The merge emits one row at a time, so the only out-of-line value it pins is that row's, at most `VALUE_LIMIT`. The fan-in is F = ⌊(`writer_pin_bytes` − `VALUE_LIMIT`) ÷ (h × 16,384)⌋, with h the scratch tree's height; `writer_pin_bytes` ≥ 2 × `VALUE_LIMIT` + 1 MiB (§13.8), so F ≥ 1. When R > F, merge passes of F runs each write their output runs first. The first build cut after the merge replaces the pin without either scratch collection, so its frames are in neither main nor a pin and the probe retires them.
  - **Bound.** Let B be the larger of the target's and a scratch tree's bytes in pages (a scratch key is 4 bytes longer), R the number of runs and p = ⌈log_F R⌉ the merge passes (p = 0 when the runs streamed straight). Each row or entry is written once into a run and once per merge pass, so the build writes at most (p + 1) × B bytes and runs at most (p + 1) × ⌈B ÷ `dirty_bytes`⌉ + p + 1 build cuts. At the defaults (`dirty_bytes` = `writer_pin_bytes` = 64 MiB, `VALUE_LIMIT` 16 MiB, h ≤ 4) F is 768, so one merge pass covers about 64 GiB of entries. The build's packs on disk never exceed (p + 1) × B: the last scratch tree and the target, plus, under an export lease or with `probe_budget` 0, the retired scratch packs until the lease ends or a probe runs. Disk and cuts grow with the index size, not with entries times leaves.
  - When the build's Hot pages reach `dirty_bytes`, the chunk ends with a **build cut**. That is an ordinary writer cut whose only holder change sets the **build pin** to the working map: `ReplacePin` when a `build` pin is listed (an orphan of an earlier refused or crashed build included), `AddPin` otherwise. The build pin has owner 3 and name `build`, with empty streams, catalog and keyed roots, and main's head as its version.
  - The build cut emits the build's Hot pages into class-3/4 packs through T2. Like any cut, it publishes `next_stamp` past every draw, so an orphan's frames never share a stamp after reopen.
  - No build writes a pack outside a cut. Pack sequences come from the installed `next_pack`, which only the writer's cuts advance (AP16). `ChildCutContext` and `child_cut_tiered` run only on the prepare child's scratch directory, never on a live directory.
  - After a build cut the build continues from the pin's tree as that cut published it, never from its pre-cut map: the cut moved the build's Hot pages to Cold locations, and the next chunk copies on write from those (as `hold_import` returns the packed tree). That packed tree is the working map's base.
  - The build pin shares no page with main. So it never makes commits retain old versions (`retaining`), and it is never promoted. The cut's account is main's sum plus the pin's (`account_tiered`). No admission counts `account_tiered` (§13.8), so a build cut never refuses for the pin's size.
- **Main under build cuts.** A build cut is a cut over main too. It folds every overlay main holds (§13.6a, the cover rule), moves main's Hot Tiered pages to Cold locations, and runs the probe. The probe may relocate frames that main's Tiered roots reach and repoint those roots (§13.6 "The probe").
- **Re-base rule (v2.171, review 3228 F3).** The plan was staged with the head's roots.
